north_star: Five-second fleet verification with earned calm: nothing fabricated, failure never impersonates health, staleness never wears current-data authority, and every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine. The interface is keyboard-first, follows Dispatch as if built by one hand, respects specialist manifesto ownership, and meets the repository engineering and lifecycle bars.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the trigger-to-spawn-to-act loop is a cold, serial, single-shot pipeline that has been optimised at the edges (MCP endpoint warmup, codex token prewarm, a bounded routing-decision cache, quota-gate folding) while its three largest economic levers sit untouched. (1) **The model is bound before the payload exists.** `_run` resolves the catalog winner at `spawner.py:1300` and only assembles the system prompt, situational preamble, routing instructions and memory context ~600 lines later at `spawner.py:1899-1938`; consequently `DispatchIntent.min_context_tokens` and `max_cost_usd_per_call` are never supplied by any call site and the catalog's `max_context_tokens` envelope — the whole point of the "undeclared is unproven" contract — gates nothing at spawn time. (2) **Nothing in the system reasons about prompt-cache economics.** The ledger faithfully records `cached_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_tokens` (`model_routing.py:2610-2618`) and never reads them back: the routing score's cost term is a synthetic fixed 2000/500-token profile (`model_routing.py:689-690`), the tie-break is an explicit round-robin that alternates equal-priority entries and therefore guarantees a cold provider prefix on alternation, and `_compose_system_prompt` claims a "stable for token-cache efficiency" layering while placing the most volatile layer (the context-bus preamble) *above* the semi-static routing instructions. (3) **Every trigger is a cold subprocess and every co-due task is its own cold subprocess.** The scheduler dispatches each due task serially, one full session each (`scheduler.py:2073-2160`), even though the same file already contains the exact coalescing argument for deferred notifications ("the whole point ... is defeated if the flush still sends one message per row", `scheduler.py:1663-1671`). The one cross-turn reuse mechanism that does exist — provider-native resume — is wired to a Claude CLI invocation that also passes `--no-session-persistence` on the same command line, has no hit/miss telemetry, is tested only against a fake adapter, and appears nowhere in `openspec/specs/core-spawner`. The ideal is a loop that measures its own payload before it buys a model, keeps warm prefixes deliberately warm, coalesces co-due work into one purchase while keeping per-task truth separable, pays for injected context only where that context is demonstrably used, and can serve its highest-volume lowest-value lane (Switchboard classification, < 5 s p99 per its manifesto) without leaving the machine at all.

findings.title: Provider resume is passed on the same command line as --no-session-persistence, with no evidence it has ever worked
findings.detail: `ClaudeCodeAdapter.invoke` unconditionally passes `--no-session-persistence` (documented in the module header as "ephemeral session (not stored in Claude Code history)") and then, when the spawner supplies one, appends `--resume <id>` immediately after it. If nothing is persisted there is nothing to resume. The spawner's failure path treats a failed attempt-1-with-resume as a handle problem and loops back for a full second cold invocation of the same candidate (evicting the handle, writing no `runtime_failure` row, consuming no failover slot) — so on a resume-capable conversational turn the plausible steady state is two full-price cold attempts per turn plus the latency of the first. Nothing meters it: there is no `resume_hit`/`resume_miss` counter, no session-row flag, and no dossier chip; the only tests exercise a fake adapter that records the kwarg. The whole mechanism is also absent from the core-spawner spec, whose Claude scenario lists the flags and never mentions resume — so no spec obliges anyone to prove it.

findings.title: The context-floor and per-call-cost fit gates are structurally unreachable: the model is bound before the prompt is assembled
findings.detail: `derive_dispatch_intent` is called at exactly one site and supplies only `deadline_s=timeout_override`; `min_context_tokens` and `max_cost_usd_per_call` are never passed by anything in the repository, so the `evaluate_fit` branches that exclude a candidate with too small (or undeclared) a window and the branch that excludes a candidate above a per-call price cap can never fire in production. The ordering makes it worse than an omission: model resolution runs at spawner.py:1300, while the system prompt override, situational preamble, timezone instruction, routing instructions and memory context — the layers that actually determine the token floor — are only assembled at spawner.py:1899-1938. The winner is chosen before the payload exists, so the catalog's `max_context_tokens` envelope cannot be enforced at spawn time even in principle. An over-long assembled prompt is discovered by the provider after process spawn, classified as a pre-tool-call runtime failure, and paid for again on the next same-tier candidate, which is usually no larger.

findings.title: Five independent context fetches run serially on the spawn critical path, one of them an embedding plus cross-schema vector search
findings.detail: `fetch_system_prompt_override`, `fetch_situational_context_preamble`, `fetch_general_timezone_instruction`, `fetch_routing_instructions` (switchboard only) and `fetch_memory_context` are awaited one after another with no data dependency between them. The last is not a round trip but a pipeline: it resolves an embedding engine on a thread, embeds the prompt, and runs `memory_context(..., include_fleet_knowledge=True)`, which additionally reaches into other butlers' schemas for a "Fleet Knowledge" section. All of this is serialized in front of every single spawn, including the Switchboard classification spawn that carries a < 5 s p99 manifesto SLA.

findings.title: System-prompt layering claims cache stability while putting the most volatile layer second
findings.detail: `_compose_system_prompt`'s docstring states the layering order is "stable for token-cache efficiency" and then orders it base -> timezone -> situational context preamble (explicitly annotated "dynamic, from context bus") -> routing instructions ("semi-static") -> memory ("dynamic per-request"). Any change to the context-bus preamble therefore invalidates the provider prefix for the routing-instruction block below it as well, even though that block was deliberately sorted `(priority ASC, created_at ASC)` at fetch_routing_instructions specifically "to maximise token-cache hit rates". The volatility gradient runs the wrong way in the middle of the prompt.

findings.title: The routing score's cost term is a synthetic fixed token profile and is blind to cache reads, though the real profile is in the ledger
findings.detail: `compute_routing_score` folds cost in as `_reference_cost_usd`, which prices every candidate against a hardcoded 2000 input / 500 output token profile. Real profiles differ by more than an order of magnitude across lanes (a cheap-tier classification turn versus a briefing session), so the cost penalty is systematically mis-scaled per butler and per tier. It is also cache-blind: `pricing.estimate_cost` at this call site passes no cached/cache-creation split, so a candidate with a high cache-read ratio scores exactly as expensive as one that re-pays full input price every call — while `public.token_usage_ledger` already carries the per-catalog-entry cached and cache-creation totals that would make the term true.

findings.title: Round-robin tie-break actively destroys prompt-cache affinity
findings.detail: When several enabled entries tie on effective priority in the winning tier and none has enough evidence to score, resolution alternates between them via `public.model_round_robin_counters`, incremented on every logical resolution. For equal-priority entries on different providers or model ids this guarantees the next session lands on a cold prefix, discarding a warm cache that a provider would have honoured for the following few minutes. Nothing in the resolution path knows a warm prefix exists, so the fairness policy silently outranks the cache policy that isn't there.

findings.title: The ground-truth routing doc still documents the retired six-tier vocabulary as the live enum
findings.detail: docs/runtime/model-routing.md — one of the documents this lens is instructed to treat as ground truth — presents `TRIVIAL / MEDIUM / HIGH / EXTRA_HIGH / DISCRETION / SELF_HEALING` as "the `Complexity` enum", with a table of typical uses. That vocabulary was retired in migration core_092/093; the live canonical six are `reasoning / workhorse / cheap / specialty / local / legacy` and callers emitting the old strings trigger a loud deprecation warning. An operator tuning the Models tab from this page is reading a routing contract that no longer exists.

findings.title: The `local` complexity tier sits in the canonical fallthrough order with no local runtime adapter to serve it
findings.detail: `Complexity.LOCAL` is a canonical tier and `TIER_FALLTHROUGH_ORDER` routes through it between `specialty` and `legacy`, but the registered adapters are claude, codex, gemini, opencode and api — none of which is a local-inference runtime. The only path to local execution is configuring OpenCode's provider options to point at an Ollama base URL, which is mentioned solely in adapter docstrings and appears in no spec, no seed, and no operator documentation. In practice the tier is a hole in the fallthrough chain rather than a capability, and the vision's anti-pattern about daemon-level internet dependence has no lever behind it.

moves.title: Two-phase dispatch: assemble the payload, then bind the model
moves.why: Doctrine non-negotiable 4 says the daemon is deterministic infrastructure — measuring a prompt before buying a model is exactly the kind of determinism the daemon owes the session. docs/runtime/model-routing.md's capability-fit section builds an entire context-floor and per-call-price gate on the premise that undeclared is unproven, and today that gate cannot fire because no call site supplies a floor and the winner is chosen ~600 lines before the payload exists (spawner.py:1300 versus 1899-1938). Owner payoff: a session is never bought from a model that cannot hold its own prompt, and the receipt gains a measured floor the owner can read next to the excluded candidates. Serves every domain manifesto indirectly (a truncated briefing is a wrong briefing); no manifesto amendment needed.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/spawner.py `_run` (reorder: context assembly block at 1899-1938 moves above resolution at 1271-1360; keep a cheap quota-unaware top-candidate peek from the bounded routing cache purely to fire `_fire_speculative_prewarm` early, so the prewarm win at spawner.py:1145-1200 is preserved); src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py `derive_dispatch_intent` (`min_context_tokens` now always supplied from a measured estimate, `max_cost_usd_per_call` from the active spend rule); src/butlers/core/model_routing.py `DispatchResolution`/`CandidateRecord.describe()` gains `measured_context_tokens`; openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md new Requirement "Payload measured before model binding" plus an amendment to "Dynamic Model Resolution at Spawn Time"; openspec/specs/model-catalog/spec.md Model Resolution scenario for the floor exclusion.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add a deterministic `estimate_prompt_tokens()` (chars/4 floor plus adapter-declared overhead) and record it on the session row and receipt — no behaviour change, pure measurement, so the distribution is known before anything gates on it. 2) Move the assembly block above resolution behind a prewarm-preserving peek; assert by test that prewarm still fires before the gates. 3) Supply `min_context_tokens` from the measurement and let `evaluate_fit`'s existing exclusion do its job; surface `excluded_hard_fit: context_floor` on the Models/session dossier. 4) Supply `max_cost_usd_per_call` from the spend rule and add the deny path with a real reason string.

moves.title: Prompt-cache economics: a stable-prefix contract, cache-affinity routing, and a cost term made of real tokens
moves.why: Vision's success marker is a system that is boring and cheap enough to leave running for weeks; the single largest untaken lever is that the fleet re-buys the same system prefix on every spawn while the ledger already records exactly what it would have saved (cached_input_tokens / cache_creation_tokens, model_routing.py:2610-2618) and never reads it back. Three defects compound: volatile layers sit above semi-static ones (spawner_context.py:116-146), the cost term is a fixed synthetic 2000/500 profile (model_routing.py:689-690), and round-robin deliberately alternates equal-priority candidates (model_routing.py:1119-1128). Owner payoff: a visible cache-hit rate and a dollar figure for cache-attributable savings on the Spend page, plus faster first output on the interactive lane. Serves the Switchboard staffer contract's < 5 s p99 classification SLA (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:37) — the classification prefix is the most repeated prompt in the system.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py `_compose_system_prompt` (reorder to base -> routing -> timezone -> preamble -> memory, i.e. monotonically increasing volatility, with an invariant test that fails if a layer moves up); new `public.prompt_prefix_affinity` (butler, effective_tier, prefix_digest, catalog_entry_id, last_served_at, ttl_s sourced from the catalog row's `capabilities` envelope) plus `prefix_digest` on the session row and on `public.model_dispatch_attempts`; src/butlers/core/model_routing.py new `WINNER_REASON_CACHE_AFFINITY` ranked above `WINNER_REASON_ROUND_ROBIN` and below `WINNER_REASON_EVIDENCE_SCORE`, recorded on the receipt like any other winner reason; `_reference_cost_usd` replaced by an observed per-(butler, effective_tier) token profile read from `public.token_usage_ledger` including the cached/cache-creation split; src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py gains a cache-savings row; openspec/specs/model-catalog/spec.md (Model Resolution + a new "Prefix affinity tie-break" requirement), openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md (System Prompt Composition: volatility ordering is normative).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Reorder the prefix and lock it with an invariant test; emit `prefix_digest` on sessions — measurement only. 2) Replace the synthetic cost profile with the observed ledger profile; keep the ranking formula unchanged so the diff is attributable. 3) Add the affinity table and the cache-affinity winner reason, applied only where round-robin would otherwise have fired (never overriding evidence score or priority). 4) Spend page: cache-hit rate and cache-attributable savings, with the usual degraded envelope when the ledger source is unavailable.

moves.title: Shift sessions: coalesce co-due scheduled tasks into one purchase without losing per-task truth
moves.why: The scheduler already carries the exact argument in this file for deferred notifications — "the whole point of a butler opting into batch delivery is defeated if the flush still sends one message per row" (scheduler.py:1663-1671) — and then dispatches co-due prompt tasks one full cold session each, serially (scheduler.py:2073-2160). A butler with a 07:00 briefing, a 07:00 inbox triage and an 07:05 check-in pays three process spawns, three MCP tool discoveries, three system-prompt assemblies and three memory-context embeddings for one wake-up. This is a primitive built once and generalized nowhere, in the one place where generalizing it is pure margin. Owner payoff: the morning fleet wake-up costs one session per butler instead of N, and the briefing lands sooner. Serves general, health, finance, relationship and home manifestos, all of which own multiple daily cron duties.
moves.integration_points: `{schema}.scheduled_tasks` gains `dispatch_group TEXT NULL` and `coalescable BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (butler-db-schema migration); src/butlers/core/scheduler.py `tick()` gains a planner between the due-fetch and the claim loop that groups claimed, same-butler, same-complexity, coalescable prompt tasks due within one tick window; the composed prompt carries an explicit per-task terminal contract and each task's `last_run_at`/`last_result` (scheduler.py:2208-2213) and completion hook fire from its own slice; a task whose terminal is missing from the composed output is recorded `unknown`, never `success`; must reconcile with the existing stagger key (`_next_run(..., stagger_key=, max_stagger_seconds=)`), which currently spreads tasks apart and would otherwise defeat grouping — grouping happens on the due window, staggering on the schedule; openspec/specs/core-scheduler/spec.md new Requirement "Co-due prompt-task coalescing" mirroring the deferred-notification coalescing requirement's idempotency language.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the columns and the planner behind `coalescable=false` for every seeded task — grouping is computed and logged, nothing is composed (proves the grouping is stable against the stagger). 2) Compose for a single opt-in task pair in one butler, with the per-task terminal contract and the `unknown` terminal for a missing slice. 3) Per-task provenance: each slice writes its own `last_result` and fires its own completion hook; a group failure leaves every slice retryable exactly as the solo path does. 4) Opt in the morning cron cluster per butler; report sessions-saved and tokens-saved on the Spend page.

moves.title: Context-yield ledger: pay for injected context only where it is demonstrably used
moves.why: Every spawn buys a memory context at a 3000-token default budget plus a cross-schema Fleet Knowledge section (spawner_context.py:96-108, modules/memory/__init__.py:388-397) and nothing anywhere measures whether a single injected block was used. That is the run-09 systemic theme of computed-then-discarded truth pointed at the largest recurring line item in the fleet's bill. Owner payoff: a plain sentence — "you paid N tokens for Fleet Knowledge last month; it was referenced in 3% of sessions" — and a budget that shrinks itself where the yield is zero. Serves the memory subsystem's own contract (docs/modules/memory.md) and every butler manifesto that promises to remember without promising to re-read everything.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py (each layer returns a structured block with a stable `layer_id` and, for memory, the `memory_id`/entity ids it carried, instead of a bare string); new `public.context_injection_ledger` (session_id, layer, token_estimate, assembly_ms, referenced BOOL, trial_arm TEXT NULL); the deterministic reference signal is citation matching against the session's captured tool-call arguments and result text, which the spawner already holds; a hold-out arm — 1-in-N sessions omits one layer — restricted to `Consequence.OBSERVE` intents only (src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py:57-73) so a consequential session is never silently degraded, and labelled as a trial wherever the session is shown; openspec/specs/module-memory/spec.md and openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md "Memory Context Injection" amendment; a yield column on the Spend page's per-butler breakdown.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Structure the layers and record size plus assembly latency per layer — measurement only, no behaviour change. 2) Add the deterministic referenced signal from captured tool calls and result text. 3) Add the observe-only hold-out arm and the paired comparison view. 4) Let per-butler `context_token_budget` be tuned from measured yield, with the owner seeing the before/after and the change recorded as an ordinary consequential edit.

moves.title: Prove resume, meter it, or retire it
moves.why: The one cross-turn reuse mechanism in the system is passed on the same command line as `--no-session-persistence` (claude_code.py:448, 456-457), has no hit/miss telemetry, is tested only against a fake adapter, and is absent from openspec/specs/core-spawner. If it is failing, the cost is a second full cold attempt on every conversational turn plus the first attempt's latency, on the lane the owner actually watches; if it is working, nobody can show it. Either way this is the north star's 'failure never impersonates health' applied to a capability the receipt already advertises as `session_resume`. Owner payoff: a warm-start / cold-start chip on the turn that is true, and either a real per-turn saving or one fewer wasted attempt. Serves the Messenger and Switchboard staffer contracts (conversational turn latency) and the dashboard-chat surface's turn spine.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/runtimes/claude_code.py (the `--no-session-persistence` / `--resume` combination is resolved one way or the other, and `supports_resume` becomes conditional on whichever flag set actually persists); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2004-2025 and 2370-2390 (record `resume_outcome` ∈ hit / miss_evicted / not_attempted on the session row and as a distinct non-failover attempt outcome so the doubled spend is visible in `public.model_dispatch_attempts` instead of invisible); new `butlers.spawner.resume_outcome_total{butler,runtime_type,outcome}` counter alongside the existing failover counters; openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md new Requirement "Provider-native session resume" with scenarios for the eviction path and for an adapter that declares resume but cannot persist; one integration test against the real binary rather than the fake adapter.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add `resume_outcome` telemetry and the counter with no behaviour change — one day of real traffic settles whether resume has ever succeeded. 2) Resolve the flag contradiction in whichever direction the telemetry proves, and make `supports_resume` reflect it. 3) Spec the requirement and add the real-binary integration test. 4) Surface the warm/cold chip on the turn.

moves.title: A local tier that actually exists: sovereign inference for the classification lane
moves.why: `Complexity.LOCAL` is a canonical tier sitting in the fallthrough order with nothing registered to serve it (model_routing.py:106, 110-117); the only local path is an undocumented OpenCode/Ollama provider option mentioned in a docstring. Meanwhile the highest-volume lowest-value inference in the fleet — the Switchboard routing/classification spawn at `cheap` tier, one per inbound message — is a paid network call with a < 5 s p99 SLA (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:37), and the vision explicitly lists daemon-level internet dependence as an anti-pattern with LLM calls as 'the exception, not the rule'. Owner payoff: the routing hop, the calendar quick-add parse, and chronicler narration stop costing money and stop depending on the network; the Spend page can report what fraction of fleet inference never left the machine. Implies a Switchboard manifesto amendment adding a per-classification cost target beside the existing latency SLA.
moves.integration_points: new `src/butlers/core/runtimes/local.py` registered via `register_adapter` with honest `declared_capabilities` (`tool_use: false`, `structured_output: true`) so the existing capability-fit machinery excludes it from every tool-using trigger automatically and no new gate is needed; `public.model_catalog` seed rows at `complexity_tier='local'` with declared `max_context_tokens`/`max_output_tokens` (undeclared stays unproven); src/butlers/core/pricing.py zero-cost entries so the routing score's cost term reads it as genuinely free rather than as unpriced-and-neutral; src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py classification spawn and src/butlers/api/calendar/quick_add.py (already `Complexity.CHEAP`, already single-turn, already schema-constrained) request `local` with fallthrough to `cheap` — so a missing local runtime degrades to today's behaviour rather than failing; src/butlers/jobs/model_verify.py probes it like any other entry; openspec/specs/model-catalog/spec.md seed-data amendment and a new openspec/specs/runtime-local capability spec alongside runtime-opencode; roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md SLA table amendment.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Land the adapter with declared capabilities and no traffic; verify via the existing probe path that it answers and that capability fit excludes it everywhere tools are required. 2) Route calendar quick-add (the smallest, most schema-bound lane) to `local` with fallthrough, and compare accuracy against the cheap-tier baseline using the existing dispatch-attempt evidence. 3) Route Switchboard classification, guarded by the routing-scorecard accuracy spec so a local regression is caught as a routing-accuracy finding, not a cost win. 4) Spend page: fraction of fleet inference served locally, and the Switchboard manifesto amendment recording the cost target.

audits.ideal: The ideal loop measures before it buys, keeps what it has already paid for, and buys once for work that is one wake-up. Concretely: context assembly runs first and in parallel (one gather, not five serial awaits, with the memory embedding and cross-schema fleet-knowledge query treated as the network-shaped call it is), producing a measured payload; only then is a model bound, with the measured floor and the active spend rule supplied to the dispatch intent so the catalog's declared context envelope and per-call price cap finally gate something. The prompt is layered in strictly increasing volatility so the provider's prefix cache survives a context-bus change, resolution prefers the catalog entry that last served the same prefix digest within its declared cache TTL — a cache-affinity winner reason ranked above the fairness round-robin and recorded on the receipt like any other — and the routing score's cost term is built from the observed per-(butler, tier) token profile in the ledger, cache split included, instead of a synthetic 2000/500 guess. Co-due prompt tasks for one butler compose into one shift session with a per-task terminal contract, so the morning wake-up is one purchase while each task keeps its own result row, its own completion hook, and an honest `unknown` when its slice never terminated. Every injected context layer is ledgered with its size, its assembly latency, and a deterministic used/not-used signal, with observe-only hold-out arms so the owner can see what Fleet Knowledge actually earns. Cross-turn reuse is either proven and metered — a resume hit/miss counter and a warm-start chip that is true — or removed, never advertised as a capability while contradicted by the flags on its own command line. And the `local` tier stops being a hole in the fallthrough order: a registered local adapter with honest declared capabilities serves the classification and structured-extraction lanes, so the loudest, cheapest, most repeated inference in the fleet costs nothing and never leaves the machine.

audits.ideal: The ideal Butlers perception layer is open-world at the boundary and closed-loop at the evidence spine: adding a source the owner cares about is a configuration act, not an engineering act, and every source that enters produces a typed `ingest.v1` event that lands on a butler's evidence surface with provenance, freshness, and a door back to the originating signal. Three tiers coexist. Tier 1 is a **generic subscription connector** — the owner declares a URL (Atom/RSS, ICS, JSON, a selector on a page), a cadence, and a `control.pinned_target`, and the whole long tail of published obligation (bin day, utility outage, school calendar, visa policy, clinic hours, drug recall, product restock) becomes perceivable with zero new code. Tier 2 is **authenticated personal-record connectors** where the data only exists behind the owner's own credentials — clinical records, telephony, shipments — each with an account registry, a per-account error isolation boundary, and a real domain table under the consuming butler. Tier 3 is **zero-LLM context producers** (the atmosphere precedent) that turn already-owned facts into the derived quantity the owner actually reasons with — most importantly the *minutes between where the owner is and where they must next be*. Layered over all three is the inverse of perception: an **approvals-gated action surface** so the fleet can complete the loop it currently only narrates — check in, refill, cancel, download the statement — with every attempt a ledgered, screenshot-backed, one-door evidence artifact. Together these make the marginal cost of a new sense approximately zero and the marginal cost of a new *hand* explicit, gated, and auditable.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet perceives thirteen sources and every one of them was hand-built: adding a fourteenth requires editing a closed `Literal` and a hardcoded pairing dict inside the Switchboard staffer's own contract module (`roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:24-86`), so "what butlers can perceive" is gated on a code change in another agent's roster directory, and the spec that a connector author would consult as the registry is stale enough to produce an invalid envelope (`openspec/specs/connector-base-spec/spec.md:107,111` still says `telegram`/`telegram` and omits `whatsapp_user_client`, `discord`, `gaming`, `wellness`, `spotify_user_client`, `activitywatch`). The consequence is visible in what the fleet cannot see: the Health butler's entire clinical surface — labs, prescriptions, immunizations, visits — is self-report (`roster/health/MANIFESTO.md`, Meal Write Path: "There is no external connector"), and a grep for FHIR/lab/dispense across `src/` and `roster/` returns nothing; the Relationship butler's Dunbar tiering scans exactly three channels (`roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:803-807`) so a forty-minute phone call with a parent — the highest-weight interaction a person has — is structurally unrepresentable, while Discord already ingests and is silently dropped on the floor; nothing in the repo computes the travel time between the owner's OwnTracks position and their next located calendar event, so "leave in twelve minutes" is unrepresentable despite both inputs being owned; and no shipment, parcel, or physical-arrival obligation exists anywhere. On the action side the gap is starker: the fleet can remind the owner to check in for a flight but cannot check in, and `sms` is a validated `NotifyChannel` (`contracts.py:62`) with recipient resolution wired (`src/butlers/daemon.py:901`) that no adapter backs, so a butler can spend a session composing a delivery that the contract accepts and the runtime refuses. The in-flight slate (atmosphere, SimpleFIN, flight status, ActivityWatch) is closing the authoritative-source tier one bespoke connector at a time — correct in direction, but it never builds the primitive that would make the next twenty sources free.

findings.title: `sms` is a validated notify channel with recipient resolution and no delivery adapter
findings.detail: `NotifyChannel` admits `"sms"` and `daemon.py` maps it to the `has-phone` predicate for recipient resolution, so a butler session can construct, validate, and route an SMS delivery intent end-to-end; the Messenger staffer's contract owns only telegram/email/whatsapp egress and `deliver()` rejects the channel at the last hop. The failure is loud but terminal: the session's tokens are spent, the message is composed, and the owner is never told anything. This is the connector-lens instance of the run-09 'acceptance impersonating completion' theme at the egress boundary.

findings.title: Discord ingests but is invisible to Dunbar tiering — a whole connector's perception is computed then discarded
findings.detail: `src/butlers/connectors/discord_user.py` exists, `discord`/`discord` is a registered canonical pairing, and Discord messages land in `switchboard.message_inbox` with a `source_channel` — but `_INTERACTION_SYNC_CHANNEL_MAP` enumerates only telegram_user_client, whatsapp_user_client, and email, so every Discord interaction is dropped by `interaction_sync` and never becomes a relationship interaction fact. The spec simultaneously claims the job is 'Channel-agnostic — new channels (Slack, Discord) can be added by extending the SYNC_CHANNELS list', which reads as if Discord were supported.

findings.title: The ingestion boundary is closed-world: every new sense requires editing the Switchboard staffer's contract module
findings.detail: `SourceChannel` and `SourceProvider` are closed `Literal`s and `_ALLOWED_PROVIDERS_BY_CHANNEL` is a hardcoded dict consulted by `IngestSourceV1._validate_channel_provider_pair`. Everything downstream is already open-world — the filter-gate scope is a `connector:<type>:<identity>` string, `connector_registry` self-registers on first heartbeat, and `filtered_events` is keyed by `connector_type` text — so the enum is the single artificial chokepoint that makes perception O(engineering) per source instead of O(config). It also places the extension point inside a roster directory the doctrine treats as another agent's governing surface.

findings.title: connector-base-spec's canonical channel/provider catalog is stale enough to produce an invalid envelope
findings.detail: The spec is what `.claude/skills/adding-connectors-and-modules/SKILL.md` Phase 1 sends a connector author to as the pairing registry. It documents `telegram`/`telegram` (the code split this into `telegram_bot` and `telegram_user_client`), and omits `whatsapp_user_client`, `discord`, `gaming`, `wellness`, `spotify_user_client`, and `activitywatch` entirely. An author following the spec literally writes an envelope that fails Pydantic validation at the ingest boundary.

findings.title: Interaction-sync's hour-offset idempotency hack caps the fleet at twelve interaction channels forever
findings.detail: Because `store_fact()` derives its idempotency key from `(entity_id, scope, predicate, valid_at)`, `interaction_sync` disambiguates per-channel same-day facts by assigning each channel a distinct hour-of-day (incoming 0,1,2; outgoing +12). There are only 24 hours, so the scheme admits at most twelve channels per direction before incoming and outgoing collide — and it burns a real timestamp field to carry a channel discriminator, making every interaction fact's `occurred_at` a fiction. Any move that adds telephony, SMS, Discord, or Slack to Dunbar has to replace this first.

findings.title: The Health butler's entire clinical surface is owner self-report with no external evidence path
findings.detail: Measurements, medications, conditions, symptoms, and meals are all manually entered — the manifesto states it outright for meals ('There is no external connector; meals are always entered manually'), and a repo-wide grep for FHIR, lab result, dispense, or prescription ingestion returns nothing but skill prose and a `pharmacy` memory predicate. The manifesto's core promise ('helps you understand your real patterns' on adherence; 'bring better information to every health conversation') therefore rests entirely on the owner doing the data entry the system exists to absorb, which inverts vision.md's success measure.
findings.evidence: roster/health/MANIFESTO.md (Meal Write Path — Who writes/Trigger); src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/002_seed_predicates.py:669-674; about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:124-126

moves.title: Watched Source connector + open source-channel registry — make a new sense a configuration act
moves.why: vision.md's success measure is 'the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs', and the largest untapped reservoir is not any one API — it is the long tail of *published* obligation that no bespoke connector will ever be worth building for: municipal waste and street-cleaning calendars, utility outage notices, condo/estate circulars, school and course calendars, visa and border-policy pages, drug recalls, clinic hour changes, transit service alerts, product restocks, library due dates. Today each of those costs a full four-component integration; with a generic subscription connector each costs one owner-pasted URL. This is the direct antidote to the run-09 systemic theme 'primitives built once and generalized nowhere' — and it is the only move on this list whose value compounds with every future one. Owner payoff: anything the world publishes about the owner's life becomes a butler-perceived event, routed deterministically, with a real evidence door back to the source item. Manifestos served: Home (bin day, outage, estate notices — its 'alerts you when conditions drift' promise currently stops at HA device state), Travel (destination advisories), Education (syllabus/course feeds), Health (recall and clinic notices), Lifestyle (venue and release news), Finance (tariff and fee-change notices). No new butler required; Home needs a one-line manifesto amendment to admit 'obligations of the residence' alongside comfort/energy/devices.
moves.integration_points: Contract: replace the closed `SourceChannel`/`SourceProvider` Literals and `_ALLOWED_PROVIDERS_BY_CHANNEL` (roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:24-86) with a DB-backed `public.source_channel_registry` (channel, provider, display_name, git-seeded on first boot per vision.md rule 5), validated in `IngestSourceV1._validate_channel_provider_pair` (contracts.py:150-170) — unregistered pairs still hard-fail at ingest. Connector: new `src/butlers/connectors/watched_source.py` implementing the full base contract (filtered-event flush, replay drain, `IngestionPolicyEvaluator` scope `connector:watched_source:<source_id>`, heartbeat, ConnectorMetrics). Schema: `connectors.watched_sources` (id, url, kind atom|rss|ics|json|selector, jsonpath/selector, cadence_s, target_butler, etag, last_modified, last_item_hash, status) + `cursor_store` checkpoint keyed `(watched_source, <source_id>)`. Envelope: channel `feed`/provider `feed`; `event.external_event_id` = item GUID or content hash; `control.pinned_target` = the declared target butler, which already routes deterministically without LLM classification (openspec/specs/connector-base-spec/spec.md:190-197); `control.ingestion_tier=full`. Dashboard: CRUD under `src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_connectors.py` plus a catalog entry in `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/available`. Specs: new `openspec/specs/connector-watched-source/`; amend `connector-base-spec` §ingest.v1 Envelope Schema (spec.md:98-113) to reference the registry table rather than an inline enum, which also repairs the stale-catalog finding.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Registry table + contract swap, with a regression proving an unregistered (channel, provider) pair is still rejected at the boundary and that the git seed reproduces today's eighteen channels exactly. 2) Atom/RSS connector with ETag/Last-Modified conditional GET, content-hash delta, and the mandatory first-poll baseline (SKILL.md 'First poll baseline' gotcha) so subscribing to a feed does not flood the fleet with its archive. 3) Dashboard CRUD + one real seeded source end-to-end to a pinned butler, with the filtered-events and replay paths exercised. 4) ICS kind (calendar-shaped feeds: waste collection, school terms) emitting one event per changed VEVENT. 5) JSON/selector kind behind an explicit owner acknowledgement that scraped selectors are fragile, with `source_error` surfaced honestly rather than as silence.

moves.title: Owner device bridge — telephony ledger (calls + SMS) for the relationship blind spot
moves.why: The Relationship manifesto promises 'a feed of who you've talked to and when' and 'the one who notices when someone has been quiet for a while', and Dunbar tier scoring is the mechanism. It scans three text channels and cannot see a single phone call — the highest-weight, highest-intimacy interaction a person has, and the one whose absence most reliably means a relationship is drifting. A forty-minute call with a parent produces exactly zero fleet signal today, while a one-word Telegram reaction produces a fact. Calls also carry a true *duration*, which makes them the first genuine episode-shaped relationship evidence the Chronicler could project ('how much time did I spend talking to people this month'). SMS is the second lane on the same bridge: appointment reminders, bank alerts, delivery notices, and clinic confirmations arrive there and are invisible to Finance, Health, and Travel. Owner payoff: the relationship graph finally reflects the owner's actual social life rather than the subset of it that happens in chat apps, and transactional SMS obligations stop being missed. Manifestos served: Relationship (interaction history, Dunbar), Chronicler (retrospective time from real evidence), Health/Finance/Travel as SMS consumers. Distinct from the ledger's notification-mirror idea: a call is not a notification, and duration/direction/answered-vs-missed is the part that carries Dunbar-grade weight — the mirror can later ride the same bridge as a third lane.
moves.integration_points: Bridge: new `src/butlers/connectors/device_bridge.py` consuming a paired Android companion over a local endpoint, following the whatsapp-bridge sidecar precedent already documented in the base spec (openspec/specs/connector-base-spec/spec.md:527-533) and mirrored by `src/butlers/connectors/whatsapp_user_client.py`. Contract: register channels `telephony` (provider `device_bridge`) and `sms` (provider `device_bridge`) in the new source registry from move 1. Prerequisite fix: `_INTERACTION_SYNC_CHANNEL_MAP` and both hour-offset dicts (roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:803-828, :1198-1199) must be replaced with a channel-discriminating idempotency key before two more channels are added — the current scheme caps at twelve and corrupts `occurred_at`; fix it and add Discord in the same slice. Identity: senders resolve through the existing `has-phone` predicate path that `ContactWeightResolver` already cross-references (openspec/specs/connector-base-spec/spec.md:582), so no new identity plumbing. Privacy: an `IngestionPolicyEvaluator` block rule at scope `connector:device_bridge:<device>` suppressing short-code and OTP/2FA traffic before any Switchboard call, with the drops visible in `connectors.filtered_events` rather than silent. Chronicler: a `CallsAdapter` projecting calls into `chronicler.episodes` (duration-bearing) and missed calls into `chronicler.point_events`, following the `MealsAdapter` pattern. Specs: new `openspec/specs/connector-device-bridge/`; amend `passive-interaction-sync` (spec.md:69, :80-88, :257).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Replace the hour-offset channel discriminator with a real key and add Discord to the sync map — a self-contained bug fix that proves the new scheme on an already-ingesting channel. 2) Bridge process + connector with the call-log lane only: base-contract obligations, per-device checkpoint, heartbeat, metrics. 3) Interaction facts for calls, direction- and duration-annotated, feeding Dunbar. 4) SMS lane with the OTP/short-code block rule landed before the first message flows. 5) Chronicler CallsAdapter and the day-close 'time spent talking' read.

moves.title: Clinical record connector — patient-access FHIR labs, dispenses, encounters, immunizations
moves.why: The Health butler is the fleet's most manifesto-rich butler and its most evidence-starved: 'Measurements... Medications... whether you're staying on track... Conditions... bring better information to every health conversation' is today entirely owner-typed (roster/health/MANIFESTO.md Meal Write Path states the no-connector position outright). This inverts vision.md's success measure — the owner is doing the data entry the system exists to absorb. Patient-access FHIR (and its regional equivalents) exposes exactly the evidence the manifesto is written around: LOINC-coded lab panels with reference ranges, medication dispense records that make adherence *observed* rather than self-reported, encounter summaries, immunizations, allergies. It is also the highest-stakes 'staleness never wears current-data authority' surface in the fleet: a lab value is meaningless without its draw date and range. Owner payoff: 'what were my labs, and are they trending' answered from the record instead of memory; refill-due and overdue-panel awareness; a doctor's-visit prep pack assembled from the actual chart. Manifesto served: Health, with no amendment needed — this is the manifesto's own stated purpose finally acquiring a source. Chronicler gains a genuinely new evidence lane; Travel's pre-trip checklist skill can finally check real prescription coverage instead of prompting.
moves.integration_points: Account registry: `public.clinical_accounts` + companion entity role `clinical_account`, credentials as secured `entity_info` type `fhir_refresh_token` (SMART-on-FHIR authorization-code + refresh), registered per SKILL.md Phase 1.2 (RFC 0004) and following the `public.google_accounts` pattern including the `is_primary` singleton partial unique index. Connector: `src/butlers/connectors/fhir_patient.py`, channel `clinical` / provider `fhir`, endpoint_identity `fhir:<issuer-host>:<patient-id>`, per-account error isolation and independent backoff, `_lastUpdated` cursor in `cursor_store`. Health schema (roster/health/migrations/): `health.observations` (LOINC code, value, unit, reference range low/high, effective_at, issued_at), `health.medication_dispenses`, `health.encounters`, `health.immunizations`. Module tools in `roster/health/tools/`: `lab_result_history`, `lab_trend`, `medication_fill_adherence`, each returning the draw date and range so no value is ever rendered rangeless. Chronicler: adapter projecting encounters/dispenses to `chronicler.point_events` with `sensitivity` set high and a shorter retention, using the MealsAdapter precedent. Ingestion: default `control.ingestion_tier="metadata"` (payload.raw None) with Tier-1 full payload only after explicit owner opt-in, so the raw chart is not replicated into `message_inbox` by default. Specs: `openspec/specs/clinical-account-registry/`, `openspec/specs/connector-fhir-patient/`, `openspec/specs/module-health-clinical/`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Account registry + SMART auth flow + dashboard connect/validate, no ingestion — prove credential lifecycle and revocation first, given the sensitivity. 2) Observations (labs) only: connector, table, one MCP read tool, one dashboard read surface showing value + range + draw date + freshness. 3) MedicationDispense lane and the adherence tool that replaces self-report. 4) Encounters/immunizations and the visit-prep pack. 5) Chronicler adapter with sensitivity-aware retention.

moves.title: Authenticated web-action module — let butlers finish the loops they currently only narrate
moves.why: Every connector on this list expands what the fleet *perceives*; the fleet's ceiling on absorbed mental labor is now what it can *do*. The Travel manifesto promises 'We will never let you miss a check-in window' — but the butler can only remind; the owner still opens the airline site. Finance detects a subscription renewing and can only warn; Health can flag a refill and not request it; Home can see a utility bill and not download the statement. An owner-approved, credential-scoped browser executor turns every one of those from a nudge into a completed errand — and Butlers already has the exact machinery required to make it safe: the approvals command-contract spine with `park_pending_action` (the same gate that guards connector disconnect), the run-10 propose-then-act ordering, consequence gating on irreversible writes, and S3 blob evidence. Owner payoff: the difference between an assistant that tells you what to do and one that does it, with a full screenshot-and-step ledger for every attempt so nothing is taken on trust. Manifestos served: Travel (check-in), Finance (statement download, cancellation), Health (refill request), Home (utility portal); doctrine-compatible as a pure module (vision.md rule 2 — tools only, no core changes) with all judgment in the ephemeral session and a deterministic executor in the daemon (rule 4).
moves.integration_points: New module `src/butlers/modules/web_actions/` implementing the `Module` ABC (`src/butlers/modules/base.py`): `web_action_propose` (renders a typed plan — site, goal, steps, reversibility class — and returns without acting) and `web_action_execute` (accepts only an approved proposal id). Gate: register a command contract alongside `CONNECTOR_DISCONNECT_COMMAND` in `src/butlers/modules/approvals/command_contracts.py`, parked via `park_pending_action` exactly as `src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_connectors.py:69-73` does, so the approval lands on the existing Decisions/Approvals surface with the run-09 consequence-gate treatment for irreversible actions (payment, cancellation, submission). Credentials: per-site secured `entity_info`, never rendered into a session's context — the executor injects them, and the projections stay content-blind following the in-flight `project-secret-read-endpoints-content-blind` pattern. Evidence: `public.web_action_runs` (proposal_id, approval_id, site, outcome, terminal_reason, request_id) plus per-step screenshots and the final DOM snapshot to blob storage (`openspec/specs/s3-blob-storage/`), giving one evidence cohort per run on the signal-to-session-to-evidence spine. Specs: `openspec/specs/module-web-actions/` plus an amendment to `openspec/specs/module-approvals/` for the new consequence class.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Read-only lane first: authenticated *fetch and extract* (download a statement, read an account balance page) — no writes, so the approval gate can be exercised without a consequential action existing yet. 2) The proposal/approval/execute contract and the run ledger + screenshot evidence door. 3) One reversible write end-to-end (airline online check-in) as the proving tenant for Travel's manifesto promise. 4) Consequence-gated irreversible class (cancel a subscription) with a distinct confirm treatment and an abandon path. 5) Failure honesty: a run that ends mid-flow records a terminal reason and never reports success — the executor must never let a timeout impersonate completion.

moves.title: Leave-by feed — the minutes between where the owner is and where they must next be
moves.why: The fleet already owns both halves of the most-used assistant sentence in existence and never joins them: OwnTracks knows the owner's position, the calendar knows the next located obligation, and nothing anywhere in the repo computes a travel time (no routing, directions, commute, or leave-by code exists). 'Leave in twelve minutes, traffic on the expressway' is unrepresentable today. This is also the missing input to two features that already shipped half-blind: `calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar` calls two events conflicting on time alone when the real conflict is that the transit between them is impossible, and `calendar_prep`/`briefing` present a day without ever saying when it starts moving. Following the in-flight atmosphere precedent this is a zero-LLM deterministic context producer, not a message connector — cheap, honest, and degradable. Owner payoff: earned calm about the single most time-critical daily decision, and a conflict radar that stops crying wolf on back-to-back events in the same building while staying silent on ones forty minutes apart. Manifestos served: General (day prep and tomorrow-prep schedules), Travel (trip-day timing), Home ('Say I am leaving' departure scene finally has a trigger instead of a phrase).
moves.integration_points: New job `src/butlers/jobs/travel_time.py` registered on the General butler, modelled directly on `src/butlers/jobs/atmosphere.py` and the `add-atmosphere-feed` change (zero-LLM context producer, `public.travel_time_readings` append-only + `travel_time_feed_status` singleton recording every attempt so degraded is distinguishable from unconfigured). Inputs: next calendar event carrying a location via the shared calendar module, last OwnTracks fix (`openspec/specs/connector-owntracks/`), and `public.atmosphere_readings` (precipitation widens the buffer). Output: a context-bus signal written under the single-writer discipline documented at `src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:11-17` (a `leaving_soon` signal with a bounded TTL, self-healing if the producer stops), consumed by `src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py` and `src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py`, and joined into `openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar/` so a conflict is scored on transit feasibility. Delivery: through the insight broker's single attention budget, never a direct `notify()`. Routing engine: self-hosted OSRM/Valhalla or a keyed ORS endpoint, configured as non-secret `entity_info` mirroring the `home_coordinates` precedent from the atmosphere change — no always-on network dependency at the daemon level (vision.md anti-pattern). Specs: new `openspec/specs/travel-time-feed/`; amend `openspec/specs/context-bus/` with the new signal.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Table pair + job computing leave-by for the next located event, with the four honest states (no location on the event, no recent position fix, routing source error, stale reading) each distinguishable in the response envelope. 2) One proving read surface on the General day-prep output. 3) Context-bus signal + TTL and the Home departure-scene consumer. 4) Conflict-radar transit feasibility join. 5) Weather-aware buffer from the atmosphere feed.

moves.title: Shipment & order lifecycle connector — the only obligation class with a physical deadline the fleet cannot see
moves.why: Deliveries are pure recurring mental labor of exactly the kind vision.md targets: the owner holds in their head what is in transit, when it lands, and which one has gone wrong. Butlers sees the shipping-confirmation email and does nothing structural with it — no repo-wide signal for shipment, parcel, tracking number, or carrier state exists. The high-value events are not the happy path but the exceptions: delivery failed, held at depot, signature required, address query, return window closing — each a real deadline with a real cost for missing it. It also closes a reconciliation loop with the in-flight SimpleFIN bridge: a card charge with a delivered order behind it is a settled purchase; one without is either a pending charge or a problem. Owner payoff: 'what is arriving, what needs me, and what did I pay for that never came', with no mental inventory. Manifesto: none currently owns physical arrivals — Lifestyle explicitly disclaims it, Home scopes to comfort/energy/devices, Finance owns the money not the goods. This move therefore *implies* a Home manifesto amendment ('what is arriving at the residence and what it needs from you'), which is the same amendment move 1's municipal tenants need — file them together rather than inventing an errands butler.
moves.integration_points: Connector: new `src/butlers/connectors/shipments.py`, channel `logistics` / provider `carrier_tracking` in the move-1 registry; state table `connectors.shipments` (tracking_number, carrier, order_ref, status, eta, last_exception, source_message_id) with the cursor keyed per tracking number. Seeding: tracking numbers harvested from the existing Gmail ingestion path (`openspec/specs/connector-gmail/`) by a small extraction tool plus a manual add endpoint — the connector itself stays transport-only per vision.md rule 7. Emission: delta-detection with a mandatory first-poll baseline (SKILL.md 'First poll baseline' gotcha) so enrolling an in-flight parcel does not replay its history; one `ingest.v1` event per *state transition*, with `control.pinned_target` set to the consuming butler and `control.policy_tier="high_priority"` only for exception states. Consumers: Finance reconciliation against `add-simplefin-finance-bridge` settled transactions; Home arrival awareness; a Chronicler point event for delivery. Dashboard: shipment list under the Home butler's router (`roster/home/api/router.py`) with degraded-mode flags per the response-conventions doc. Specs: new `openspec/specs/connector-shipments/`; amendment to `roster/home/MANIFESTO.md`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Manifesto amendment and the scope decision, filed jointly with move 1's residence-obligations tenants — do not build until an owner owns the domain. 2) Table + manual-add endpoint + one carrier, exception states only, so the first thing the fleet ever says about a parcel is the thing worth saying. 3) Gmail tracking-number extraction as an enrollment source. 4) Additional carriers behind one normalized status vocabulary. 5) Finance reconciliation join against the settled-transaction feed.
