audits.ideal: In the ideal system the fleet is not twelve specialists who occasionally message each other; it is one household staff that can hold a shared piece of work. Four primitives make that true. (1) A **joint objective** is a durable, owner-visible container with a declared division of labor: each participating butler holds a *stake* it alone may write, acceptance is explicit, refusal is a first-class terminal, and the objective cannot close while any stake is non-terminal — so "three butlers are on it" is a queryable fact with a closure receipt, not an inference. (2) A butler can ask another butler to **do** something, not only to answer something: a mandate request that the target may refuse, that never bypasses the target's own manifesto or approval gate, and whose refusal comes back on the same wake spine as an answer. (3) A concern that only two butlers can see together has a **co-signed** home: conditions carry attestations from more than one producer, a producer can declare that its evidence alone is insufficient to open an owner door, and two butlers who disagree about the same fingerprint produce one contradiction door rather than two confident ones or a silent winner. (4) Every multi-butler dispatch **joins**: one inbound message that fans out to three domains produces one owner-facing resolution with per-domain attribution and an honest accounting of the segment that never terminated, and a butler that receives work outside its scope hands it forward with the request identity intact instead of answering badly. All four run over the Switchboard as registrar, arbiter, and joiner — no new sanctioned channel, no schema crossing, no butler gaining another butler's authority.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today every cross-butler mechanism is a one-shot with no memory of a shared goal. `delegate_ask` carries exactly one question and one answer (`src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:14-18`); the domain-event bus carries one publish and N notifications and explicitly refuses to treat "the subscriber did nothing" as anything at all (`src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:68-75`); RFC 0010's briefing view is a once-a-day read-only union (`alembic/versions/core/core_063_v_briefing_contributions.py:123`); the context bus carries state facts with TTLs (`openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md`). Nothing durable spans more than one hop, so there is no object in the system that means "Travel, Finance and Health are jointly working on the March trip," and no way to ask whether that work finished. The collaboration that does exist is vestigial: the entire fleet's standing-subscription graph is two edges seeded by Alembic migrations (`core_186:168`, `core_189:31`) and no roster code ever subscribes; two of the four declared event types set `permitted_subscribers = []` and are structurally unhearable (`roster/finance/domain_events.toml:16`, `roster/health/domain_events.toml:16`); the one butler that tightened its tool surface without listing `domain_events` (`roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-20`) silently dropped out of the bus entirely. Multi-butler fan-out dispatches segments and stamps `subrequest_id`/`segment_id` on every envelope (`src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1343`, `src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:697`) but nothing reads them back; the table that held `join_policy`/`abort_policy` was deleted as a dead feature (`roster/switchboard/migrations/014_drop_dead_feature_tables.py:42`), so one owner message becomes three uncoordinated replies. Owner-facing standing concerns admit exactly one producer by construction (`src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.py:37-46`), so a cross-domain concern either gets a single butler's over-confident authorship or two duplicate doors. And a butler handed work outside its scope has no forward move — the only re-routing path is `correct(misroute)`, post-hoc and requiring a *later* session to notice the mistake (`src/butlers/core/corrections.py:60,66`). The fleet shares data. It does not yet share work.

findings.title: Two of the four declared domain events are structurally unsubscribable
findings.detail: `finance.budget_pressure` and `health.recovery_state` — the fleet's only two derived cross-domain advisories — both declare `permitted_subscribers = []`, and the contract registry refuses every subscription request from a butler outside that list before any `public.butler_subscriptions` row is written. Empty list deliberately means 'refuse everyone' (domain_event_contracts.py:237-241 comment). So Finance and Health publish minimized advisories onto a bus that, by contract, nobody can ever hear. The publish path runs, the ledger row is written, the fan-out finds zero subscribers, and the work is discarded.

findings.title: The entire fleet's standing-subscription graph is two Alembic-seeded edges; no butler ever subscribes
findings.detail: The only writes to `public.butler_subscriptions` outside the core module itself are two migration INSERTs: finance←travel.trip_booked and health←travel.trip_active. No roster job, tool, or session anywhere calls the subscribe tool. The bus therefore has a static two-edge topology fixed at migration time, and a butler cannot decide at runtime that another domain's signal matters to it — which is the entire point of a standing subscription. A hardened publisher-owned contract layer, a delivery ledger, a reconciliation sweep with bounded retry, and a reaction-receipt ledger were all built around two hardcoded edges.

findings.title: Tightening a butler's tool surface silently removes it from the fleet bus
findings.detail: `core_groups` defaults to None = all groups enabled (daemon.py:1315,1344). Only three butlers enumerate groups explicitly. Finance lists `domain_events`; Relationship lists `delegation` but not `domain_events`, so the butler whose domain most obviously needs cross-domain signal (birthdays→gift budget, socializing→health load) cannot publish, subscribe to, or receive a single domain event. Nothing warns at boot that an explicitly-enumerated tool surface has cut a butler out of fleet participation — the loss is invisible and indistinguishable from 'no events happened'.

findings.title: The owner condition ledger admits exactly one producer per condition, so cross-domain concerns have no honest home
findings.detail: `source` is `"{origin_butler}:{category}"`, and both the advisory lock and the `snapshot_complete` resolution scope are keyed on it. A concern that exists only because two butlers' evidence combines (Health's recovery state plus General's calendar load; Travel's departure plus Finance's unpaid balance) can only be filed by one butler claiming sole authorship on partial evidence — a door opened with more authority than its evidence supports. Worse, when two butlers each observe the same real concern from their own side, they produce two independent conditions with two escalation clocks, and neither can resolve the other's: the owner gets duplicate doors for one problem and closing one leaves the other escalating.

findings.title: Multi-butler fan-out stamps join identifiers on every envelope and never joins
findings.detail: Both the decomposition path and the direct route path stamp `subrequest_id`, `segment_id`, and `fanout_mode` into the route.v1 envelope. Nothing in `src/butlers/core/` ever reads them back; the only place a join could have lived — `fanout_execution_log`, which carried `join_policy` and `abort_policy` columns — was dropped as a dead feature table with no replacement. The spec's own fan-out requirement stops at per-segment `dispatch_outcomes` and 'partial success', with no requirement that the owner receive one answer. Consequence: one message mentioning a trip, a symptom and a bill produces three independent butler replies to the owner, no cross-check between them, and a segment that never terminates is indistinguishable from one that had nothing to say.

findings.title: A butler handed work outside its scope has no forward move; the only re-route is post-hoc and owner/session-initiated
findings.detail: `correct(correction_type="misroute")` requires `target_session_id` — the UUID of the session that *already made* the mistake — so re-routing can only happen from a later session that notices, and it is rate-limited to 10 corrections per correcting session per hour. There is no tool by which the receiving butler, in the moment, declines with a suggested target or hands the request forward with the request identity preserved, and no way to split a request (keep the part I own, forward the rest). In practice a partially-out-of-scope request is answered badly by whoever got it, and the misroute is never measured — which also starves the routing scorecard and rule-promotion of its highest-signal training data.

findings.title: No channel in the system lets one butler ask another to act
findings.detail: The delegation ledger is scoped to questions by construction ('ask a question that another butler's domain covers'), and the domain-event contract layer states outright that `reaction_expectation`/`reaction_contract` are documentation the bus never enforces and that 'did not act' is never an error. The union of the two sanctioned MCP channels is therefore read-only with respect to other butlers' domains: every cross-domain *action* has to be relayed by the owner by hand, which is precisely the mental labor the vision says the system exists to absorb.

moves.title: Joint Objective register: a durable multi-butler project with a declared division of labor and one closure verdict
moves.why: Vision rule 3 sanctions the Switchboard as the only inter-butler channel but the system has never used it to hold a *shared unit of work* — every existing primitive is one hop (delegate ask/answer, event publish/deliver, briefing union). Run 09's systemic theme 'acceptance impersonating completion' has no cross-butler cure today because there is no object that can refuse to close. Owner payoff: 'Plan the March Japan trip' becomes one row he can open — Travel: flights booked (delivered, evidence: booking id); Finance: budget check (blocked, needs a spend decision); Health: vaccination lead time (accepted, due 14 Feb); Home: away-mode window (proposed, not yet accepted) — instead of four unrelated notifications over three weeks and no way to ask whether the trip is actually handled. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md Responsibilities already claims 'fanout for multi-domain messages' — this is the durable half it never built) and requires one manifesto amendment there adding 'joint objective registrar'. Deliberately NOT the Fleet Case File (read-side retrospective assembly of an existing incident) and NOT RFC 0026 commitments (owner obligations to third parties with no deterministic producer): this is a forward-looking, write-side contract among butlers with acceptance, refusal and closure receipts.
moves.integration_points: New `src/butlers/core/joint_objectives.py` + core-chain migration creating `public.joint_objectives` (id, title, owner_summary, initiator_butler, status, target_date, opened_at, closed_at, closure_receipt JSONB) and `public.objective_stakes` (objective_id, butler, deliverable, state ∈ proposed|accepted|declined|blocked|delivered|withdrawn, decline_reason, evidence_ref, updated_at; UNIQUE(objective_id, butler)). New reserved core group `objectives` in `src/butlers/core_tools/` registering `objective_open`, `objective_stake_offer`, `objective_stake_update`, `objective_close` — stake writes gated on `butler_name` at the tool boundary so a butler can only ever write its own row, and `objective_close` refuses while any stake is non-terminal. Stake offers dispatch through the existing shared transport `src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard_route_dispatch.dispatch_via_switchboard_route`, exactly mirroring `dispatch_delegated_ask` (`_delegation.py:150`). Escalation of a stalled objective reuses `src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.reconcile_snapshot` under source `switchboard:objective-stalled`. New spec `openspec/specs/joint-objectives/spec.md`; amend `openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md` to route >1-hop work here rather than at repeated one-shot asks. Dashboard: new `/objectives` route on the Dispatch shell, each stake a door to that butler's evidence.
moves.slice_plan: S1: tables + core module + `objective_open`/`objective_stake_update` with the own-row-only guard and the non-terminal closure refusal (tests first: closing with one `proposed` stake must fail). S2: `objective_stake_offer` dispatch over `dispatch_via_switchboard_route` + a receiving-side wake mirroring `delegation_wake.handle_delegate_wake`, with `declined` as a first-class terminal. S3: stalled-objective condition producer + `/objectives` dashboard read with per-stake evidence doors. S4: first real objective end-to-end — a booked trip opens an objective with Travel/Finance/Health stakes off `travel.trip_booked`.

moves.title: delegate_act: a mandate request across butlers where the target keeps every ounce of its authority
moves.why: The union of the two sanctioned channels is read-only with respect to other domains: `_delegation.py:14-18` scopes the ledger to questions and `domain_event_contracts.py:68-75` declares reaction contracts unenforceable documentation. So every cross-domain action is relayed by the owner by hand — the exact mental labor vision.md:120-137 says the system exists to absorb. Owner payoff: Travel books a trip and Home arms away-mode for the window without the owner repeating himself; Health asks General to hold a recovery block after a flagged week. Serves the Home manifesto directly — roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:17 promises 'Say "I'm leaving" and we handle it', which today only the owner can say — and Travel's roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md:15 promise that 'nothing falls through the cracks'. Critically it does not weaken rule 3 or rule 6: the target butler's session decides, refusal is a terminal, and any consequential write still passes the target's own approval gate, so no butler ever inherits another's authority.
moves.integration_points: Extend `src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py` with `delegate_act` on the existing reserved `delegation` core group; extend `public.delegation_ledger` (alembic/versions/core/core_162_delegation_ledger.py) with `kind` (ask|act, default ask) and `mandate` JSONB, and add `declined` + `decline_reason` to the answer terminals in `src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py`. Dispatch and return reuse `dispatch_via_switchboard_route` and `src/butlers/core/delegation_wake.py` unchanged. Enforcement point: the receiving butler's action still goes through `src/butlers/core/approvals_policy.py` — add an explicit test that a delegated act requiring approval produces an approval request attributed to the *target* butler, not the asker. Spec: amend `openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md` with an 'Action Delegation' requirement stating the target's refusal right and the no-authority-transfer rule.
moves.slice_plan: S1: ledger `kind`/`mandate` columns + `delegate_act` tool + `declined` terminal, refusal round-trips on the wake path. S2: approval-gate conformance test (delegated act inherits the target's gate, never the asker's). S3: first real pair — `travel.trip_booked` fires a `delegate_act` to Home for the away-mode window; Home may decline with reason and the owner sees the decline, not silence.

moves.title: Co-signed owner conditions: corroboration before a door opens, and one contradiction door when butlers disagree
moves.why: The north star says nothing fabricated and staleness never wears current-data authority; `owner_conditions.py:37-46` violates the spirit of both across domains by admitting exactly one producer per condition. A cross-domain concern is either filed by one butler on partial evidence with full authority, or filed twice with two escalation clocks the owner cannot reconcile. Owner payoff: 'You are over-committed the week of the 12th' opens once, co-signed by General (calendar load) and Health (recovery state), each with its own evidence door — and when Travel says a trip is active while Health's context signal says at_home, the owner sees one honest contradiction door instead of two butlers each acting confidently on a fact the other refutes. Serves the Health manifesto's 'only honesty' commitment and the Switchboard contract (the arbiter is the Switchboard, the one agent whose domain is the system). Distinct from the known entity-merge authority move (that is identity resolution) — this is disagreement about domain *claims* on an already-resolved subject.
moves.integration_points: New `public.condition_attestations` (condition_id, attesting_butler, stance ∈ corroborates|contradicts, evidence_ref, observed_at, confidence; UNIQUE(condition_id, attesting_butler)) alongside `public.owner_conditions`. `src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py` / `owner_conditions.py` gain `corroboration_required: int = 0` on `reconcile_snapshot` so a producer can declare its own evidence insufficient to open a door — the condition sits `pending_corroboration` and never reaches the owner until a second butler attests. New deterministic Switchboard sweep beside `src/butlers/core/domain_event_reaction_sweep.py` that opens a single `switchboard:cross-domain-contradiction` condition when two attestations on one fingerprint disagree. Surfacing: `GET /api/system/conditions` (`src/butlers/api/routers/`) gains co-signer rows and a contradiction state; the dashboard Standing Conditions panel renders each co-signer as its own evidence door. Spec: amend the owner-condition-ledger spec and RFC 0026 §3 with a Corroboration requirement.
moves.slice_plan: S1: attestations table + `corroboration_required` gate + `pending_corroboration` state, with a test that an uncorroborated condition never reaches the delivery surface. S2: contradiction sweep + the single arbiter condition. S3: API + Standing Conditions panel co-signer/contradiction rendering. S4: first real co-signed producer (General calendar load + Health recovery state for over-commitment).

moves.title: Join the fan-out: one inbound message, one owner-facing resolution, honest per-segment accounting
moves.why: The Switchboard's own infrastructure contract claims 'fanout for multi-domain messages' as a responsibility, and every route envelope already carries `subrequest_id`/`segment_id`/`fanout_mode` — but nothing reads them, and the table that held `join_policy`/`abort_policy` was deleted as dead with no replacement. That is Run 09's 'computed-then-discarded truth' at the fleet's most owner-visible seam. Owner payoff: a message that mentions a flight, a symptom and a bill returns one reply with three attributed sections instead of three uncoordinated pings across the day; and when Health's segment never terminates, the reply says '2 of 3 domains answered — Health has not returned' rather than looking complete. This is the unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine applied to multi-domain requests. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (no amendment needed — it already claims the responsibility) and every domain manifesto's implicit promise that a request is not silently half-handled.
moves.integration_points: New `public.request_segments` (request_id, segment_id, subrequest_id, target_butler, state ∈ dispatched|accepted|answered|failed|abandoned, terminal_at, result_ref, join_policy) written from the `__switchboard_route_context` the envelope already carries at `src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1343` and `src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:696`, and settled by `route_execute` (`src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:511`). A Switchboard joiner beside `src/butlers/core/route_inbox.py` applies the declared `join_policy` (all|any|first) and `abort_policy`, reinstating the semantics `roster/switchboard/migrations/001_switchboard_messaging.py:472-483` designed. Egress goes through the existing Messenger notify spine — one composed reply, not N. Unterminated segments after the deadline become a `switchboard:segment-abandoned` owner condition. Spec: add a 'Fan-Out Join and Single Resolution' requirement to `openspec/specs/conversation-decomposition/spec.md` (§59-72) and to `openspec/specs/butler-switchboard/spec.md`.
moves.slice_plan: S1: `request_segments` table + write-on-dispatch/settle-on-terminal from the existing envelope fields (no behavior change; the join identifiers finally persist). S2: joiner with `join_policy=all` + a composed single reply for the decomposition path, with per-domain attribution. S3: abandoned-segment condition + the '2 of 3 answered' honesty line. S4: extend to the direct `route_to_butler` path and retire the per-segment independent notify.

moves.title: Owner forward-draw register: every butler declares what it is about to spend of the owner's money and hours, Finance renders the verdict
moves.why: roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md:20 promises 'We will never surprise you with a bill you forgot about' — a promise Finance structurally cannot keep, because it only knows what it ingested from email and bank feeds. Travel's booked flight, Home's scheduled maintenance, Education's course subscription and Health's appointment copay are all money the fleet itself is committing, invisible to the butler that promised no surprises. The same is true of the owner's hours: every butler schedules against a calendar none of them owns. Owner payoff: before the month starts, one honest line — 'March: $2,940 already committed against a $2,300 discretionary norm; 19 hours already claimed across Education, Health and Travel' — with each row a door to the butler that claimed it. Serves the Finance manifesto directly and requires no amendment: Finance keeps sole authority over the verdict, other butlers only declare their own intent. Distinct from `finance.budget_pressure` (retrospective, actuals-based) and from any attention-budget work (that is delivery frequency, this is money and hours).
moves.integration_points: New `public.owner_draw_claims` (claiming_butler, resource ∈ money|calendar_hours, amount, currency, window_start, window_end, certainty ∈ intended|committed|settled, evidence_ref, superseded_by, created_at) — write-your-own-row only, enforced at the tool boundary like `objective_stakes`. Filing tool on a new reserved `draws` core group; the *reading* verdict is a Finance-owned MCP tool and a deterministic Finance job (`roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py`, which already calls `owner_conditions.reconcile_snapshot` in-process) that opens `finance:forward-oversubscription` when declared draws exceed the owner's declared capacity. Surfaced in the daily briefing via `src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py` and on the Finance dashboard page (`roster/finance/api/router.py`). Producers: `roster/travel/modules/tools.py:96` on booking, Home maintenance scheduling (`openspec/specs/home-maintenance-scheduling`), Education curriculum. Spec: new `openspec/specs/owner-forward-draws/spec.md`; amend `openspec/specs/finance-budgets/spec.md` with a forward-commitment requirement.
moves.slice_plan: S1: table + own-row-only filing tool + Finance-owned summarize tool (read path only, no verdict). S2: Travel files a money draw at `record_booking` and a calendar-hours draw for the trip window — first end-to-end producer. S3: Finance oversubscription condition + briefing line with per-butler doors. S4: Home maintenance and Education subscription producers; `settled` reconciliation against real Finance transactions so a claim is retired by evidence, not by expiry.

moves.title: Negotiated handoff: a butler can decline with a target, or keep its half and forward the rest, in the moment
moves.why: The only re-routing path today is `correct(misroute)`, which requires the UUID of the session that already made the mistake and is capped at 10/hour — post-hoc, dependent on a *later* session noticing, and therefore almost never exercised. A butler handed a partially-out-of-scope request answers it badly and the misroute is never measured, which also starves `openspec/specs/routing-scorecard` and `switchboard-rule-promotion` of their highest-signal input: a butler's own declaration that this was not its work. Owner payoff: the request that mentions both a symptom and an insurance claim is not dropped or half-answered — Health keeps the symptom, forwards the claim to Finance with the same request identity, and the owner sees one chain with two hops rather than one thin answer. Serves vision.md's success marker 'the owner sends a message from any channel and the right butler handles it without manual routing' — currently only true when the first guess is right — and the Switchboard infrastructure contract's classification-accuracy responsibility. No manifesto amendment: declining out-of-scope work is exactly what rule 6's binding governing document already implies each butler should do.
moves.integration_points: Two new core tools in the `infra` group registered in `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py` beside `route_execute` (:511): `handoff(to_butler, reason, retained_scope)` and `decline_scope(reason, suggested_butler)`, callable only from a session that received a `route.execute` envelope (guarded on `get_current_runtime_session_routing_context`, `src/butlers/core/tool_call_capture.py`). Handoff re-dispatches through `dispatch_via_switchboard_route` preserving `request_id` and appending a hop to `switchboard.routing_log` (roster/switchboard/migrations/001_switchboard_messaging.py) with `hop_index` + `handoff_reason`; when Move 4 lands, a handoff opens a new segment on the same `request_id` so the join covers it. Declines and handoffs feed `openspec/specs/routing-scorecard/spec.md` and `openspec/specs/switchboard-rule-promotion/spec.md` as first-class misroute evidence, and a repeated (from, to, reason) triple becomes a promotable routing rule. Bounded by a hop cap (2) so a handoff loop is structurally impossible. Spec: amend `openspec/specs/butler-switchboard/spec.md` and `openspec/specs/error-recovery-corrections/spec.md` to scope `correct(misroute)` back to genuine after-the-fact repair.
moves.slice_plan: S1: `decline_scope` + routing_log hop columns + scorecard ingestion (measure the misroute rate before changing behavior). S2: `handoff` with request identity preservation and the hop cap; owner-visible chain in the conversation/session view. S3: `retained_scope` split — the butler keeps its part and forwards the rest as a sibling segment. S4: rule promotion from repeated handoff triples.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the "knowledge graph" is ten disconnected private graphs plus a summary index. Each memory-loading butler (chronicler, education, finance, general, health, home, lifestyle, relationship, switchboard, travel — roster/*/butler.toml `[modules.memory]`) owns its own `facts`, `rules`, `memory_links`, and — critically — its own `predicate_registry` (src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:406), so the schema of the graph itself forks ten ways while every butler's LLM silently mints new predicates into its private copy as `status='proposed'` (storage.py:1947-1973) that no route, tool, or page ever shows the owner. Growth is therefore unbounded and unreviewed, and trust erodes from four directions at once: the graph deletes its own revision history on a nightly timer (`purge_superseded_facts`, storage.py:3316-3327), leaving orphaned `memory_links` edges and NULLed `supersedes_id` lineage, so "what did you used to believe and why did that change?" is unanswerable; `memory_links.relation='contradicts'` is a legal edge (001:353) that nothing in the repository ever writes, so divergent truth never surfaces and merely makes composite-scored retrieval nondeterministic; the only cross-butler read path gates confidential content on a model-chosen argument (`max_sensitivity`, __init__.py:1814-1824) — exactly the caller-asserted-authority hole AGENTS.md:395-401 forbids elsewhere — and its provenance pointers lead nowhere because no fetch-by-provenance verb exists anywhere in src/; and the fleet's only "graph health" metric is episode cleanup lag (openspec/specs/memory-graph-health/spec.md:53-59), an inventory number silent on anchoring, provenance completeness, promotion yield, or contradiction backlog. The one real cross-domain knowledge flow — chronicler proposing a companion enrichment to relationship (src/butlers/chronicler/writeback.py:631-675) — posts a typed proposal into a mailbox no code reads. The graph grows; nothing tells the owner whether it is getting better or just bigger.

findings.title: Cross-butler catalog sensitivity ceiling is caller-asserted, not server-derived
findings.detail: `memory_catalog_search` accepts `max_sensitivity` as an LLM-supplied argument and `resolve_allowed_sensitivities` simply honors it, so any butler's session reads every other butler's `pii`/`confidential` catalog summaries by passing one string. The spec requires that results the caller is not authorized to view MUST be excluded, but nothing in the system ever establishes what the caller is authorized to view. Same forgery class AGENTS.md bans for actor attribution, sitting on the fleet's only cross-butler read path.

findings.title: Superseded-fact purge measures its retention window from creation, not supersession
findings.detail: The nightly `memory_purge_superseded` job deletes `validity='superseded'` facts where `created_at < now() - 7 days`. The docstring promises the window keeps recent superseded facts for short-term forensics, but a fact created two years ago and superseded one minute ago is deleted on the very next 04:10 run. The forensic window is effectively zero for exactly the long-lived facts whose revision matters most.

findings.title: Purging facts orphans the provenance graph and silently severs lineage
findings.detail: `memory_links` carries no foreign keys, so `supersedes`/`derived_from`/`supports` edges survive their deleted targets permanently and the link table accumulates phantom edges; `facts.supersedes_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so the surviving successor loses even the pointer to what it replaced, with no event recording the loss. Episode deletion was deliberately given content-free tombstones for exactly this reason; fact deletion got no equivalent.

findings.title: memory_entity_neighbors traverses a store that structural edges are forbidden from entering
findings.detail: The traversal CTE follows `facts.object_entity_id` inside the butler's own schema, but the consolidation contract forbids structural relationship predicates (works_at, married_to, friend_of, member_of) in memory facts and routes them to `relationship.entity_facts`, allowing exactly three narrative predicates to carry `object_entity_id`. The fleet's only graph-traversal tool can therefore see planned_dinner_with / wake_coordination / social_exchange_with and nothing else — in every butler, including relationship's own.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:709-716, 731-745; src/butlers/modules/memory/skills/consolidate/SKILL.md ('Only these predicates may carry object_entity_id'; 'Registry-relational edges are not memory facts'); openspec/specs/module-memory/spec.md:310

findings.title: Novel predicates auto-register as 'proposed' and are surfaced to nobody
findings.detail: Any unrecognized predicate an LLM passes to `store_fact` is inserted into that butler's `predicate_registry` with `status='proposed'` and inferred flags. There is no `/api/memory/predicates` route, no status filter on `memory_predicate_list`, and no frontend surface for proposed predicates — so the schema of the knowledge graph grows unboundedly, differently in each of ten schemas, with zero owner review and no promotion path from `proposed` to `active`.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1947-1973; src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:354-2281 (no predicate endpoint in the route list); src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/reading.py:171-200

findings.title: predicate_registry scope CHECK excludes six of the ten memory-loading butlers
findings.detail: The constraint admits only global, health, relationship, finance, home, travel. Education, lifestyle, chronicler, general, messenger and switchboard all enable `[modules.memory]` and cannot register a domain-scoped predicate at all; their knowledge is forced into `scope='global'`, collapsing the namespace that retrieval filters and both property- and edge-fact uniqueness keys depend on.

findings.title: Chronicler's cross-butler enrichment proposal has no consumer or terminal state
findings.detail: `build_relationship_enrichment_proposer` posts `metadata.kind="enrichment_proposal"` with a `dedup_key` into relationship's mailbox via `post_mail`. A repository-wide grep finds the string only at the producer and its test: nothing dispatches on the kind, nothing reads the dedup_key, nothing records accept/reject. The chronicler manifesto's stated promise to propose enrichments ends in an unread mailbox — delivery impersonating adjudication.

findings.title: The catalog's provenance pointer has no retrieval path
findings.detail: `memory_catalog_search`'s docstring states it returns `(source_schema, source_table, source_id)` so the full canonical memory can be retrieved from the owning butler, and the spec repeats it. No MCP tool, API route, or Switchboard verb anywhere accepts that triple. Cross-butler discovery terminates at a truncated summary; the promised second hop does not exist.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1828-1832; openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:197-201; no fetch_by_provenance/catalog_fetch symbol exists under src/

findings.title: memory_events is an append-only audit stream with no reader
findings.detail: Five write sites populate `memory_events` (consolidation success/failure, dead-letter, entity merge, correction-driven forget) and a whole spec exists to enrich its columns 'to support structured audit queries'. Nothing in src/butlers/api/, the frontend, or any MCP tool ever SELECTs from the table. The graph's only audit trail is unreadable in the product — and the decay sweep, the single largest source of belief change, emits nothing into it at all.

findings.title: Decay ignores the usage signal the retrieval path already records
findings.detail: Every recall bumps `reference_count` and `last_referenced_at` on the returned facts and rules, but `run_decay_sweep` anchors effective confidence solely on `last_confirmed_at or created_at`. A fact the fleet retrieves daily expires on exactly the same schedule as one no session has ever touched — the usage evidence is computed and then discarded from the only decision it could inform.

findings.title: Fact scope is a free-text LLM argument that no butler ever configures
findings.detail: `facts.scope` defaults to 'global'; `memory_store_fact` exposes `scope` as an open string parameter chosen by the model; and no `[modules.memory]` block in any butler.toml sets a scope default (they set only `groups`). The documented namespace model — 'Facts live in namespaces (global, health, relationship, finance…)' — is unenforced and in practice unpopulated, while `scope` is a component of both property-fact and edge-fact uniqueness keys.

moves.title: Belief-revision ledger: the graph stops deleting its own history
moves.why: Chronicler's manifesto already states the fleet's position — 'corrections never delete or rewrite the canonical projection; later corrections win; history is always recoverable' (roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md:29-32) — and the memory module violates it nightly, deleting superseded facts on a creation-time clock, orphaning `memory_links` edges and NULLing `supersedes_id` lineage. The north star requires every consequential clause be a door on an unbroken evidence spine; today the door 'why does the system believe this now?' opens onto a deleted row. Owner payoff: 'what did you used to think about X, when did that change, and on what evidence' becomes answerable for every fact, and a belief flip becomes a reviewable event rather than a silent overwrite. Serves relationship ('a friend who never forgets', MANIFESTO.md:3-7), health and finance equally; no manifesto amendment needed.
moves.integration_points: New `fact_revisions` table in the memory Alembic branch (subject, predicate, entity_id, object_entity_id, scope, content, content_hash, confidence, permanence, valid_at, superseded_at, superseded_by_fact_id, reason enum {supersession, retraction, decay_expiry, merge_repoint, correction}, evidence_link_ids). New `facts.superseded_at` column. Write sites: `store_fact`'s supersession branch (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1366-2010, in the same transaction as the validity flip), `forget_memory` (:2425), `run_decay_sweep` expiry (:3140-3200), `entity_merge` repoint (tools/entities.py:844-880). Rewrite `purge_superseded_facts` (:3273-3355) to key the window on `superseded_at`, blank `embedding`/`search_vector` instead of DELETEing the row, and hard-delete only once the revision row exists. Add FK-with-cascade or an explicit integrity sweep for `memory_links` (migrations/001:341-352). New `GET /api/memory/facts/{id}/revisions` in src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py. Amend openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md with a 'Belief revisions are never destroyed' requirement.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Migration: `fact_revisions` + `facts.superseded_at`, backfilling superseded_at from `memory_links(relation='supersedes').created_at`. 2) Write the revision row in `store_fact`'s supersession transaction only; leave the purge untouched. 3) Extend to the forget / decay-expiry / merge write sites. 4) Rewrite the purge onto the superseded_at clock with column-blanking, plus the memory_links integrity sweep. 5) API route and a revision timeline on the fact detail surface.

moves.title: Contradiction as a first-class artifact, with an owner docket
moves.why: `memory_links.relation='contradicts'` has been a legal edge since the first memory migration (001:353) and nothing has ever written one; the consolidation output contract has no contradiction channel at all (skills/consolidate/SKILL.md). Divergent truth therefore never surfaces — it silently makes composite-scored retrieval nondeterministic, which is precisely staleness wearing current-data authority. This is a structural reason the lens tiers weak: the graph has no way to say 'these two beliefs cannot both be true'. Owner payoff: contradictions arrive as a short resolvable list with both sides, their evidence and named verbs, instead of quietly degrading recall. Serves every fact-holding manifesto; resolve verbs respect specialist ownership by routing each contradiction to the butler whose scope holds the losing side.
moves.integration_points: Consolidation: add a `contradictions[]` array ({fact_id_a, fact_id_b|new_fact_index, basis, evidence_episode_ids}) to the prompt contract in src/butlers/modules/memory/skills/consolidate/SKILL.md, the schema in consolidation_parser.py, and persistence in consolidation_executor.py:288-340 via `create_link` (storage.py:2213). Deterministic detector: a bounded read-only pass in the daily sweep modelled on ann_observability.py, flagging (a) two active property facts sharing (entity_id, predicate) across different `scope` values, (b) an active property fact refuted by strictly newer temporal facts on the same (entity_id, predicate), (c) same-(entity_id, predicate) disagreement across butlers via `public.memory_catalog`. New `contradictions` table (fact_a, fact_b, source_schema_a/b, basis, detected_at, state pending|resolved_a|resolved_b|both_valid|dismissed, decided_at). New `GET /api/memory/contradictions` and `POST /api/memory/contradictions/{id}/resolve` in src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py plus a Dispatch docket on /memory. New openspec capability `memory-contradictions`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Detector (a) only — same entity+predicate across scopes — writing `contradicts` links and `contradictions` rows, no UI. 2) Read API plus docket list showing both sides with evidence doors. 3) Resolve verbs on the approval spine (a resolve retracts a live belief, so it is a consequential write). 4) Add the consolidation `contradictions[]` channel. 5) Cross-butler detector (c) over the catalog.

moves.title: One fleet ontology: public predicate registry with an owner curation queue
moves.why: Non-negotiable rule 6 says each manifesto defines 'the conceptual frameworks it uses to structure and prioritize knowledge within its domain', but the vocabulary encoding those frameworks is ten private per-schema copies (migrations/001:406) that drift the moment any butler's LLM mints a predicate, and the auto-registered `proposed` rows (storage.py:1947-1973) appear in no route or page. Six of the ten memory-loading butlers cannot even register a domain-scoped predicate because the scope CHECK predates them (001:428). Owner payoff: the graph's schema becomes a small, curated, reviewable list — adopt / alias / rename / deprecate / reject — instead of an invisible pile quietly forking the fleet's meaning of every relation. `public.entities` and `public.memory_catalog` already precedent the shared table, so rule 3 is respected.
moves.integration_points: Promote `predicate_registry` to `public.predicate_registry` (core Alembic branch) with a child `public.predicate_usage(predicate, butler, usage_count, last_used_at)` so per-butler telemetry survives the merge; replace the frozen scope CHECK with a scope set derived from the roster (roster/*/butler.toml). Grants mirror the narrow model in openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:52. Reads/writes at src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:1578, 1607, 1947-1990 and tools/reading.py:171-260 become schema-qualified. New `GET /api/memory/predicates` (with `?status=proposed`) and `POST /api/memory/predicates/{name}/{adopt|alias|deprecate|reject}` in src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py, plus an Ontology surface under /memory. Amend openspec/specs/module-memory/spec.md and docs/modules/knowledge-base.md; retire the per-schema table in a memory migration.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Read API plus Ontology page fanning out over the existing per-schema registries and showing the drift as-is — this alone makes the invisible visible. 2) `public.predicate_registry` + `predicate_usage` migration with a merge-and-reconcile backfill that reports name collisions rather than silently picking a winner. 3) Repoint all module reads/writes; drop the per-schema table. 4) Curation verbs plus roster-derived scope validation. 5) Block `proposed` predicates from `memory_context` injection until adopted.

moves.title: Graph integrity observation: metrics that say whether the graph is getting better
moves.why: The existing `memory-graph-health` capability measures exactly one thing — episode cleanup lag (spec.md:53-59, models/memory.py:178-191) — an inventory number silent on whether the graph is trustworthy. The north star demands five-second fleet verification with earned calm; nothing today would tell an owner the anchoring rate is falling, provenance is missing, or the vocabulary is forking. Owner payoff: one honest strip answering 'is this graph healthy?' with doors into the offending rows. It reuses the complete/incomplete/unknown coverage discipline the spec already established, so a partial fan-out can never impersonate an all-clear. Serves every memory-loading butler; no manifesto amendment.
moves.integration_points: Extend openspec/specs/memory-graph-health/spec.md with a second requirement set and a `GraphIntegrityPoolObservation` model in src/butlers/api/models/memory.py:178-193, computed in the existing fan-out at src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:213-272 and :354+. Per-pool metrics, each with exact numerator/denominator and nullable-on-unknown: entity-anchoring rate (`facts WHERE entity_id IS NULL AND validity='active'` — unanchored facts can never join the entity graph); provenance completeness (active facts with no `memory_links` row of relation `derived_from`); dangling-edge count (`memory_links` whose target row is gone — guaranteed nonzero today); vocabulary drift (`predicate_registry` rows with `status='proposed'`, plus registered-but-unused); promotion yield (episodes reaching `consolidated` vs `failed`/`dead_letter` per 7-day window, and facts produced per consolidated episode); contradiction backlog. Mirror the aggregate into `memory_stats` (tools/management.py:147-200) so butler sessions can self-assess.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Anchoring rate, provenance completeness and dangling edges — pure SQL over existing tables, no new writes. 2) Promotion yield from `episodes.consolidation_status` and the consolidation `memory_events` rows. 3) Vocabulary drift once the ontology move lands. 4) Dispatch health strip on /memory with each metric a door into a filtered inspect view. 5) Contradiction backlog wired in.

moves.title: Cross-domain fact routing: a typed knowledge-proposal spine with terminal states
moves.why: Chronicler already does the right thing architecturally — it never writes `relationship.entity_facts`, it proposes over MCP (writeback.py:631-675) in service of its manifesto — but the proposal lands as free-text mail with a `metadata.kind` and a `dedup_key` nothing in the repository reads, so a correct design terminates in an unread inbox. Meanwhile the other nine butlers have no channel at all: health learning something about a person, finance learning an employer, lifestyle learning a dietary constraint all either drop it or bury it in their own private `facts` where the manifesto owner can never see it. Owner payoff: knowledge flows to the specialist who owns it, every proposal reaches a terminal state, and the owner can see what one butler tried to tell another. Serves non-negotiable rules 3 and 6 directly — MCP-only through the Switchboard, and specialist manifesto ownership of the write.
moves.integration_points: New `public.knowledge_proposals` (proposer_butler, target_butler, entity_id, predicate, proposed_content, object_entity_id, scope, evidence JSONB of source pointers, dedup_key UNIQUE, state pending|accepted|rejected|superseded|expired, decided_by, decided_at, resulting_fact_id) in the core Alembic branch, grants shaped like `public.memory_catalog`. New `knowledge_proposals` tool group on the memory module (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py, alongside the existing `entity` group): `knowledge_propose`, `knowledge_proposal_list` (target-scoped), `knowledge_proposal_decide` — accept writes through the TARGET butler's own `store_fact`/`relationship_assert_fact`, never a foreign write. Switchboard routing so a proposal wakes the target butler as a classified request rather than a mailbox item (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py). Rewire `build_relationship_enrichment_proposer` (src/butlers/chronicler/writeback.py:631-675) onto `knowledge_propose` and delete the `post_mail` path. Owner-facing `GET /api/memory/proposals` plus a Proposals lane on /memory. New openspec capability `cross-butler-knowledge-proposals`; amend roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md:34-39 to name the spine.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Table plus `knowledge_propose`/`knowledge_proposal_list` with dedup and expiry, chronicler migrated off `post_mail` as the first producer. 2) `knowledge_proposal_decide` writing through the target's own authoritative writer, recording the accept in `memory_events` and `fact_revisions`. 3) Switchboard wake-up so proposals get adjudicated on a schedule rather than opportunistically. 4) Owner Proposals lane with accept/reject visibility. 5) Second and third producers (health→relationship, finance→relationship) to prove generality.

moves.title: Evidence- and usage-aware decay, and forgetting the owner can see
moves.why: Decay today is a pure function of the confirmation clock (storage.py:3127-3129) while the retrieval path already records exactly the signal decay is missing (search.py:565-571) — truth computed and then discarded at the decision point. Worse, a fact whose entire evidence base has been reaped decays identically to one still backed by live episodes, and every expiry is silent: nothing tells the owner what the system stopped believing this week. The relationship butler's whole promise is 'a friend who never forgets' (MANIFESTO.md:3-7), yet it quietly expires facts nobody watched leave. Owner payoff: what the fleet actually uses stops evaporating, orphaned beliefs fade faster, and forgetting becomes a reviewable weekly digest with a one-click keep.
moves.integration_points: `run_decay_sweep` (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:3031-3270): make effective confidence use `max(last_confirmed_at, last_referenced_at)` as the recency anchor and apply an evidence multiplier derived from live `derived_from` links versus `episode_tombstones` (migrations/010). Emit one `memory_events` row per fading/expiry transition with the inputs — the sweep currently emits none — and extend openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md:69-118 ('Retention-class-aware decay sweep') with the usage and evidence inputs plus the event requirement. Reader side: `GET /api/memory/forgotten?window=7d` over `memory_events` (the first reader that stream has ever had), surfaced as a weekly Dispatch digest with `memory_confirm` (tools/feedback.py) as the keep verb, routed through the insight broker so it shares the single attention budget.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Emit decay transition events into `memory_events` — no behaviour change, just make forgetting observable. 2) `GET /api/memory/forgotten` plus the digest surface with the confirm verb. 3) Fold `last_referenced_at` into the recency anchor behind a `memory_policies` column so thresholds stay owner-tunable. 4) Evidence multiplier from live-versus-tombstoned provenance. 5) Route the digest through the insight broker.

moves.title: Server-derived catalog read authority and a real fetch-by-provenance hop
moves.why: The only cross-butler read path gates confidential content on an argument the model chooses (`max_sensitivity`, __init__.py:1814-1824) — the caller-asserted-authority hole AGENTS.md:395-401 names as 'a forgery hole and a misattribution bug at the same time' — and the spec's authorization scenario (memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:225-229) has no mechanism behind it. The same tool's docstring promises a second hop back to the owning butler that exists nowhere in the codebase, so cross-butler reads terminate at a truncated summary. Owner payoff: cross-butler discovery becomes both safe and actually useful — a butler can follow a hit to the real fact through the sanctioned channel, and every above-normal read is attributable. Serves non-negotiable rules 1, 3 and 5 and the switchboard staffer contract.
moves.integration_points: Strip `max_sensitivity` from the `memory_catalog_search` tool signature (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1798-1855) the way `IgnoresCallerAssertedActor` strips caller-asserted actors (src/butlers/api/audit_emit.py pattern); derive the ceiling from a `catalog_read_sensitivity` key in the calling butler's `runtime_config` (rule 5: operational tuning lives in the DB, edited on the dashboard), resolved inside the module and passed to `search_catalog` (search.py:919-960). Log every above-`normal` catalog read to `memory_events` with `actor_butler`. Add `memory_catalog_fetch(source_schema, source_table, source_id)` as a Switchboard-brokered verb (src/butlers/modules/switchboard/, MCP-only per rule 3) that asks the owning butler for the canonical row and returns it under the same server-derived ceiling. Amend openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:197-233 with a 'sensitivity ceiling is server-derived' requirement and a fetch-by-provenance requirement; update docs/modules/memory.md:199-207.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Remove the parameter, hard-default to `normal`, add the `runtime_config` key and dashboard control — closes the hole immediately. 2) Audit every above-normal read into `memory_events`. 3) `memory_catalog_fetch` through the Switchboard, honouring the same ceiling and recording the fetch. 4) Spec and docs amendment.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet's proactivity is a set of per-butler cron jobs that each hand-roll their own trigger logic and funnel candidates into one well-governed broker (`roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py`). The delivery half is genuinely world-class — budget, dedup, cooldown, engagement decay, quiet hours, clustering — but the *production* half is unowned. Every trigger is level-on-presence: something appeared (a transaction, a symptom, a bill, a birthday) and a job noticed. Almost nothing is triggered by *absence*, and the two absence checks that exist are domain-local reimplementations that cannot tell "the owner stopped doing this" from "the sensor stopped reporting" — `roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:340-410` fires "No weight measurement in 20 days — consider logging a new measurement" purely on elapsed time, never consulting `src/butlers/core/liveness.py`, so a broken Google Health connector produces a fabricated claim about the owner's behaviour. Meanwhile the system computes truths it then throws away: `finance.recurring_groups.next_expected_date` is written (`roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py:327,361`) and read only for a display list (`roster/finance/tools/overview.py:754`), so a salary that did not land or a subscription that silently stopped is invisible; `chronicler.routines` mines the owner's weekly rhythm (`src/butlers/chronicler/routines.py:319`) and nothing consumes it; `COMMITMENT_DIRECTIONS` admits `other_to_owner` (`src/butlers/core/commitments.py:123`) but the sole producer hardcodes `owner_to_other` (`roster/relationship/tools/commitments.py:601`), so what *others* owe the owner has no home; `seasonal_periods` and `deadlines` both require the owner to declare them by hand. And the whole proactive layer has no liveness of its own: `scheduled_tasks.last_result` is written (`src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:2212`) and read by nothing, so a scan job that fails every night for a month reads to the owner as calm. The ideal is one production spine — declared watches, an absence primitive that knows whether its sensor was alive, mined rhythm and periodicity feeding it, and a coverage ledger that makes proactive silence provably earned rather than merely quiet.
audits.ideal: A world-class Butlers proactivity layer has three parts the current system only has one of. (1) A **declared watch registry**: every proactive trigger in the fleet is a row — owning butler, data source, evaluation cadence, last evaluated, last fired, suppression count, owner mute state — so the owner can ask "what are you watching for me?" and get a complete, honest answer, and so a broken producer surfaces as *lost coverage* rather than as calm. (2) An **absence primitive alongside the presence primitive**: `public.expected_signals` generalizes the infra deadman pattern (`src/butlers/jobs/external_deadman.py`, `calendar_sync_deadman.py`) to owner data. Producers register expectations they already compute — finance's `next_expected_date`, health's measurement cadence, home's device reporting interval, chronicler's mined routine windows — and one deterministic sweep reconciles absence episodes onto `public.owner_conditions`, with a mandatory sensor-liveness join so an absence whose feeder was down is recorded `unmeasurable`, never `absent`. Absence never impersonates behaviour; the sensor's own silence never impersonates the owner's. (3) **Inference producers for the declarative machinery that already exists**: `deadline_create` and `seasonal_period_create` are excellent engines with no fuel — expiries harvested from typed evidence and annual recurrences mined from the owner's own two-year history should propose into them behind an owner confirmation door, exactly as `secrets_lifecycle` already does for infrastructure. Above all of it, the broker stays the single attention budget and the single door; new triggers never earn a second channel, and every proactive statement carries the watch that fired it and the evidence cohort behind it.

findings.title: Health measurement-gap fires on elapsed time without checking connector liveness — a dead feeder becomes a fabricated claim about the owner
findings.detail: `_scan_measurement_gaps` computes a median cadence from `facts` history and fires when `time_since_seconds >= _GAP_WARNING_MULTIPLIER * median_cadence_seconds`, with no reference to whether the ingesting connector (google_health) has been alive across the gap window. `src/butlers/core/liveness.py` computes exactly that signal and is not consulted. The delivered message asserts owner behaviour ("No {mtype} measurement in {n} days ... Consider logging a new measurement") from what is in fact missing ingestion. This is the north star's "nothing fabricated / failure never impersonates health" clause violated at the point of delivery, and it is the template two other absence checks would copy.
findings.evidence: roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:340-410 (fire condition at :386, message at :400-404); src/butlers/core/liveness.py:35

findings.title: `scheduled_tasks.last_result` is written by three call sites and read by none — a dead proactive scan is indistinguishable from calm
findings.detail: The scheduler records dispatch outcome into `last_result` after every run, and `core_tools/_scheduling.py` does the same for tool-driven runs. Nothing reads the column: not the schedules API, not `src/butlers/core/qa/sources/*`, not the condition ledger, not the dashboard. If `relationship_insight_scan` or `finance_anomaly_insight_scan` throws every night, the only owner-visible symptom is the absence of insights from that domain — which is exactly what a quiet week looks like. Proactive coverage has no liveness.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:2212 (write), src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:2245 (only reader, a list projection), src/butlers/core_tools/_scheduling.py:275,288

findings.title: `finance.recurring_groups.next_expected_date` is computed and persisted but never compared to now — a missing recurring charge or missing income is undetectable
findings.detail: `detect_recurring` derives `next_expected_date = last_seen_date + median_interval` and upserts it. The only consumer is the subscription-overview projection, which formats it for display. No job in `roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py` (insight_scan, anomaly_insight_scan, bill_reconciliation_sweep) queries `recurring_groups WHERE next_expected_date < now()`. So "your salary did not land", "the gym stopped charging you — did that membership lapse?", and "the mortgage debit is 6 days late" are all outside the fleet's reach although the expectation is already in the database.
findings.evidence: roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py:327,352-372 (write); roster/finance/tools/overview.py:737-763 (sole read, display only); roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py:791,1467 (scans that do not consult it)

findings.title: `other_to_owner` and `self` commitment directions have zero producers; the `waiting_for` kind is unreachable
findings.detail: `butlers.core.commitments` validates a three-value direction enum and a five-value kind enum, and the escalation job (`src/butlers/jobs/commitment_escalation.py`) escalates any of them. The only producer in the repo, `capture_commitment`, hardcodes `direction=_DIRECTION_OWNER_TO_OTHER` and can only resolve `kind` to `promise` or `follow_up`. Nothing anywhere creates a `waiting_for`. Half the ledger's declared expressive range — everything another party owes the owner — is dead schema, and the change proposal deferred it explicitly rather than by oversight.

findings.title: `chronicler.routines` is mined with confidence and staleness lifecycle and consumed by nothing
findings.detail: Two migrations and a deterministic miner produce owner weekly routines (dow_mask, local window, support_count, confidence, last_confirmed_at, missed_mine_cycles). The only readers are the miner's own reconciliation and the owner-review PATCH route. No deviation detection, no delivery-timing use, no context-bus publication, no domain event — chronicler has no `domain_events.toml` at all, unlike travel/health/finance. The single richest behavioural model the fleet holds about the owner is inert.

findings.title: Three independent absence mechanisms, no shared primitive, and none records why it believes the signal is absent
findings.detail: Infra absence is a deadman (`external_deadman`, `calendar_sync_deadman`); health absence is a median-cadence gap scan; relationship absence is a Dunbar-tier cadence scan. Each re-derives "expected by when", each fires straight into `propose_insight_candidate`, and only finance routes standing concerns through `public.owner_conditions` at all (two sources: bill-overdue, spending-anomaly). There is no place to ask "what does the system expect to see, and by when", and no absence carries the evidence cohort that would let the owner open the door on it.

findings.title: Seasonal awareness and deadline tracking are engines with no producers — both require the owner to hand-declare every instance
findings.detail: The seasonal spec's only creation paths are `seasonal_period_create` and a fixed preset list (`us-tax-season`, `year-end-holidays`, ...); the deadline spec's only creation path is `deadline_create`. Nothing in the fleet mines a period or infers a deadline from the years of transactions, trips, calendar history and documents it already holds, even though `detect_recurring` already classifies `yearly` frequency and `secrets_lifecycle` proves the expiry-watch pattern for infrastructure credentials. Two well-built pieces of proactive machinery therefore stay empty unless the owner does the work the system exists to absorb.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/seasonal-awareness/spec.md (Requirement: Common Seasonal Period Presets); openspec/specs/deadline-tracking/spec.md (Requirement: Deadline Registration); roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py:325 (_classify_frequency yields 'yearly'); src/butlers/jobs/secrets_lifecycle.py

moves.title: `public.expected_signals` — one absence primitive that knows whether its sensor was alive
moves.why: Vision's success marker "scheduled tasks ... recover from transient failures" and the north star's "failure never impersonates health" both fail at the absence boundary today: health tells the owner they stopped logging when in truth the connector died (roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:386), and finance cannot tell them a recurring debit never arrived even though it already computed when to expect it (roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py:327). One primitive replaces three hand-rolled absence checks and adds the honesty none of them has: an expectation whose feeder was not alive across the window resolves `unmeasurable`, never `absent`. Owner payoff: "your 28th-of-month salary credit has not appeared and it is the 2nd", "the freezer sensor has not reported since Sunday", "you have not logged blood pressure in 20 days — and yes, the watch was syncing the whole time". Serves finance, health and home manifestos without amendment; each stays the producer and the speaker for its own domain.
moves.integration_points: New core module `src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py` + core Alembic migration for `public.expected_signals` (source, fingerprint, expected_by, tolerance_seconds, feeder_key, derivation_evidence, last_observed_at). Sweep job `src/butlers/jobs/expected_signal_sweep.py` on Switchboard (`roster/switchboard/butler.toml`), reconciling onto `public.owner_conditions` via `butlers.core.owner_conditions.reconcile_snapshot` with source `"{butler}:absence:{class}"`, and proposing through `propose_insight_candidate` only on transition. Mandatory feeder-liveness join to `src/butlers/core/liveness.py` before any episode opens. First producers: `roster/finance/tools/pattern_recognition.py` (register on every `recurring_groups` upsert), `roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:340` (replace `_scan_measurement_gaps` in place), `src/butlers/jobs/home.py` (device reporting cadence). New spec `openspec/specs/expected-signal-absence/spec.md`; amend `openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md` to name absence as a first-class candidate origin.
moves.slice_plan: 1) core module + migration + `unmeasurable` semantics with liveness join, unit-tested against a synthetic feeder outage. 2) Health cutover: `_scan_measurement_gaps` becomes a producer, and the fabricated-claim regression gets a test. 3) Finance producer on `recurring_groups` (missed charge + missed income), with `evidence_opened` carrying the derivation window. 4) Home device cadence. 5) Standing Conditions panel filter `class=absence` + evidence door.

moves.title: Waiting-on-them: a producer for `other_to_owner` commitments off the owner's own message stream
moves.why: `butlers.core.commitments` already carries the full lifecycle, confidence bands (0.6 create / 0.8 surface), escalation schedule and closure receipt for three directions, and `src/butlers/jobs/commitment_escalation.py` will escalate any of them — but the only producer hardcodes `owner_to_other` (roster/relationship/tools/commitments.py:601) and must be invoked by an LLM that chose to call the tool. The commitment-lifecycle proposal deferred broader extraction deliberately ("prove the pattern in one domain first"); the pattern is proven. Owner payoff: the mental labour Butlers exists to absorb is not only "what did I promise" but "what am I still owed" — the contract the lawyer said would come Monday, the refund the airline promised, the reply that never came. The 0.6/0.8 bands are already the anti-noise mechanism, so this adds obligations without adding messages. Serves the Relationship manifesto (counterparty state) and, for the non-person cases, argues a Messenger-side follow-up lane rather than a new butler.

moves.title: Watch registry: a declared, owner-visible list of everything the fleet is watching, with coverage liveness
moves.why: Today every trigger is a hardcoded block inside a job file and the owner cannot enumerate them; worse, `scheduled_tasks.last_result` is written and read by nobody (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:2212), so a scan that has failed nightly for a month is indistinguishable from a calm month. The north star demands that staleness never wear current-data authority — proactive silence is the most authoritative claim the system makes, and it is currently unbacked. Owner payoff: one page answers "what are you watching for me, when did each last look, and what did it decide not to tell me", and muting becomes per-watch ("stop watching my Steam hours") instead of a global budget cut. It is also the substrate the already-filed feedback verbs and expired-unseen accounting need in order to attribute a verdict to a producer rather than to a dedup key.
moves.integration_points: New `public.watches` (watch_key, owning_butler, category, data_source, evaluation cadence, muted_by_owner) seeded from git per butler — identity, so declared in `roster/{butler}/watches.toml` alongside `domain_events.toml`, loaded by a core registry mirroring `src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py`. `propose_insight_candidate` (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:179) gains a required `watch_key` and refuses an undeclared one, fail-closed, exactly as the event bus does. A sweep reads `scheduled_tasks.last_run_at`/`last_result` and reconciles `infra_conditions` source `proactive_coverage` when a watch's owning job is failing or overdue. New router `src/butlers/api/routers/insights.py` (`GET /api/insights/watches`) — there is no insights router today. Spec: new `openspec/specs/watch-registry/spec.md` + amendment to `proactive-insight-engine` making `watch_key` part of the candidate schema.
moves.slice_plan: 1) `watches.toml` loader + `public.watches` + fail-closed `watch_key` on the broker, with every existing producer declared (this alone produces the first complete inventory). 2) Coverage-liveness sweep reading `last_result`, opening an infra condition on a dark watch. 3) `GET /api/insights/watches` with last-evaluated, last-fired, suppressed counts. 4) Per-watch owner mute honoured in the delivery cycle. 5) Dashboard surface on the existing Standing Conditions/System page.

moves.title: Chronicler publishes `chronicler.rhythm_deviation` — the mined routine finally gets a consumer, without Chronicler ever nudging
moves.why: Chronicler's manifesto is explicit: "I do not nudge you", one daily message, memory write-back silent. That refusal is why its best asset is inert — `chronicler.routines` carries dow_mask, local window, support_count and confidence (roster/chronicler/migrations/018_routines.py) and nothing reads it. The manifesto-correct shape is publish-not-speak: Chronicler observes that a high-confidence routine window passed with zero corroborating signal for the Nth consecutive occurrence, or that a lane's daily minutes in `daily_rollups` deviated beyond its own 8-week band, and puts a minimized advisory on the domain-event bus. Health and General decide whether that is worth saying — their manifestos own that call, not Chronicler's. Owner payoff: the single most JARVIS-like trigger class the fleet can honestly produce — "you have broken your weekday pattern three days running" — arrives from the butler that owns the owner's wellbeing, on evidence from the butler that owns the past. Serves the Chronicler manifesto by staying inside it, and the Health manifesto by giving it a behavioural signal it cannot otherwise see.

Publication via `src/butlers/core/domain_events.record_event`; reaction on the Health side through the existing `domain_event_reactions` path, terminating in `propose_insight_candidate` so the one attention budget still governs. Baseline table for lane bands via a new chronicler migration.

moves.title: Expiry harvest: give `deadline_create` the producers `secrets_lifecycle` already has for infrastructure
moves.why: The deadline engine is complete — thresholds, escalation state machine, dependencies, prompt context injection (openspec/specs/deadline-tracking) — and entirely unfuelled, because every deadline must be typed by hand. Meanwhile the same repo already runs `src/butlers/jobs/secrets_lifecycle.py` to watch credential expiry automatically: the pattern is proven for infrastructure and absent for the owner's own life. Owner payoff: the passport that expires inside the visa lead time, the card that expires before the annual renewal it funds, the warranty that lapses next month, the prescription that runs out mid-trip — all sitting in data the fleet already holds (travel bookings, `finance` subscription/bill facts, home maintenance records, health medication rows) and none of it watched. Serves the Travel, Home, Finance and Health manifestos; the crucial constraint is that a harvested expiry is a *proposal* — it enters as an owner-confirmable candidate, never as a silently registered deadline, so a wrong extraction never becomes a schedule the owner did not agree to.
moves.integration_points: A typed `expires_on` predicate convention on `relationship.entity_facts`/domain fact tables (predicate taxonomy: `openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md`), harvested per-domain by the butler that owns the source — travel from bookings, finance from `subscriptions`/`bills` facts, home from maintenance records, health from medication rows. A shared helper `src/butlers/core/expiry_harvest.py` turns a confirmed expiry into a `deadline_create` call on the owning butler's `scheduled_tasks` with domain-appropriate `lead_time_days`/`alert_thresholds`. Confirmation rides the existing approvals spine (`src/butlers/modules/approvals`, `openspec/specs/module-approvals`) rather than a new gate. moves.title: Mined annual recurrence — the owner's own year, learned instead of declared
moves.why: `seasonal_periods` exist only as hand-typed rows or a fixed five-preset list (openspec/specs/seasonal-awareness), and the scheduler's seasonal-context injection is a good engine idling. The fleet holds multi-year evidence of the owner's actual annual shape: `finance.transactions` (whose `_classify_frequency` already recognises `yearly`), Chronicler `daily_rollups` and episodes, calendar history, Travel trips, and Health symptom/environment correlations. Owner payoff: "last year you started the insurance renewal in the second week of September, and the quote took eleven days" — anticipation from the owner's own history rather than from a US-centric preset list, which is the difference between a personal system and a calendar app. This is the only trigger class in the fleet that can be genuinely *earned* by longevity, and it directly serves the vision's measure ("runs for weeks without intervention ... progressively more autonomy"). Serves General as the cross-domain owner-context butler, with Finance and Travel as evidence contributors; if General's manifesto does not stretch to owning learned periodicity, this implies a small amendment naming annual owner-rhythm as General's.
moves.integration_points: Deterministic miner `src/butlers/jobs/annual_recurrence.py` (zero LLM, matching the Chronicler routine miner's discipline) over read surfaces the owner already grants: `finance.recurring_groups WHERE estimated_frequency='yearly'`, `public.calendar_events` history, `chronicler.daily_rollups`, travel trips. Registers into `public.expected_signals` (move 1) so a mined annual event that fails to recur is itself an absence.
