audits.ideal: A single Autonomy Envelope policy layer sits above the approval gate and answers one question before anything is parked: may this class of act proceed right now, given how absent the owner actually is? It reads a measured owner-reachability state (present / quiet / away / unreachable, each stamped measured-vs-assumed with its evidence), matches the invocation to a declarative per-(butler, action-class) envelope that names the deepest absence it tolerates, its consequence class, its bounded budget (counts and committed money, not just tokens), and its mandatory reversal window; and it authorizes an unsupervised act only when the tool has a registered compensating action so the owner can undo it on return. Anything outside its envelope enters a durable escalation ladder that tries the owner's channels in order over hours — not one Telegram push and silence — and, when the ladder exhausts, reaches an explicit safe-hold terminal that names what was deliberately not done and, where the envelope allows, takes the reversible holding action instead. Every act taken under an envelope, every rung attempted, every hold and every lapse writes one row into an unsupervised-action ledger, and the owner's first authenticated presence after an absence opens one Homecoming review: what proceeded and on whose authority, what it committed, what is still revertible and until when, what is held and now needs a decision, what lapsed unattended. Before a known absence the owner — or the Travel Butler, drafting from the itinerary — signs a time-boxed Absence Plan that elevates specific envelopes for exactly the trip window and expires on its own. Absence never silently becomes consent, never becomes disengagement, and never becomes a fabricated calm.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has a strong approval gate and nothing above it. The gate is binary and presence-blind: `_make_gate_wrapper` (src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py:545-640) decides owner-vs-non-owner and standing-rule-vs-park and never reads `public.user_context`, even though the context bus already tracks `traveling`, `sleeping`, `away`, and `dnd` (openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md:26) and no file under src/butlers/modules/approvals/ imports `is_user_in_context`. The only runtime authority model is five booleans that are default-allow and fail-open (src/butlers/core/permissions.py:68-78, :28-35) with no dimension for presence, consequence, amount, or time-box, so "what may proceed without the owner" is literally not expressible. Notification of a parked action is one hardcoded Telegram push emitted once at park time (src/butlers/modules/approvals/notifications.py:140, :186; called only from park.py:109) with no second channel, no rung, and no retry sweep for a `failed` outcome (:373, :392, :442) — an owner abroad with a dead Telegram path is unreachable by construction. Nothing sweeps expiry (`expire_stale_actions` exists only as an MCP tool, module.py:437, and an API route, api/routers/approvals.py:1383, and is absent from the scheduled_jobs.py registry), so a consequential act that dies unattended produces no event, no attention-ledger row, and no word to the owner until someone clicks it. `reversibility` is a CHECK-constrained string that is printed and never read (migrations/005_decision_dossier.py:87, notifications.py:116); the only real undo in the repo is calendar's hardcoded inverse map (api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:3147). And the one mechanism that does react to owner silence reads it backwards: fourteen days of no reply auto-downgrades proactive insights to `off` with no automatic restoration (openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:144-154), so a two-week trip is punished as if the owner had judged the insights useless. The distance to the ideal is not the gate — it is that there is no policy layer above the gate at all.

findings.title: Disengagement ratchet cannot distinguish an absent owner from a rejecting one
findings.detail: Engagement is defined as the owner sending any message within 60 minutes of delivery. An owner asleep, traveling without connectivity, or otherwise unreachable produces engagement_rate 0.0; after 14 such days the system auto-downgrades verbosity to `off`, and the spec explicitly forbids any automatic restoration when engagement returns. Absence is permanently interpreted as rejection, and the owner must notice and manually re-enable a subsystem that silenced itself for being ignored by someone who was not there. No reachability state is consulted anywhere in the ratchet.

findings.title: Approval escalation is one hardcoded channel, emitted once, never retried
findings.detail: `build_approval_request_envelope` and `build_approval_digest_envelope` both hardcode `"channel": "telegram"`. `emit_approval_push` has exactly one caller — `park_pending_action` at park time — so there is no second attempt, no alternate channel, and no scheduled sweep that re-drives a reservation whose outcome is `failed` (recorded when no owner Telegram recipient resolves, when APPROVAL_CALLBACK_SECRET is unavailable, or on any egress exception). The `push_outcome` honesty flag makes the failure visible only on a dashboard the absent owner cannot see. For the owner-absent case this is the load-bearing defect: one dead channel makes every consequential act unreviewable until it lapses.

findings.title: No scheduled expiry sweep, so a lapsed approval is never announced
findings.detail: Expiry is enforced correctly but lazily: `expire_pending_action_if_stale` fires only on a decision attempt, which is a proper denial boundary. But `expire_stale_actions` is reachable only as an MCP tool and an API route and appears nowhere in the scheduled-job handler registry. Consequence: an action whose window elapses while the owner is away emits no `action_expired` event, writes no attention-ledger row, and produces no notification. The owner returns to a queue whose rows still read `pending` with a past `expires_at`, and nothing states 'these N consequential things died unactioned while you were gone' — staleness wearing current-data authority.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/module.py:437; src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1383-1401; src/butlers/modules/approvals/operations.py:55-101; src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py (no approvals handler in the registry)

findings.title: The only runtime authority model is five booleans, default-allow and fail-open
findings.detail: `ENFORCED_PERMISSIONS` is exactly `calendar.write, cross_butler, email.send, notify, spawn`; a missing row means allowed (`PERMISSION_DEFAULT_GRANTED = True`) and a failed lookup also means allowed. There is no axis for owner presence, consequence class, monetary amount, blast radius, reversal window, or time-box, and no way to say 'this may proceed only while I am reachable' or 'this may proceed for the next nine days only'. The matrix cannot express any part of an owner-absent policy, and the approvals gate consults it not at all when deciding to park.

findings.title: `reversibility` is a decorative dossier string that no code branches on
findings.detail: The column is CHECK-constrained to a fixed vocabulary and rendered into the Telegram dossier line, and that is the whole of its life: no gate decision, no executor behavior, no retention rule, and no revert path reads it. The only actual undo in the repository is calendar's hardcoded inverse-tool map, reachable from one bespoke endpoint. Unsupervised execution is therefore un-underwritable — no machinery could promise 'this can be taken back when you return'.

findings.title: Quiet-hours deferral silently shortens the owner's decision window
findings.detail: `expires_at` is fixed at park time as `now + expiry_hours`, but when the Owner Attention Policy is in its quiet window the push is deferred to the window's end instead of dispatched. The action's clock keeps running through the hold, so an action parked at the start of an overnight quiet window reaches the owner with up to nine fewer hours of decision time than its configured expiry states — while the dossier still prints the original `Expires:` value as though the full window were available.

moves.title: Owner Reachability State — one measured, evidence-carrying answer to "is the owner there?"
moves.why: vision.md:6-10 makes the Switchboard the keeper of shared situational awareness, and the north star forbids staleness wearing current-data authority. Today three subsystems each guess at owner presence from a different partial signal — quiet hours from a clock (core/approvals_policy.py), engagement from a 60-minute inbound window (openspec/specs/insight-delivery/spec.md:48-62), and context-bus signals nobody in the approvals path reads (openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md:26). Owner payoff: every downstream decision about acting alone rests on one honest, citable reading rather than three silent inferences, and the disengagement ratchet stops punishing travel. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (shared situational awareness); requires a contract amendment naming reachability as a Switchboard responsibility.
moves.integration_points: New `src/butlers/core/owner_reachability.py` + `public.owner_reachability_observations` (append-only) and a derived reader returning `{state: present|quiet|away|unreachable|unknown, since, confidence, provenance: measured|assumed, evidence[]}`; inputs are last owner-resolved ingress per channel (butlers/identity.py resolve_contact_by_channel), last approval decision in `pending_actions.decided_at`, last dashboard turn (core/dashboard_turns.py), and active `public.user_context` rows; consumers are `core/attention_ledger.py`, `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py`, `modules/approvals/gate.py`, and the envelope evaluator; new spec `openspec/specs/owner-reachability/spec.md` plus an amendment to the total-disengagement scenario at openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:144.
moves.slice_plan: 1) table + reader + spec, provenance-honest with an explicit `unknown` state when no source is fresh; 2) wire the ratchet to exclude days where the state was `unreachable` (fixes finding 1); 3) expose it as one honest chip on /overview and in the LLM context preamble.

moves.title: Autonomy Envelopes — the declarative policy layer above the approval gate
moves.why: security.md:101-121 defines gates but says nothing about who may act when the owner cannot answer, and the permissions matrix cannot express it (src/butlers/core/permissions.py:68-78). Standing rules answer 'have I approved this exact shape five times' (openspec/specs/autonomy-tracker/spec.md:71-98) — a pattern question. Nothing answers the policy question 'may this class of act proceed at all while I am away, and how much of it'. Owner payoff: one page where the owner states, per domain, exactly how far the fleet may go alone — and a system that can prove it stayed inside those lines. Serves every domain manifesto by making each specialist's autonomy explicit rather than emergent; implies a doctrine amendment adding an Autonomy Envelope section to about/heart-and-soul/security.md beside Approval Gates.
moves.integration_points: New `public.autonomy_envelopes` (butler, action_class, max_reachability_state, consequence_class, window budget, reversal_window_hours, requires_compensator, audit reason) superseding the five-boolean matrix in `src/butlers/core/permissions.py`; evaluation hook inside `_make_gate_wrapper` (src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py:545-640) before the park branch, writing `decided_by = 'envelope:<id>'` and a new `action_envelope_authorized` event type extending the canonical list at openspec/specs/module-approvals/spec.md:243; `/settings/permissions` (openspec/specs/dashboard-permissions/spec.md) becomes the envelope editor under its existing mandatory-reason discipline; new spec `openspec/specs/autonomy-envelopes/spec.md`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) table + evaluator + spec with every envelope defaulting to 'never proceed unsupervised' (fail-closed, unlike today's default-allow matrix); 2) gate integration behind a config flag with a dry-run mode that only records what it would have authorized; 3) matrix page → envelope editor with a blast-radius preview reusing the TARGET-STATE preview at openspec/specs/module-approvals/spec.md:422.

moves.title: Escalation ladder with an explicit safe-hold terminal
moves.why: security.md:118-120 requires the approval mechanism to work across all notification channels and timeouts to result in denial — today it is one Telegram push, once, with no retry (notifications.py:140, :186; park.py:109) and denial arrives silently (finding 3). Owner payoff: an approval genuinely chases the owner across channels over hours, and when it truly cannot reach them the fleet takes the reversible holding action and says so, instead of letting a real-world consequence expire into nothing. Serves the Messenger infrastructure contract (it owns outbound delivery and channel parity) and the Switchboard contract's escalation-procedure responsibility.
moves.integration_points: New `approval_escalation_attempts` (action_id, rung, channel, attempted_at, outcome) in the approvals module schema; ordered rungs resolved from the owner's `relationship.entity_facts` channels (telegram → secondary telegram → email → dashboard push) rather than the hardcoded string at notifications.py:140; a scheduler handler `approval_escalation_sweep` registered in `src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py` that also drives the missing `expire_stale_actions` sweep; each attempt records into `core/attention_ledger.py`; `ActionStatus` gains a `safe_hold` terminal, amending the Status Transition Contract at openspec/specs/module-approvals/spec.md:71-119 and the channel-parity requirement at :361.
moves.slice_plan: 1) the sweep + attempts table + expiry sweep (kills findings 2 and 3 with one job); 2) multi-rung channel resolution with per-rung wait taken from the envelope; 3) `safe_hold` terminal plus optional envelope-declared holding action.

moves.title: Compensating-action registry — reversal windows as the currency that buys unsupervised authority
moves.why: An envelope should only authorize an unsupervised act if the owner can take it back. Today `reversibility` is a printed string nothing reads (finding 5) and the only inverse-action machinery is calendar's hardcoded map (api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:3147). Owner payoff: 'what did the fleet do while I was gone, and can I undo it?' becomes one door per item instead of a research project. Serves the Home manifesto ("we ask for confirmation before destructive actions") by giving it a second safety net, and the Travel and Messenger manifestos whose acts are the ones most likely to fire unsupervised.
moves.integration_points: Extend `ToolMeta` in `src/butlers/modules/base.py` with `compensating_action: {tool_name, args_from_result}`; `src/butlers/modules/approvals/executor.py` persists pre-state plus a materialized compensator plan alongside `execution_result`; new `POST /api/approvals/actions/{id}/revert` in `src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py` replaying the plan through `dispatch_approved_action`'s owning-daemon seam (never re-entering the gate) and appending an `action_reverted` event; generalize then retire `_UNDO_INVERSE_TOOL` in `api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:3147`; envelope evaluation refuses to authorize any tool lacking a registered compensator; amends the Shared Executor Path requirement and the `reversibility` semantics in openspec/specs/module-approvals/spec.md.
moves.slice_plan: 1) ToolMeta field + startup registry validation mirroring `validate_owner_command_registry` (command_contracts.py:126); 2) executor pre-state capture + revert endpoint, proved on calendar by replacing the hardcoded map; 3) messenger/home/travel compensators, then flip the envelope precondition on.

moves.title: The Homecoming Review — one unsupervised-action ledger replayed as a single session on return
moves.why: The 'provable audit story for everything done while unsupervised' has no home today: acts land in `pending_actions`, escalation attempts nowhere, lapses nowhere (finding 3), and the audit log (openspec/specs/dashboard-audit-log/spec.md) is a flat mutation stream with no absence framing. North star: every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine. Owner payoff: five-second verification of a week away — what proceeded and on whose authority, what it committed, what is still revertible and until when, what is held awaiting them, what died unattended. No existing manifesto owns fleet-wide narration, so this implies a Switchboard infrastructure-contract amendment rather than a new butler.
moves.integration_points: New `public.unsupervised_ledger` (act_id, butler, envelope_id, reachability_state_at_decision, consequence_class, committed_cost_usd, revert_deadline, outcome) written by the envelope evaluator, the escalation sweep, and the expiry sweep; new `/homecoming` dashboard route in Dispatch, addressable by absence window, with a Revert door per item (move 4) and a Decide door per held item linking to the existing approvals detail route; a matching deterministic Telegram digest composed like `format_approval_request_message` (no LLM, mirroring notifications.py's zero-model contract); new spec `openspec/specs/owner-homecoming-review/spec.md`; triggered by the reachability state transitioning back to `present` (move 1), not by a clock.
moves.slice_plan: 1) ledger table + writes from the sweeps — valuable even before envelopes authorize anything, because it captures lapses and escalations; 2) /homecoming page with revert and decide doors; 3) return-transition trigger + one-shot digest with a coalescing guard.

moves.title: Committed-cost authority — a real-world spend budget beside the token ceiling
moves.why: The only ceiling in the system halts the LLM fleet on token spend (openspec/specs/dashboard-spend-dashboard/spec.md:310-319); nothing bounds the real-world cost of an unsupervised act. The Finance manifesto is explicit that finance gains no ability to move money, so the right shape is not payment authority but a committed-cost budget: any act creating an obligation declares its estimate, decrements a per-window envelope budget, and hard-parks when the budget cannot cover it. Owner payoff: 'while I was away the fleet could commit at most $150; it committed $42 across three acts, each still revertible.' Serves the Travel manifesto (rebooking and change fees are exactly this) and the Home manifesto (device/energy commitments); the Finance manifesto is preserved unchanged and becomes the ledger of record for what was committed.
moves.integration_points: Add `estimated_cost_usd NUMERIC` to `pending_actions` (a fifth dossier field alongside why/evidence/blast_radius/reversibility; migration under src/butlers/modules/approvals/migrations/) and an `_estimated_cost` gate-only dossier key in the schema injection at gate.py:143; new `public.autonomy_budget_ledger` decremented inside the envelope evaluator's transaction; `/settings/spend` gains a 'committed-cost authority' panel beside the token ceiling reusing the existing `audit.append("spend.ceiling")` pattern; amends openspec/specs/dashboard-spend-dashboard/spec.md and the new autonomy-envelopes spec; travel and home declare cost estimators for their obligating tools.
moves.slice_plan: 1) dossier field + ledger + evaluator decrement with a fail-closed 'unknown cost cannot be authorized' rule; 2) spend-page panel and Homecoming roll-up; 3) travel/home estimator adoption.

moves.title: Absence Plans — time-boxed, owner-signed envelope elevations drafted from the itinerary
moves.why: An envelope set tuned for normal life is wrong for a nine-day trip, and asking the owner to remember to widen it is exactly the mental labor vision.md:120-137 exists to absorb. A plan signed in advance keeps single-user sovereignty intact (vision.md:60) — there is no deputy and no second authority, only the owner deciding earlier. Owner payoff: before a trip, one screen shows exactly what changes, for exactly which dates, and it expires on its own. Serves the Travel manifesto directly ("prepare with peace of mind"; upcoming trips ranked by urgency): the Travel Butler proposes the plan from a stored trip and the owner signs or edits it.
moves.integration_points: New `public.absence_plans` (window_start, window_end, envelope_overrides JSONB, signed_by, signed_at, reason) read by the envelope evaluator, with a hard rule that a plan cannot outlive its window and cannot be extended by any non-human actor; a Travel-side producer drafting a plan from a `travel.trips` row and posting it as a pending action through the normal gate, so the plan itself is approved by the machinery it governs; composer on `/settings/permissions` beside the envelope editor with a diff view against defaults; new requirement in `openspec/specs/autonomy-envelopes/spec.md` plus a scenario added to `openspec/specs/butler-travel/spec.md`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) table + evaluator override with expiry enforcement and an audit row per activation and expiry; 2) the /settings composer with the defaults diff; 3) the Travel-drafted proposal path, gated like any other consequential write.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the home butler does not perceive a house — it caches a bag of Home Assistant entity-ID strings. Its entire durable model of the physical world is three tables (roster/home/migrations/001_home_tables.py:78-126): one upserted current-state row per entity with no history, an actuation log with no actor/session/approval/status column, and a calendar-interval maintenance list. Rooms exist only as an in-memory `_area_cache` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:227) and a denormalized `area_name` string stuffed into JSONB (line 2058), so no butler can name a room and mean the same room. Presence is one fleet-wide boolean set by any person entity reading `home` (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:196), timestamped by the module's own write clock rather than the house's, so an HA outage leaves `at_home` and every reported room temperature wearing full current-data authority (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:2083; roster/home/api/router.py:338-343; src/butlers/jobs/home.py:168-210). All history is a live recorder call that returns `available: False` when HA is down (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:1389-1430) even though the connector already writes every state change durably to `connectors.home_assistant_history` (alembic/versions/core/core_084_home_assistant_history.py:7-19), which home has SELECT on (scripts/init-db.sql:420-426) and never reads. And the one tool that can unlock the front door is the only consequential write in the roster with no approval gate at all (roster/home/butler.toml:38 vs roster/messenger/butler.toml:71-77): the manifesto's confirmation promise is enforced by prose in AGENTS.md asking the model to wait for an emoji. Two of the manifesto's four promise pillars — Scene Composition, and the money half of Energy Awareness — have no schema, no tool, and no spec requirement anywhere.
audits.ideal: A JARVIS in a physical household keeps its own model of the house, not a cache of someone else's. Home Assistant stays the sovereign local hub and the only transport — no vendor cloud — but the butler holds a durable perception ledger built from the state-change stream the connector already persists, so the house's past survives HA restarts, recorder purges, and outages, and every reading carries the timestamp the sensor reported, never the timestamp the writer ran. Rooms and devices are first-class identities in `public.entities` (place/other), so climate, presence, calendar, sleep, and energy join on the same study, the same dryer. Presence is owner-scoped and room-resolved with an honest unknown, and it feeds the context bus with lead time — arriving in eight minutes, not merely absent — so pre-conditioning is possible instead of reactive. Actuation is the sharp end: every service call is a proposal against a declared physical-risk map, parked on the approval spine when it is consequential, executed with a receipt carrying session, request, approval, outcome, and a post-condition read confirming the house actually changed. Routines are butler-owned composable objects with per-step evidence, not opaque HA scenes triggered by name. Energy is denominated in the owner's currency against a declared tariff and handed to finance as a reconcilable estimate that learns its own accuracy. Maintenance is due when the house says so — runtime hours, discharge slope — not when a calendar interval elapses. Everything consequential is a door on an unbroken spine; nothing stale ever claims to be current.

findings.title: The physical actuator is the only consequential write in the roster with no approval gate
findings.detail: `roster/home/butler.toml:38` declares `[modules.approvals]` with no `enabled` key and no `gated_tools`; `parse_approval_config` defaults `enabled = raw.get("enabled", False)` (src/butlers/config.py:526), so the gate never wraps anything. The module declares `ToolMeta(arg_sensitivities={"domain": True, "service": True})` for `ha_call_service` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:266, specced at openspec/specs/module-home-assistant/spec.md:358) — metadata computed for a consumer that is switched off. Every other butler that loads approvals enables it and pins gated tools: messenger gates `telegram_send_message` (roster/messenger/butler.toml:71-77), relationship gates `memory_reclassify` (roster/relationship/butler.toml:164-169), switchboard gates `connector_disconnect` (roster/switchboard/butler.toml:46-52). A memory reclassification is gated; `lock.unlock`, `alarm_control_panel.alarm_disarm`, and `cover.open_cover` on the garage are not. The manifesto states 'Arm/disarm automations require explicit user confirmation' and 'We ask for confirmation before destructive actions'; the only enforcement is a prose instruction to the model to wait for an emoji reaction (roster/home/AGENTS.md, Safety and Confirmation).
findings.evidence: roster/home/butler.toml:38; src/butlers/config.py:526; roster/home/modules/__init__.py:263-267; roster/messenger/butler.toml:71-77; roster/relationship/butler.toml:164-169; roster/switchboard/butler.toml:46-52

findings.title: Snapshot freshness is the writer's clock, so an HA outage reads as a healthy house
findings.detail: `_persist_entity_snapshot` sets `captured_at = now()` for every entity on every cycle regardless of whether HA reported anything (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:2078-2084), and `_snapshot_loop` runs unconditionally, never checking `_ws_connected` (lines 2010-2018). If the WebSocket dies and the REST poll also fails (`_poll_loop` swallows exceptions at line 1322), the in-memory cache freezes while `captured_at` keeps advancing. `/snapshot-status` then reports those advancing bounds as the freshness signal (roster/home/api/router.py:338-343), and `_read_entity_snapshot` — the reader behind the daily environment report, device health check, and energy digest — does not select `captured_at` at all and applies no staleness check (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:168-210). The owner receives a Telegram message asserting current room temperatures that may be days old, with no degraded envelope and no door to the truth. This inverts 'staleness never wears current-data authority' in the one domain where a wrong reading has physical consequences.

findings.title: `at_home` asserts owner presence from any person entity, and measures freshness on the wrong clock
findings.detail: `resolve_presence` returns True the moment any fresh `person.*` or `device_tracker.*` row reads `home` (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:184-199) — a housemate, a guest's phone, a robot vacuum's tracker. The resulting `at_home` signal is fleet-wide and read by every butler as 'the owner is here' (it gates insight delivery and quiet hours). No owner scoping is applied even though the identity key exists and is already used correctly one directory over: the chronicler resolves presence entities through `connectors.home_assistant_persons.ha_entity_id` (src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/home_assistant.py:40-42). Compounding it, freshness is evaluated against `row['captured_at']` (line 188) — the writer clock from the previous finding — not the HA-reported `last_updated` the same table carries.

findings.title: Physical actuation is off the signal-to-session-to-evidence spine, and a failed command looks like a successful one
findings.detail: `ha_command_log` carries only `domain, service, target, data, result, context_id, issued_at` (roster/home/migrations/001_home_tables.py:88-99) and `_log_command` writes nothing more (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1881-1935): no `session_id`, no `request_id`, no approval reference, no actor. The only correlation handle is HA's own `context_id`, which points into HA, not into the butler spine. The owner reading `/api/home/command-log` (roster/home/api/router.py:241) sees '03:12 lock.unlock front_door' with no reachable answer to who asked, which session ran, or why. Worse, failures are written into the same `result` column as successes — `log_result = result if result is not None else error_result` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1922) — with no status column, so a failed unlock and a completed unlock are structurally identical rows until something parses the JSON for an `error` key.

findings.title: The house has no memory of itself, while a durable house-history table sits readable and unread
findings.detail: `ha_entity_snapshot` is one upserted row per entity by construction — `ON CONFLICT (entity_id) DO UPDATE` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:2079), specced as such at openspec/specs/butler-home/spec.md:120-131 ('a later state update for the same entity MUST overwrite its row in place'). Every historical question therefore requires a live WebSocket call to HA's recorder, which returns `{'available': False}` when HA is unreachable (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:1389-1430) and is bounded by HA's own purge window. Meanwhile the connector already persists every state change indefinitely with full attributes to `connectors.home_assistant_history` (alembic/versions/core/core_084_home_assistant_history.py:7-19), and butler roles are granted SELECT on the whole `connectors` schema explicitly 'for dashboards/routes' (scripts/init-db.sql:420-426). No file under `roster/home/` or `src/butlers/jobs/home.py` references it. The chronicler mines the owner's house history; the home butler cannot.

findings.title: Scene Composition — a full manifesto pillar — has no schema, tool, spec requirement, or UI
findings.detail: The manifesto dedicates an entire promise section to composable scenes ('Scenes are composable: build them from smaller automations, combine them, modify them. No coding required') and lists 'Build and trigger scenes' under What You Can Do. The implementation is one pass-through wrapper, `_activate_scene`, which requires an `entity_id` starting with `scene.` that someone authored inside Home Assistant's own UI (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1943-1994). There is no scene or routine table in roster/home/migrations/001_home_tables.py, no scene requirement anywhere in openspec/specs/butler-home/spec.md (requirements at lines 9-160), and no actuation or scene route in roster/home/api/router.py — the single pane can read the house and edit maintenance items but cannot act on the house at all. The `scenes` skill under roster/home/.claude/skills documents a capability the butler does not have.

findings.title: Energy Awareness ships kWh only; the money half of the promise has no representation
findings.detail: The manifesto promises 'how much you're spending', 'optimizations that save money', and a digest tracking 'progress toward your efficiency goals'. `_build_digest_message` emits kWh totals, kWh top consumers, percentage anomalies, and three canned English recommendations — no currency, no tariff, no rate, no cost anywhere (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:1612-1677). There is no tariff table in roster/home/migrations/001_home_tables.py and no cost field on the energy endpoints (roster/home/api/router.py:521-752). An owner cannot be told what an anomaly cost them, and finance — which owns bills and promises 'never surprise you with a bill' (roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md:20) — never hears from home before the utility bill lands.

findings.title: `away` and `commuting` are declared fleet signals with zero producers, while OwnTracks data sits unread by home
findings.detail: `ContextSignal` declares `away` and `commuting` (src/butlers/context_bus.py:31,33); no `set_context` call for either exists across src/butlers/jobs/ or src/butlers/core_tools/ — the home producer only clears `at_home` and returns the string 'away' inside its own result dict (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:235-238). Meanwhile the OwnTracks connector durably persists GPS points with region-transition triggers to `connectors.owntracks_points` (alembic/versions/core/core_081_owntracks_points.py:7-31), and the provider feature catalogue explicitly asserts the pairing ('owntracks', 'home', 'Location tracking', 'medium') (alembic/versions/core/core_107_provider_feature_catalogue.py:183-184). The catalogue advertises a home capability the home butler does not implement — no file under roster/home/ references owntracks.

findings.title: The energy digest hardcodes TLS verification off, silently overriding owner config
findings.detail: `_fetch_weekly_statistics` constructs `HAStatisticsClient(..., verify_ssl=False)` as a literal (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:1412-1416), while the shared client's own default is `verify_ssl: bool = True` (src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant_statistics.py:89) and the owner-facing knob `HomeAssistantConfig.verify_ssl` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:170) is never consulted on this path. An owner running HA over HTTPS who sets `verify_ssl = true` in `[modules.home_assistant]` gets it honored by the module's REST and WebSocket clients (lines 346, 810) and silently ignored by the weekly energy job.

moves.title: `home.observations` — a butler-owned perception ledger for the house, sourced from the connector's durable history
moves.why: Vision non-negotiable #4 ('the daemon is deterministic infrastructure') and the anti-pattern 'designing features that require an always-on internet connection to function at the daemon level' both argue the house's past should live in the butler's own schema, not behind a live call to a hub that may be down. Today it does not: `ha_entity_snapshot` overwrites in place (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:2079) and all history is a live recorder call degrading to `available: False` (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:1389-1430), while `connectors.home_assistant_history` already retains every state change with attributes indefinitely (alembic/versions/core/core_084_home_assistant_history.py:7-19) and butler roles already hold SELECT on that schema (scripts/init-db.sql:420-426) — a primitive built once and generalized to exactly one consumer, the chronicler. Owner payoff: 'has the study been colder than usual this month' and 'what did the dryer draw last winter' become answerable offline, and the daily environment report stops silently depending on HA being reachable. Serves the home manifesto's 'Ask about your home', 'Get daily environment reports', and 'Track energy consumption' promises; the Chronicler manifesto benefits downstream from the same rollups.
moves.integration_points: New migration roster/home/migrations/002_home_observations.py adding `home.observations` (entity_id, space_id, metric, value_num, value_text, unit, observed_at from HA `last_updated`, ingested_at, source) and `home.observation_rollups` (entity_id, bucket_start, period, min/max/mean/last/sample_count). New deterministic job `butlers.jobs.home.run_observation_rollup` registered in `_DETERMINISTIC_SCHEDULE_JOB_REGISTRY['home']` (src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py:1317-1424), reading `connectors.home_assistant_history` on a (recorded_at, id) tuple watermark in cursor_store. New `home.ha_source_health` recording `last_ha_contact_at` distinct from `captured_at`, written only on a real HA read (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:947-1033 WS path, 1331-1356 REST seed), consumed by `/api/home/snapshot-status` (roster/home/api/router.py:315) and by a new freshness guard in `_read_entity_snapshot` (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:168). New spec openspec/specs/home-observation-ledger/spec.md plus an amendment to openspec/specs/butler-home/spec.md:120 which currently mandates live-state-cache-only. The cross-schema read is already sanctioned by init-db.sql's connector-read grant; document it against RFC 0010 guardrails.
moves.slice_plan: 1) `ha_source_health` + freshness guard so staleness stops impersonating currency before any new storage lands (fixes finding 2 on its own). 2) `home.observations` writer job with watermark plus backfill from existing history. 3) hourly/daily rollups; repoint `run_environment_report` trend text at rollups. 4) repoint `_fetch_weekly_statistics` at rollups with a live-HA reconciliation check so the digest survives an HA outage.

moves.title: Spaces: make rooms and devices first-class entities the whole fleet can name
moves.why: The identity model (docs/concepts/identity-model.md; `public.entities` with entity_type IN ('person','organization','place','other'), alembic/versions/core/core_002_identity.py:86-95) already has a `place` type and nothing in the house uses it. Rooms exist only as an in-memory `_area_cache` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:227) and a denormalized `area_name` string merged into snapshot JSONB (line 2058), so 'the study' in a home memory fact, 'the study' in a chronicler presence episode, and 'the study' in a calendar location are three unrelated strings — a primitive built once and generalized nowhere, in the one domain where physical location is the natural join key. Owner payoff: 'is the study warm enough for my 3pm call' resolves calendar + climate + occupancy against one identity, and 'the bedroom sensor' means the same device to home, chronicler, and health. Serves the home manifesto's room-scoped Comfort Management promise; extends the identity-model doc rather than amending any manifesto.
moves.integration_points: New tables in roster/home/migrations/002_*: `home.spaces` (space_id, entity_uuid FK to public.entities with entity_type='place', ha_area_id, floor, function, aliases) and `home.space_devices` (ha_entity_id, ha device_id, space_id, role ∈ sensor/actuator/presence, capabilities JSONB). Seeded by a new `home.sync_registries` deterministic job extending the module's area/entity registry fetches (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1358-1428) with HA's `config/device_registry/list`, resolving each area through the shared resolve-or-create entity resolver per the `butler-memory` shared skill. `/areas` (roster/home/api/router.py:208) becomes a table-backed spaces read instead of an in-memory cache read. Memory taxonomy amendment in roster/home/.claude/skills/memory-taxonomy so room facts carry the place entity id. New spec openspec/specs/home-spaces/spec.md; amend openspec/specs/module-home-assistant/spec.md:143 (Area and Entity Registry Cache) to make the persisted table the source of truth.
moves.slice_plan: 1) `home.spaces` + registry sync + entity resolution, no consumer changes. 2) `home.space_devices` with device-level grouping so 'the bedroom sensor' is one device, not five entities. 3) repoint `/areas`, `_discover_areas_and_sensors` (src/butlers/jobs/home.py:1053) and comfort-preference loading (line 1129) onto spaces. 4) stamp space_id on observations and on the actuation receipt.

moves.title: Owner-scoped, room-resolved presence with arrival lead time
moves.why: The north star forbids fabrication and stale authority; today `at_home` is asserted by any person entity reading `home` on a writer-clock freshness check (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:184-199), a fabricated owner signal read fleet-wide as ground truth for quiet hours and insight delivery. Meanwhile `away` and `commuting` are declared vocabulary with no producer (src/butlers/context_bus.py:31-33) and the provider catalogue advertises owntracks × home 'Location tracking' (alembic/versions/core/core_107_provider_feature_catalogue.py:183-184) against `connectors.owntracks_points` (core_081) that home never opens. Owner payoff: the manifesto's flagship line — 'When you walk into a room, it's already adjusted to your liking' — becomes possible for the first time, because the butler knows which room, and knows you are eight minutes out rather than merely absent. Serves the home manifesto's Comfort Management promise; the room signal also lets messenger and the insight broker pick a room-appropriate moment.
moves.integration_points: Rewrite `run_home_presence_context_producer` (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:203) to (a) resolve presence entities to the owner via `connectors.home_assistant_persons.ha_entity_id`, the key src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/home_assistant.py:40-42 already uses, refusing to assert on unresolved entities; (b) evaluate freshness on HA-reported `last_updated`, not `captured_at`; (c) publish `away` on fresh not-home, and `commuting` with an ETA in metadata derived from `connectors.owntracks_points` region transitions. New `home.occupancy` producer publishing a new `ContextSignal.in_space` (value = space_id) from binary_sensor motion/occupancy/mmWave entities bound through `home.space_devices`, with a per-space decay window and an explicit unknown. Requires extending `ContextSignal` (src/butlers/context_bus.py:21) and openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md; new schedule entry in roster/home/butler.toml beside `context_producer_home_presence` (line 92).
moves.slice_plan: 1) owner scoping + HA-clock freshness on the existing producer (pure honesty fix, no new signal). 2) publish `away` explicitly instead of only clearing `at_home`. 3) `in_space` occupancy producer over `home.space_devices`. 4) OwnTracks-derived `commuting` + arrival ETA; rewire the existing `atmosphere_preconditioning` job (roster/home/butler.toml:77-81) to fire on approach rather than on a 3-hourly cron.

moves.title: The physical consequence gate: a declared risk map, a real approval spine, and an actuation receipt
moves.why: Doctrine rule #6 makes the manifesto binding, and the home manifesto twice promises confirmation before consequential physical action ('Arm/disarm automations require explicit user confirmation'; 'We ask for confirmation before destructive actions'). Enforcement today is prose in roster/home/AGENTS.md while `[modules.approvals]` is loaded and never enabled (roster/home/butler.toml:38; src/butlers/config.py:526) — so a memory reclassification is gated (roster/relationship/butler.toml:168) and unlocking the front door is not. The receipt is equally broken: ha_command_log has no actor, session, request, or status column (roster/home/migrations/001_home_tables.py:88-99) and writes failures into the same `result` column as successes (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1922), so /command-log cannot tell the owner who acted or whether it worked. Owner payoff: the house cannot be opened, disarmed, or shut down without a door the owner walks through, and every physical action is traceable back to the signal that caused it. Serves the home manifesto's stated safety character; no amendment needed — this is the manifesto finally being enforced.
moves.integration_points: New seeded table `home.actuation_risk` (domain, service, target_pattern, risk_tier, rationale) with defaults marking lock.unlock, alarm_control_panel.*, cover.open_cover on garage-class targets, climate.set_temperature beyond declared safety bounds, and switch.turn_off on freezer/medical-class devices as always-require; consumed by `[modules.approvals] enabled = true` plus `[modules.approvals.gated_tools.ha_call_service]` in roster/home/butler.toml:38, matched by the existing pattern-constraint engine (src/butlers/modules/approvals/rules.py:41-98) over the already-declared arg_sensitivities (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:266). Migration adds session_id, request_id, approval_id, status, space_id, verified_at, verified_state to ha_command_log; `_log_command` (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1881) takes them from the ambient request context. New roster/home/domain_events.toml — the file does not exist, only finance, health, travel have one — declaring `home.actuation_executed` and `home.safety_condition` with permitted_subscribers and minimized payloads per src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py. Amend openspec/specs/module-home-assistant/spec.md:271 (Control Tool) and :309 (Command Audit Logging); amend openspec/specs/butler-home/spec.md:58.

audits.ideal: The Finance butler is the fleet's single source of monetary truth: every dollar the owner will pay, has paid, or is owed enters through one ingestion spine (email receipts, owner-controlled read-only bank feeds, owner-supplied statement documents, and cost claims declared by sibling butlers on the domain-event bus), lands in one currency-honest ledger where no aggregate ever blends units or launders a stale balance into a current-looking total, and leaves through one forward-obligation ledger where every recurring commitment carries its own cancellation door — a dated deadline the owner can act on before the charge, not a digest bullet after it. Statements verify ledger completeness so the butler can say "I have all of it" or name exactly what is missing rather than implying coverage it does not have. Income is modelled as streams rather than inferred from undifferentiated credits, so the headline number is forward-looking safe-to-spend rather than backward-looking monthly spend. Every consequential money action — a purchase, a cancellation, a payment — is a proposal carried on the existing approvals spine with envelope headroom stated, evidence cited, and a one-tap door; the butler holds no credential capable of moving money unless the owner has separately and explicitly granted one, and that grant is a decision, never a default.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today Finance is a strong retrospective reader and a weak forward actor, and several of its headline numbers are not honest. Ingestion is real and multi-source (email receipts, a read-only SimpleFIN bridge with genuine per-account freshness classification in roster/finance/tools/feed_reconciliation.py, CSV import via the blob store), and the deterministic job architecture — insight-scan, bill-reconciliation-sweep, anomaly-insight-scan, monthly-finance-digest, all proposing through the insight broker — is exactly right. But the aggregates on top of that ingestion fabricate: spending_summary and the dashboard endpoint sum amounts across currencies and stamp the result with the modal or MAX() ISO code (roster/finance/api/router.py:552), net_worth_history sums balances across currencies into a total with no currency at all, and cash_flow counts every credit as income and every debit as expense with no transfer exclusion, so an own-account transfer inflates both sides and the derived savings_rate. The per-account staleness the butler already computes is never selected by the accounts endpoint, so the dashboard renders a never-synced account identically to a fresh one. Forward-looking mechanism is thin: price changes are only detected after the charge posts, subscriptions carry no cancellation URL, notice period, or cancel-by date, so the manifesto's promise never to let a subscription renew without warning is met only by an LLM-written calendar reminder. There is no statement ingestion and therefore no completeness check — the butler cannot distinguish "you spent nothing on dining" from "I never saw your dining transactions." And the rest of the fleet's money is invisible: Travel books trips with no cost on the bus, Relationship keeps a real loans ledger in its own schema, and Finance's only domain_events.toml declaration is one outbound budget-pressure advisory. Nothing in the repo executes or even proposes a purchase.

findings.title: Mixed-currency spend totals stamped with a fabricated currency label
findings.detail: The dashboard endpoint computes the currency of a mixed-currency sum as COALESCE(MAX(t.currency),'USD') — the lexicographically largest ISO code among matching rows — and the MCP tool uses the modal currency over an unconditioned SUM(amount). Neither restricts the SUM to one currency. An owner holding SGD and USD accounts (the AGENTS.md guidance references GIRO/CPF, so this is the live case) gets a unit-less sum presented under an authoritative three-letter code. The butler's own budget_status does this correctly — it filters spend by the budget's currency — so the two surfaces disagree by construction, and the frontend renders the endpoint's label through Intl.NumberFormat, giving the fabricated figure a currency symbol.

findings.title: cash_flow treats own-account transfers as income and expense, inflating savings_rate
findings.detail: cash_flow aggregates income as SUM(amount) FILTER (direction='credit') and expenses as the debit equivalent, with no exclusion of the 'transfer' or 'uncategorized' categories — while spending_summary explicitly excludes both, with a comment stating transfers move money between the owner's own accounts and are not real spend (~$11k in live data per the router comment). A single savings-to-checking transfer therefore appears as income on one leg and expense on the other, and savings_rate = (income - expenses)/income is computed off the inflated denominator. The category breakdown path repeats the same aggregation. Cross-currency blending applies here too.

findings.title: net_worth totals sum balances across currencies and carry no currency field
findings.detail: net_worth_history accumulates total_assets/total_liabilities by adding each account's balance regardless of its currency, and the returned period object exposes net_worth, total_assets and total_liabilities as bare strings with no currency key — the per-account entries keep their currency, the totals discard it. A SGD checking balance and a USD brokerage balance are added into one number that denominates nothing.

findings.title: Per-account feed staleness is computed but never reaches the dashboard
findings.detail: Migration 012 added accounts.last_synced_at and account_feed_freshness() classifies every account as degraded with reason never_synced or stale, deliberately refusing to fabricate health from an absent timestamp. GET /finance/accounts selects institution, type, name, last_four, currency, metadata and timestamps — but not last_synced_at — and AccountModel has no field for it, so the Accounts panel renders an account whose feed died three weeks ago identically to one synced this morning, under a copy line inviting the owner to connect an account 'to see net-worth context'. Computed-then-discarded truth, and staleness wearing current-data authority on the one surface the owner actually looks at.

findings.title: No pre-renewal cancellation door — price changes are only detectable after the charge posts
findings.detail: The manifesto promises 'We will never let a subscription renew without warning you first.' detect_price_changes compares transaction amounts already posted against the tracked subscription amount and flags >5% moves, i.e. the owner is told after paying the new price. finance.subscriptions has no cancellation_url, notice_period_days, or cancel_by column, so even when a renewal is known there is no door to act on — only an LLM-written calendar reminder 7 days out, per the AGENTS.md calendar contract. The temporal group already exposes deadline_create with alert thresholds, and nothing in finance uses it for renewal windows.
findings.evidence: roster/finance/tools/alerts.py:334-356; roster/finance/migrations/001_finance_tables.py:110-127; roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md:20; roster/finance/AGENTS.md (Calendar Usage, subscription reminder rule); openspec/specs/deadline-tracking/spec.md

findings.title: Net-worth period totals carry no aggregate carry-forward marker
findings.detail: net_worth_history marks carried_forward per account entry but the period-level total_assets/total_liabilities/net_worth expose no indication of how much of the total is observed versus carried forward from an earlier month. A net-worth line composed entirely of balances last observed eight months ago renders identically to one taken today.

findings.title: Relationship keeps a real money ledger Finance cannot see, and no cost contract exists on the bus
findings.detail: relationship.loans stores amount, direction (lent/borrowed) and settled state — genuine owner-facing money obligations living in another butler's schema, unreachable by Finance under the MCP-only rule and undeclared on the domain-event bus. Finance's domain_events.toml declares exactly one event (finance.budget_pressure, outbound, minimized) and no inbound cost or obligation contract; travel.trip_booked carries trip identifiers and dates with no amount, so Finance's documented reaction is to guess a travel budget rather than record a known booked cost.

moves.why: Vision non-negotiable 'nothing fabricated' and the north-star clause that failure never impersonates health: today spending_summary, the /spending-summary endpoint, net_worth_history and cash_flow all emit blended-unit numbers under a single authoritative currency label (router.py:552 literally uses MAX of the ISO code string), while budget_status alone gets it right — so the butler contradicts itself. moves.title: Statement ingestion with ledger-completeness verification
moves.why: The strongest anti-fabrication guarantee a personal finance system can offer is knowing whether it has everything. Today the butler cannot distinguish 'you spent nothing on dining' from 'I never saw your dining transactions' — feed_reconciliation.py honestly reports never_synced, but nothing verifies that the transactions it does hold are complete for a period. Bank/card statements state opening balance, closing balance and a full line-item set for an exact window; ingesting them turns the ledger into a checkable claim ('March: statement closes at 4,182.30; my ledger reconstructs 3,905.10 — 11 transactions totalling 277.20 are missing') and simultaneously feeds balance_snapshots from evidence instead of manual net_worth_snapshot calls. Owner payoff: net worth and spend totals stop depending on the owner remembering to type balances in. Serves the Finance manifesto's 'reconcile the evidence' promise and 'organized and searchable, not lost'; sovereignty-clean because the statement is a file the owner already has.

New roster/finance/tools/statements.py exposing ingest_statement(storage_ref, account_id) and verify_period_completeness(account_id, period), registered via roster/finance/modules/tools.py under a new 'statements' group added to [modules.finance] groups in roster/finance/butler.toml. Extraction reuses the blob-store path proven in roster/finance/tools/data_import.py:469-475 and the LLM-driven shape of the transaction-csv-extraction skill (new statement-extraction skill) — not module-document-renderer, which is render-only (openspec/specs/module-document-renderer). Completeness adds a third arm to roster/finance/tools/feed_reconciliation.py (email vs feed vs statement) and writes balance_snapshots with source='statement' so overview.py net worth stops relying on manual snapshots. A completeness gap becomes an owner condition through the existing finance condition reconciler (roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py:752) so it is a door, not a digest line. AGENTS.md trap: schema changes need both the migration and the inline DDL in roster/finance/tests/test_integration.py. New spec openspec/specs/finance-statement-ingestion.

moves.title: Income streams and a safe-to-spend headline
moves.why: cash_flow infers income from undifferentiated credits (overview.py:525), so refunds, own-account transfers and salary are one bucket and savings_rate is derived from it — the butler has no model of income at all. The single most owner-legible number in personal finance is not 'monthly spend' (the current KPI) but 'what is safe to spend before the next payday, after everything already committed'. Serves the Finance manifesto's 'know what is coming up' and 'the foundation of feeling in control of your money'; the manifesto's framing is mostly retrospective ('where your money went'), so this implies a light amendment adding a forward-looking cashflow clause to Our Promise.

Run 09's theme 'primitives built once and generalized nowhere' applies: the domain-event bus with publisher-owned contracts, minimized payloads and reaction receipts exists and is used for exactly three events. moves.title: Spend envelopes and envelope-gated purchase proposals (execution decision-gated)
moves.why: The pursuit question asks about purchase execution under autonomy envelopes, and the honest answer is that Finance must never hold a credential capable of moving money without a separate explicit owner decision — the manifesto's scope discipline currently forbids payment initiation outright (roster/finance/AGENTS.md 'Scope discipline'), so execution requires a manifesto amendment plus owner signoff and is out of scope until both exist. What is buildable now and genuinely valuable is the envelope as a ceiling on proposals: the butler assembles the complete purchase — merchant, item, price, price history from its own transaction ledger, and envelope headroom remaining after — and hands the owner a one-tap door on the approvals spine that the owner executes. Owner payoff: the recurring 'should I rebuy this / is this a good price / can I afford it this month' loop collapses into approve/decline. Serves the Finance manifesto's control-and-awareness thesis; execution would require amending both Our Promise and the AGENTS.md scope-discipline clause, which this move deliberately does not do. Distinct from run 09's 'spend ceiling edit consequence gate', which governs LLM API spend in public.token_usage_ledger, not owner money.
moves.integration_points: Migration creating finance.spend_envelopes (name, category, period, ceiling_amount, currency, per_transaction_cap, merchant_allowlist TEXT[], is_active) — deliberately shaped so it can later project into a standing approval rule for the approvals module (src/butlers/modules/approvals/rules.py) if and only if the owner grants execution. Near-term consumers: a new propose_purchase tool registered under a 'commerce' group in roster/finance/modules/tools.py that parks a PendingAction through src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py with the advertised why/evidence contract from roster/shared/AGENTS.md, evidence citing the owner's own prior transactions for that merchant; headroom checks read against the move-1 currency-honest aggregates. Renders in the existing approvals/decisions surfaces (openspec/specs/dashboard-approvals, dashboard-decisions) — no new page. New spec openspec/specs/finance-spend-envelopes carrying an explicit non-requirement: the butler stores no payment credential and initiates no money movement.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: spend_envelopes table + headroom read surfaced in budget_status and the dashboard, no proposals. Slice 2: propose_purchase parking an approval-gated proposal with evidence and post-approval headroom stated; the owner executes the purchase themselves and the resulting transaction reconciles against the proposal. Slice 3 (BLOCKED on explicit owner decision + manifesto amendment): any credential-holding execution path — file the decision, do not build it.

moves.title: Return and warranty windows as doors on every receipt
moves.why: Every receipt the butler already reads carries two dates the owner never gets told about: the last day to return the item and the day the warranty expires. The butler stores receipt_url and rich metadata on finance.transactions and has the temporal deadline machinery in its core groups, and does nothing with either. Owner payoff: 'the monitor you bought on the 3rd is returnable until Saturday' and 'this laptop's warranty ends in 30 days' — pure absorbed mental labour, exactly the Finance manifesto's 'awareness without the work', at the smallest cost of any move here. Serves the Finance manifesto; no amendment needed (it is receipt reading, not commerce).
moves.integration_points: Columns return_by DATE and warranty_until DATE on finance.transactions (or a typed metadata contract validated in roster/finance/tools/transactions.py record_transaction, avoiding the AGENTS.md anti-pattern of state-in-prose-JSONB). Extraction guidance in roster/finance/AGENTS.md's ambiguity-handling section and the interactive-response skill. Each populated date registers through deadline_create (temporal core group, openspec/specs/deadline-tracking) with a single threshold so the alert rides the existing scheduler, and a merchant-level default return window can be learned into finance.merchant_mappings alongside category mappings. Surfaces as an 'Open windows' strip on ButlerFinanceFinancesTab. Spec: scenarios under openspec/specs/finance-transaction-schema and openspec/specs/finance-alerts.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: columns + record_transaction acceptance + deadline registration when a date is explicitly present in the receipt. Slice 2: merchant-level default return windows learned from confirmed cases. Slice 3: dashboard strip.
