audits.ideal: A butler that fails the same way twice should be the first thing that notices. The ideal is a three-layer loop with one spine. **Layer 1 — deterministic friction ledger:** the daemon (never an LLM, vision.md:80-84) derives typed friction episodes at `session_complete` from signals it already computes and currently throws away — guardrail terminations (`degenerate_tool_loop`, `tool_call_budget_exceeded`, `token_budget_exceeded`), recovered tool-call errors, timeouts, classification fallbacks, corrections targeting my sessions, `cannot_answer` delegations, and effect-free scheduled runs — each row carrying the session ids that are its evidence cohort, so every later claim is a door onto real sessions. **Layer 2 — butler-authored retrospective:** each butler runs an infrequent, precondition-gated retrospective session (spawn only when N episodes accumulated; capped spend) that reads *its own* ledger, clusters it, and writes typed **amendment proposals** — never edits. A proposal names one target (`system_prompt` / `skill` / `schedule` / `tool_surface` / `model_tier` / `ingestion_rule` / `approval_rule` / `manifesto`), the friction it claims to remove, the evidence cohort, the predicted effect, and a reversal plan. Butlers propose only about themselves; friction whose cause lives in another agent is relayed through the Switchboard as a proposal *addressed to* that agent (vision.md:71-78), respecting manifesto ownership. **Layer 3 — two adoption gates, split by what doctrine says the artifact is (vision.md:88-101):** operational tuning (DB-owned schedule rows, `runtime_config.core_groups`, tier, rules) adopts in one owner click with a ledgered before/after; identity (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, MANIFESTO.md, butler.toml) can only be adopted by rendering a pull request through the existing healing worktree/anonymizer/PR machinery — a runtime never writes a git-tracked identity file, and merge is the gate. Every adoption then carries a measurement window and a computed verdict (improved / no-change / regressed) from the same ledger, with a revert door: an adopted amendment that did not reduce its cited friction says so, and no adoption ever wears the authority of a verified improvement.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has two working instances of exactly this loop and can generalize neither. `switchboard-rule-promotion` mines repeated LLM routing agreement into `pending_review` suggestions with a genuine evidence-quality gate (openspec/specs/switchboard-rule-promotion/spec.md:8-90), and `autonomy-suggestions` mines repeated manual approvals into `pending` promotion/demotion suggestions (src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_suggestions.py:79-261) — same lifecycle, two tables, two status vocabularies, two APIs, two dashboards, and neither can carry a proposal about a prompt, a skill, a schedule, or a tool surface. Everything else in the loop is missing or hollow. The richest behavioral-friction signals the system computes are deliberately discarded by their only consumer: `_NON_ACTIONABLE_GUARDRAIL_MARKERS` drops degenerate loops and blown budgets from QA discovery as "policy stops, not product crashes" (src/butlers/core/qa/sources/session_records.py:67-75) and drops switchboard classification timeouts with a comment deferring to "switchboard routing telemetry" that turns out to be a bare OTel counter with no evidence link (session_records.py:77-88; src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:3604; roster/switchboard/tools/routing/telemetry.py:91) — correct triage, no second destination. A butler's own introspection surface is cost-shaped: `sessions_summary` aggregates tokens only and `top_sessions` ranks by tokens, though `success` and `error` sit in the same rows (src/butlers/core/sessions.py:714-780, 862-900; src/butlers/core_tools/_sessions.py:69-89). The declared self-learning channel is dead: the spec asserts runtime instances write AGENTS.md notes (openspec/specs/core-skills/spec.md:96), the writers have no callers (src/butlers/core/skills.py:275-287), and every `# Notes to self` section is empty. Meanwhile self-modification that *is* reachable is ungated: `schedule_create/update/delete` are ordinary butler-callable core tools writing `source='db'` rows the TOML sync will not reclaim (src/butlers/core_tools/_scheduling.py:60-220; src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:687-689) while sending an emoji is approval-gated (roster/messenger/butler.toml:83). QA covers crashes and produces code PRs by contract (roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md § Purpose/Non-Responsibilities); nothing in the fleet turns "I keep struggling here" into "here is the amendment I propose, and here is the evidence."

findings.title: The three richest behavioral-friction signals are computed, marked non-actionable, and routed nowhere
findings.detail: The spawner terminates sessions on `degenerate_tool_loop`, `tool_call_budget_exceeded`, and `token_budget_exceeded` and stamps a stable marker into `sessions.error` (spawner_guardrails.py:35-91; core-sessions spec § Guardrail Termination Error Markers). The only consumer, QA session-records discovery, correctly excludes them — "intentional policy stops, not product crashes" — and there is no second destination: no aggregate, no per-butler view, no proposal producer. Same for switchboard classification timeouts, dropped with a comment deferring to "switchboard routing telemetry", which is an OTel counter (`butlers.switchboard.fallback_to_general`) carrying no session ids, so no one can walk from the number to the sessions that made it. A butler that loops on the same tool every morning generates a perfect, typed, deduplicated signal that literally nothing reads.

findings.title: A butler's self-observation surface is cost-only: success and error are stored but never aggregated
findings.detail: `sessions_summary(period)` returns total sessions and four token counters grouped by model — no success count, no failure count, no error taxonomy — and `top_sessions` ranks by input+output tokens. Both are registered into the `sessions` core group that domain butlers carry by default. `sessions.success` and `sessions.error` are written on every completion and exposed row-by-row via `sessions_list`, so the data exists; the aggregate a butler would need to notice its own failure profile is the one aggregate never built. A butler asked "how am I doing?" can only answer "how much did I spend?".

findings.title: The spec-declared runtime self-note channel does not exist: AGENTS.md writers have no callers and every "Notes to self" section is empty
findings.detail: core-skills asserts `write_agents_md` / `append_agents_md` "are used by runtime instances for runtime agent notes", and butler-base-spec requires AGENTS.md to carry "a `# Notes to self` section for runtime agent notes". Neither writer is called anywhere in src/ or roster/ — the only occurrences are the definitions themselves. Consequently every butler's `# Notes to self` heading is an empty trailer, except switchboard's, which a human wrote by hand. The spec asserts a capability the code cannot perform, and the one place doctrine reserved for a butler's accumulated self-knowledge has been empty since it was reserved. (Note also that a live runtime write here would violate vision.md rule 5: AGENTS.md is git-tracked identity, not operational tuning — so the fix is a gated proposal path, not wiring the writers up.)
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/core-skills/spec.md:96; src/butlers/core/skills.py:267-287; openspec/specs/butler-base-spec/spec.md § AGENTS.md Content Principles; roster/health/AGENTS.md:125; roster/general/AGENTS.md:75; roster/lifestyle/AGENTS.md:139; roster/switchboard/AGENTS.md:30-32

findings.title: Two independent evidence→proposal→owner-decision spines with divergent vocabularies and neither extensible
findings.detail: Switchboard rule promotion writes `pending_review` suggestions into its own table with its own confirm/dismiss API, and approvals autonomy writes `pending` promotion/demotion suggestions into another table with another confirm/dismiss/supersede API and its own dashboard payloads. Both implement the identical lifecycle — mine repeated evidence, propose, human confirms or dismisses with cooldown, supersede on manual equivalent — and disagree on the very first status name. Both are hard-bound to one target type (an ingestion rule; an approval rule), so there is nowhere to put a proposal whose target is a prompt, a skill, a schedule, a tool group, or a model tier. This is the primitive built twice and generalized zero times.

findings.title: Butlers can rewrite their own operating cadence with no approval gate and no proposal record
findings.detail: `schedule_create`, `schedule_update`, and `schedule_delete` are ordinary butler-callable core tools in the `scheduling` group, enabled by default and explicitly seeded on domain butlers. A runtime-created task lands with `source='db'`, which the TOML sync deliberately does not reclaim, so a self-created schedule survives every restart and every git-config sync. Creating a recurring schedule creates recurring LLM spend and recurring owner-facing notifications — as consequential as any gated action — yet no butler gates the scheduling tools, while `telegram_react_to_message` (sending an emoji) is approval-gated on messenger. The one self-modification butlers *can* already perform is the one with no owner in the loop.

findings.title: The agent-side reporting channel is exception-shaped, so missing-affordance friction has no honest encoding
findings.detail: `report_error(error_type, error_message, traceback, call_site, tool_name, severity_hint)` is the only way a butler session can tell the ecosystem something went wrong, and every field presumes a thrown exception; the QA sources it feeds reconstruct an exception-type/call-site fingerprint from that shape. A butler that concludes "there is no tool for what the owner asked", "the skill documents a parameter the tool does not accept", or "the owner has now rephrased this three times" can only report it by fabricating an exception, which would poison the fingerprint space the crash pipeline depends on. So the highest-value diagnosis — the one only the reasoning session can make — has no channel at all.

findings.title: No dead-end classification for butler sessions, though QA already implements the concept for its own agents
findings.detail: QA detects when an investigation agent produced no commits (`_detect_no_op_branch` → `no_op_branch` error detail) and refuses to open an empty PR — the system knows how to name "ran and did nothing". Nothing applies that concept to butler sessions: a scheduled task that completes `success=true` with zero effect-producing tool calls and no `notify` is indistinguishable in every ledger, dashboard, and aggregate from one that did real work. That is the failure mode a daily schedule can repeat for months while the fleet reports green — precisely the north star's "failure never impersonates health".

moves.title: Friction ledger: typed self-observation episodes derived deterministically at session close
moves.why: vision.md:80-84 (the daemon is deterministic infrastructure; intelligence is in ephemeral sessions) says the *detection* half of a self-improvement loop must be daemon-side and testable, not an LLM guess. Today the detection half exists as discarded facts: guardrail markers dropped at qa/sources/session_records.py:67-75, classification timeouts dropped at :77-88, recovered tool errors visible only to QA's crash pipeline, corrections stored but aggregated nowhere. Owner payoff: the fleet's own recurring failure modes become countable and evidence-linked, so any later claim ("this butler struggles with X") opens onto the exact sessions that prove it — the unbroken signal→session→evidence spine, applied to the fleet's own behavior for the first time. Serves every domain manifesto by keeping each butler's promise auditable; serves roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md by giving the behavioral half of quality a home outside the code-fix pipeline that correctly refuses it.
moves.integration_points: New core Alembic migration adding `{schema}.session_friction` (id, session_id FK, episode_kind, subject — tool/schedule/route/skill name, detail JSONB, occurred_at, request_id); derivation hook in `src/butlers/core/sessions.py::session_complete` (line 232ff) reading the same `error` markers `failover_classifier.py:268` matches and the `outcome='error'` elements `tool_call_capture.py:198-226` already records; episode kinds: `guardrail_loop`, `guardrail_budget`, `tool_error_recovered`, `timeout`, `classification_fallback`, `correction_target`, `delegation_cannot_answer`, `effect_free_run`. New spec `openspec/specs/core-friction-ledger/spec.md` (sibling of core-sessions). Consumes the filed turn-closure ledger for repeated-clarification episodes rather than re-deriving them. Read path for QA stays the sanctioned-view pattern of `alembic/versions/core/core_055_v_qa_recent_failures.py` (add `public.v_fleet_friction`).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Migration + `friction_record()` writer with the four purely-mechanical kinds (guardrail_loop, guardrail_budget, timeout, tool_error_recovered) derived from data `session_complete` already holds; contract tests assert one episode per marker and zero for clean sessions. 2) `effect_free_run` classifier (success=true, no effect-producing tool call, no notify) reusing the no-op concept QA already implements at qa/dispatch.py:731. 3) `classification_fallback` + `correction_target` + `delegation_cannot_answer` producers at their existing call sites. 4) Public read view + 30-day retention job mirroring the QA evidence-retention clock in roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md § Retention Policy.

moves.title: Outcome-carrying self-observation: make a butler able to see its own failures, not just its spend
moves.why: `sessions_summary` returns tokens only and `top_sessions` ranks by tokens, while `success` and `error` sit unaggregated in the same rows — computed-then-discarded truth at the exact surface a butler would use to examine itself (core/sessions.py:714-780, 862-900). Owner payoff: the cheapest possible fix to the deepest gap — a butler asked "how are you doing?" can answer with failure counts, top friction subjects, and the sessions behind them instead of a token bill, and the daily-briefing and check-in flows every manifesto promises can finally admit "I failed at this twice this week". Serves all twelve manifestos (each promises honest reporting in its domain); no amendment needed — it widens an existing core group rather than adding scope.
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/core/sessions.py`: extend `sessions_summary` with `succeeded`/`failed`/`by_error_marker` counts (same query, added aggregates) and add `sessions_friction(period, limit)` returning grouped `session_friction` rows with their evidence session ids; register both under the existing `sessions` core group in `src/butlers/core_tools/_sessions.py:69-89` so no butler.toml change is required (roster/finance/butler.toml:14 already enables it). Amend `openspec/specs/core-sessions/spec.md` with a Session Outcome Summary requirement. Dashboard Sessions read model `src/butlers/api/read_models/sessions_v1.py` gets the same fields so operator and butler see one number.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the outcome aggregates to `sessions_summary` + spec requirement + test that a period with one failed session reports `failed=1` (today it reports only tokens). 2) Add `sessions_friction` over the ledger from move 1, gated behind ledger presence with an explicit `unavailable` reason rather than an empty list. 3) Wire the same fields into the dashboard sessions read model so the operator surface and the butler's self-view cannot disagree.

moves.title: One improvement-proposal spine: collapse the two suggestion pipelines into a typed, target-agnostic proposal object
moves.why: The fleet has built this lifecycle twice and generalized it zero times — switchboard rule promotion (`pending_review`) and approvals autonomy (`pending`) share evidence-mining, confirm/dismiss-with-cooldown, and supersede-on-manual-equivalent, disagree on the first status name, and neither can hold a proposal whose target is a prompt, skill, schedule, tool group, or tier. vision.md:103-111 (rule 6) makes every governing document binding and amendable — so an amendment needs a first-class object with evidence, not a bespoke table per target type. Owner payoff: one place where everything the fleet wants to change about itself is queued, ranked, and decided, each row a door onto the friction that motivated it and the sessions that prove the friction. Serves roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md's operator-facing case-record philosophy generalized past crashes; feeds (does not duplicate) the Owner Decision Desk already filed as bu-ckkpz.
moves.integration_points: New `public.improvement_proposals` (id, proposing_agent, target_kind ∈ {system_prompt, skill, schedule, tool_surface, model_tier, ingestion_rule, approval_rule, manifesto}, target_ref, claim, proposed_change JSONB, evidence_cohort (friction episode ids + session ids), predicted_effect, reversal_plan, status ∈ {pending, adopted, dismissed, superseded}, cooldown_until, decided_at/by) + `public.improvement_proposal_events` journal mirroring `qa_investigation_events`. Migrate both producers: `roster/switchboard/tools/routing/rule_promotion.py`/`rule_promotion_apply.py` and `src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_suggestions.py` become `target_kind` producers; their specs (openspec/specs/switchboard-rule-promotion, autonomy-suggestions) get amended to reference the shared lifecycle; new `openspec/specs/improvement-proposals/spec.md` owns statuses and evidence-quality gates (reuse the 2-distinct-days + minimum-elapsed floor rule already ratified in switchboard-rule-promotion). API: one `/api/proposals` router replacing the two suggestion endpoints; `frontend/src/api/types.ts:3500,9623-9688` collapses to one payload family.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Table + spec + lifecycle library with the ratified evidence-quality gate, and the `improvement_proposals` API behind the existing dashboard conventions. 2) Port autonomy suggestions onto it as `target_kind='approval_rule'` (keeps its MCP tools, swaps the store); delete the module-local table in the same change. 3) Port switchboard rule promotion as `target_kind='ingestion_rule'`, unifying `pending_review`→`pending`. 4) Open the remaining target kinds for moves 4/5 to write into. 5) Retire the two bespoke dashboard surfaces in favor of one proposals lane that hands off to bu-ckkpz.

moves.title: propose_amendment: the git-gated channel for a butler to amend its own prompt, skill, or manifesto
moves.why: vision.md:88-101 (rule 5) makes identity git-owned and operational tuning DB-owned; vision.md:103-111 (rule 6) forbids capabilities that contradict the governing document without a formal amendment. Together those say a butler must never write its own AGENTS.md at runtime — and today's code agrees by accident: the AGENTS.md writers exist with no callers and every `# Notes to self` section is empty (skills.py:275-287; core-skills spec:96 asserts otherwise). The honest resolution is not to wire the writers up but to give amendment a gate: the butler writes a proposal, and *adoption* renders a pull request through the machinery QA already owns. Owner payoff: a butler that has learned something durable about its domain can finally say so, in a reviewable diff, with the sessions that taught it attached — and the owner keeps the merge seat, exactly as with QA fixes. Serves every butler's own MANIFESTO.md as the amendment mechanism rule 6 requires; requires a roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md contract amendment naming a second PR class (`butler-amendment`) alongside `self-healing`.
moves.integration_points: New core tool `propose_amendment(target_kind, target_ref, claim, proposed_diff, evidence_session_ids, reversal_plan)` in a new `src/butlers/core_tools/_improvement.py` under a new `improvement` core group (default-on for butlers, off for staffers), writing to `public.improvement_proposals` from move 3 — writes a row, never a file. Adoption path reuses `src/butlers/core/healing/worktree.py`, `anonymizer.py`, and `src/butlers/core/qa/github_pr.py` with label `butler-amendment`; the whitelist gate at `src/butlers/core/qa/repo_whitelist.py` applies unchanged. Delete `write_agents_md`/`append_agents_md` (skills.py:275-287) and correct openspec/specs/core-skills/spec.md:96 to describe the proposal path — a spec that asserts an unimplementable behavior is worse than silence. Targets: `roster/{butler}/AGENTS.md` (`# Notes to self`), `roster/{butler}/.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`, `roster/{butler}/butler.toml` schedules, `roster/{butler}/MANIFESTO.md`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Core tool + group + spec, writing proposals only; contract test asserts no filesystem write occurs anywhere in the path. 2) Adoption renderer producing a branch+PR for `target_kind='system_prompt'` (the `# Notes to self` section only, append-only, anonymized) — the narrowest possible first diff class. 3) Extend to `skill` and `schedule` (butler.toml) diffs. 4) `manifesto` last, and only with a proposal template that quotes the clause being amended and requires an explicit rule-6 justification field. 5) QA contract amendment + PR-label routing so amendment PRs never enter the crash-investigation dossier.

moves.title: The retrospective: a shared, precondition-gated skill and schedule that turns friction into proposals
moves.why: The ledger and the spine are inert without an author, and doctrine puts authorship in an ephemeral session, not the daemon (vision.md:80-84). It must also not become a new unmetered inference channel: the ideas ledger's parked "deterministic precondition gates on scheduled prompt tasks" entry is exactly the discipline this needs — spawn only when there is something to read. Owner payoff: the loop actually closes on a cadence, and it costs nothing on the weeks the fleet ran clean; the owner sees a small, ranked queue of "here is what I would change about myself and why" instead of a dashboard of raw error counts they must interpret. Serves every domain manifesto (the retrospective is scoped to the butler's own promises and refusals, and the skill instructs it to reject proposals outside its manifesto scope and relay those via move 7); adds one shared skill under roster/shared/skills, no manifesto amendment required.
moves.integration_points: New `roster/shared/skills/self-retrospective/SKILL.md` (referenced from `roster/shared/BUTLER_SKILLS.md`, which already lists the shared set) documenting the read→cluster→propose sequence, the at-most-K-proposals rule, and the manifesto-scope refusal test. New `[[butler.schedule]]` entry per butler (e.g. `0 6 * * 1`, complexity `reasoning`) in each `roster/{butler}/butler.toml`, with a deterministic precondition evaluated in `src/butlers/core/scheduler.py::tick` before dispatch — skip (and record the skip) unless unclustered friction episodes ≥ threshold since the last retrospective. Consumes `sessions_friction` (move 2), writes via `propose_amendment` (move 4). Spec: extend `openspec/specs/core-scheduler/`-adjacent behavior via a `precondition` field on `scheduled_tasks`, or the friction-ledger spec if scheduler change is deferred.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Skill + schedule on one butler (health or finance — both have rich skill trees and real recurring schedules) with the precondition evaluated inside the prompt path first, so no scheduler change is needed to prove value. 2) Promote the precondition to a deterministic `scheduled_tasks.precondition` gate so the skip costs zero tokens and is recorded as a skip, not a silent no-run. 3) Roll to the remaining domain butlers; switchboard and messenger get staffer-shaped variants scoped to their infrastructure contracts. 4) Add a per-retrospective spend cap and record the retrospective's own cost against the proposals it produced — the loop must be able to prove it pays for itself.

moves.title: Adoption verification and the revert door: an adopted amendment that did not help must say so
moves.why: The north star's "failure never impersonates health" and the run-09 theme "acceptance impersonating completion" both bite hardest here: a self-improvement loop whose adoptions are never measured degrades into a machine for accumulating unfalsifiable changes to its own prompts. The existing exemplars already gesture at this — autonomy suggestions create a *demotion* suggestion when an auto-approved action later fails (openspec/specs/autonomy-suggestions/spec.md § Demotion Suggestion on Execution Failure) — but that recovery instinct exists for exactly one target type and is not a measurement. Owner payoff: earned calm. Every adopted amendment carries a window and a verdict computed from the same friction ledger that justified it, so the owner can trust the loop's own claims and revert one in a click; nothing the fleet did to itself is un-undoable or unaudited. Serves roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md's evidence-and-counter-evidence discipline, generalized to behavioral change.
moves.integration_points: `public.improvement_proposals` gains `adopted_at`, `measurement_window`, `baseline_rate`, `observed_rate`, `verdict ∈ {improved, no_change, regressed, insufficient_evidence}`, `reverted_at`; a deterministic sweep job (sibling of `src/butlers/core/domain_event_reaction_sweep.py`) computes the verdict from `session_friction` counts for the cited `episode_kind`+`subject` over matched pre/post windows — never an LLM verdict. Revert door per target class: DB targets (schedule row, runtime_config core_groups, tier, rules) revert in place with a journal event; git targets open a revert PR through the move-4 renderer. Requirement lives in `openspec/specs/improvement-proposals/spec.md`; the `insufficient_evidence` verdict is mandatory when the window holds too few sessions — the spine must be able to say "I do not know yet" rather than default to success.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Schema + sweep computing verdicts for DB-target adoptions only (schedules and rules, where before/after is unambiguous); test that a window with too few sessions yields `insufficient_evidence`, never `improved`. 2) Revert door for DB targets + journal events. 3) Extend to git targets, anchoring the post-window to merge time rather than adoption time. 4) Surface the verdict on the proposal card so an adopted-but-unverified amendment never renders with the same authority as a verified one.

moves.title: report_friction and the cross-butler friction relay: name the gap you cannot fix yourself
moves.why: The most valuable diagnosis is the one only the reasoning session can make — "there is no tool for this", "the skill documents a parameter the tool rejects", "the owner has rephrased this three times" — and today the only channel is `report_error`, whose every field presumes a thrown exception and whose consumers fingerprint on exception type and call site (self_healing/__init__.py:293-333; qa/sources/tool_call_failures.py:20-60). Encoding friction as a fake exception would poison the crash pipeline. And when the cause lives elsewhere — a misroute, a `cannot_answer` delegation — vision.md:71-78 (rule 3) and rule 6's manifesto ownership forbid one butler editing another: the proposal must travel as a message through the Switchboard, addressed to the owning agent. Owner payoff: the gaps in the fleet's own tool surface and skills stop being invisible, and cross-butler friction produces a proposal on the right desk instead of dying as a shrug in a session transcript. Serves roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md § Butler-to-staffer routing (the relay is exactly the sanctioned channel) and each receiving butler's manifesto ownership of its own amendments.
moves.integration_points: New `report_friction(friction_kind, subject, narrative, blocked_outcome, suggested_affordance)` alongside `report_error` in `src/butlers/modules/self_healing/__init__.py`, writing a `session_friction` episode of kind `agent_reported` (move 1) rather than a QA finding — no fingerprint collision with the crash pipeline. Relay: when `subject` names another agent, the proposal is routed via the existing Switchboard `route()` → tool path (the same mechanism that carries `report_finding` today, roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md § Relay reception) into the target agent's `improvement_proposals` rows with `proposing_agent` preserved, so the receiving butler's own retrospective triages it. Skill text lands in `roster/shared/skills/self-retrospective/SKILL.md` and a short line in `roster/shared/BUTLER_SKILLS.md`. Note tool-surface proposals (`target_kind='tool_surface'`) hand off to the runtime tool-surface discovery epic bu-ondtw rather than duplicating its control plane.
moves.slice_plan: 1) `report_friction` + episode kind + spec requirement; contract test that it never produces a QA finding or an exception-shaped fingerprint. 2) Relay for the two well-typed cross-agent cases (misroute correction → switchboard; `cannot_answer` delegation → the asked butler), reusing the existing route path with no new channel. 3) Free-text friction feeds the retrospective's clustering input only — it must never auto-create a proposal without passing through the move-5 author and the move-3 evidence gate.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has an entity anchor (`public.entities`, core_002_identity.py:84) and every butler stamps entity links onto the shared discovery index — `public.memory_catalog.entity_id` / `object_entity_id` are written on every fact upsert (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:433-499, 2005-2033) and there is a partial B-tree index built explicitly "for entity-anchored lookups" (alembic/versions/core/core_009_memory_catalog.py:218-223). Nothing reads it: both catalog search paths build their WHERE from tenant_id/memory_type/sensitivity only (src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:830-863, 866-908). The one real relationship graph — `relationship.entity_facts` with `object_kind='entity'` — is granted to `butler_relationship_rw` alone (roster/relationship/migrations/013_relationship_facts.py:173-175) and is never projected anywhere, so no other butler can learn that a person is the owner's sister. The owner-facing consequence is visible on the page that promises the most: `/entities/:entityId` is mounted at fleet level in the shell (frontend/src/router-config.tsx:66,145) yet every hook resolves to `prefix="/api/relationship"` (roster/relationship/api/router.py:170); its one genuine cross-butler read, the chronicler episode merge, returns `[]` on any failure (roster/relationship/api/router.py:6398-6407) into a stream, a `total`, and a daily sparkline (`_build_daily_bins`, router.py:6479) whose response model has no degraded field (roster/relationship/api/models.py:1456-1468) — a chronicler outage is rendered to the owner as quiet weeks in a relationship. The ideal is the inverse on every axis: one public-schema typed-edge projection every butler writes behind its own canonical store, a deterministic zero-LLM traversal core tool over it that needs no Rule 3 exception because it touches only public tables, and one fleet dossier route that composes public reads + timed MCP fan-out + the already-built RFC-0020 calendar overlay batch, where every section carries its own `{source, fetched_at, ok, degraded_reason}` receipt and a coverage line naming which butlers contributed, which never projected, and how many facts each is holding back by sensitivity class.
audits.ideal: From any entity the owner opens one page that answers "what does my whole household of agents know about this person, and how sure is each of them" in five seconds, and every clause on it is a door. Underneath, the fleet's knowledge graph is a single public-schema projection — `public.entity_graph_edges` — that each butler writes behind its own canonical store exactly the way `public.memory_catalog` already works: never canonical, always carrying a provenance pointer (`source_butler`/`source_schema`/`source_table`/`source_id`) back to the owning schema, a `projected_at` freshness stamp, and, for knowledge the owner classified above the shared-index ceiling, the *shape* of the link with `withheld_reason='sensitivity'` and no content. Because that table lives in `public`, every butler already has it on its `search_path` (openspec/specs/entity-identity/spec.md §"Entities table in public schema"; RFC 0010 §Integration explicitly notes public-schema tables need no cross-schema exception), so a deterministic recursive-CTE traversal tool — `entity_graph_walk` / `entity_graph_path`, registered as a new `graph` core-tool group alongside `memory_access` — gives every butler multi-hop context with zero LLM cost, zero cross-schema access, and zero doctrine exception. The dossier sits one layer above: a fleet-level `/api/entities/{id}/dossier` that fuses public-schema deterministic reads (graph edges, entity-filtered catalog rows, `list_entity_commitments`, delegation ledger, attention ledger), real-time MCP fan-out to the butlers that own the payloads (the pattern `_fetch_chronicler_activity` already proves), and the calendar's precomputed RFC-0020 overlay envelopes for upcoming touchpoints. Nothing is fabricated and nothing quietly missing: an unreachable butler is a named unavailable section, a butler that has never projected is named in the coverage receipt, a truncated walk says so, a withheld fact says "health holds 2 facts it does not publish to the fleet index" with a `delegate_ask` door beside it, and a merged entity redirects to its survivor rather than rendering an empty graph.

findings.title: Chronicler outage is rendered as owner inactivity on the entity activity stream and sparkline
findings.detail: `_fetch_chronicler_activity` catches everything (`except (ButlerUnreachableError, TimeoutError, Exception)`) and returns `[]` (roster/relationship/api/router.py:6398-6407). `get_entity_activity` then gathers relationship + chronicler entries, merges, computes `total = len(all_entries)`, and — with `bins=daily` — builds a dense per-day series including zero-count days via `_build_daily_bins` (router.py:6479, 6584-6600). `ActivityResponse` (roster/relationship/api/models.py:1456-1468) carries only `items/total/limit/offset`: no degraded flag, no `meta.sources_degraded`. The repo already owns the correct primitive (`src/butlers/api/degraded.py:17 DegradedSources`) and the convention that mandates it (docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md:66-73). Result: a chronicler restart or timeout paints genuine-looking quiet weeks into the owner's relationship history — failure impersonating health on the exact surface the dossier extends.

findings.title: memory_catalog's entity anchor is written and indexed on every fact, and read by nothing
findings.detail: core_009 declares `entity_id` (line 143), `object_entity_id` (line 172), and a partial index whose comment is literally "Entity_id B-tree index for entity-anchored lookups" (lines 218-223); the module header repeats it (line 26). `_upsert_catalog` writes both columns on every fact upsert and re-writes them on conflict (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:433-499), fed from the fact write path at storage.py:2005-2033. Both catalog readers — `_catalog_semantic_search` (search.py:830-863) and `_catalog_keyword_search` (search.py:866-908) — build their WHERE from `tenant_id`, `invalid_at`, `memory_type` and `sensitivity` only; neither `search_catalog` (search.py:910) nor the MCP tool (tools/reading.py:113) nor `GET /api/memory/catalog/search` (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1400) accepts an entity parameter. The fleet-wide entity graph is fully materialised and completely unreadable. This is a new exemplar of the known computed-then-discarded theme and is the enabling gap for the whole move.

findings.title: The relationship graph is structurally invisible to every other butler
findings.detail: `relationship.entity_facts` is the system's richest edge set (subject → object with `object_kind='entity'`, weighted, verified, validity-tracked). rel_013 grants it to `butler_relationship_rw` only (roster/relationship/migrations/013_relationship_facts.py:173-175, `_RELATIONSHIP_ROLE`), and the only widening since is a SELECT for `connector_writer` scoped to Gmail policy lookups (roster/relationship/migrations/033_connector_entity_facts_read_grant.py:26-30) plus chronicler's explicit evidence-surface grant (scripts/init-db.sql:537). Nothing projects these edges into `public`: `_upsert_catalog` is only ever called with `source_table='facts'` (storage.py:2008) and `source_table='rules'` (storage.py:2180). Consequence: the finance butler cannot know a counterparty is the owner's brother, the health butler cannot know a contact is the owner's doctor, and the neighbour rail on the fleet-level entity page (router.py:4315-4390) is relationship-only by construction.

findings.title: The shared catalog's documented "DELETE withheld" least-privilege guardrail does not exist in any real deployment
findings.detail: core_009's grant model is explicit: "Butler roles receive narrow SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE grants only" and "DELETE is intentionally withheld; catalog GC is handled by the owning butler or a periodic sweep" (alembic/versions/core/core_009_memory_catalog.py:29-33), implemented as `_CATALOG_PRIVILEGES = "SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE"` (line 63). Bootstrap contradicts it wholesale: init-db grants every butler runtime role `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public` (scripts/init-db.sql:376-379) and sets the identical set as ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for tables the migration user creates later (scripts/init-db.sql:403-407) — which is how `public.memory_catalog` itself becomes reachable. Any butler can delete any other butler's catalog rows. The same drift makes core_009's `_ALL_BUTLER_ROLES` (lines 47-57, omitting `butler_chronicler_rw` and `butler_lifestyle_rw`) and core_065's `_ROLE_SCHEMAS` (omitting `chronicler`) dead lists rather than the access model. Any new public projection table that reuses "DELETE withheld" as its guardrail inherits a guarantee that is not enforced.

findings.title: Sensitivity-excluded facts leave the fleet index silently and uncountably
findings.detail: `_is_catalog_write_excluded` drops every fact classified `pii` or `confidential` before the catalog INSERT, emitting a `logger.debug` and returning (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:86-100, 421-431). No row, no tombstone, no counter. The write-time exclusion is correct policy, but it means no catalog-backed surface can ever honestly say "this is what the fleet knows" — it can only say "this is what the fleet publishes", and today it cannot even quantify the difference. Any entity dossier built on the catalog alone under-reports by an unknown amount, which is precisely staleness/omission wearing current-data authority.

findings.title: Entity-anchored commitment lookup seq-scans the whole owner condition ledger
findings.detail: `list_entity_commitments` filters `public.owner_conditions` on `metadata->>'class' = 'commitment'` and `metadata->>'counterparty_entity_id' = $2` (src/butlers/core/commitments.py:466-488). core_184 creates only `uq_owner_conditions_active_episode (source, fingerprint)` and the per-identity episode index (alembic/versions/core/core_184_owner_conditions.py:120-130) — there is no expression index on either metadata key. The function is documented as deliberately unscoped by source ("what is outstanding between me and Sam spans every butler", commitments.py:458-464), i.e. it is the fleet's per-entity commitment read, and it is already called per entity from roster/relationship/tools/commitments.py:862. A dossier that calls it on every entity open makes a full ledger scan a page-load cost.

findings.title: A fleet-level route served entirely by one specialist's API
findings.detail: The shell mounts `/entities/:entityId` at top level (frontend/src/router-config.tsx:66,145) and redirects the legacy `/butlers/relationship/entities/:entityId` *into* it (frontend/src/router.tsx:25, router-config.tsx:154) — the information architecture already asserts that an entity is a fleet object, not a relationship record. Every hook the page uses lands on `roster/relationship/api/router.py:170` `APIRouter(prefix="/api/relationship")`. The page therefore promises fleet identity and delivers one domain plus one best-effort chronicler call, and any cross-domain addition made inside that router pulls a specialist's manifesto scope past its own boundary (vision.md Rule 6).

findings.title: butlers_with_module() returns None on missing metadata and callers widen to "all butlers"
findings.detail: `DatabaseManager.butlers_with_module` returns `None` when no module metadata has been registered "so callers can fall back to querying all butlers rather than silently returning an empty list" (src/butlers/api/db.py:333-353). For a counted-coverage fan-out that fallback is the wrong failure direction in the other axis: the dossier would report a denominator it did not verify, and a butler whose metadata is missing is indistinguishable from one that legitimately has nothing. Any fleet aggregator built on it needs to distinguish `metadata_unavailable` from `not_participating` before it prints "7 of 9 butlers contributing".

moves.title: Entity-anchored fleet dossier on a public typed-edge projection, with a zero-LLM graph traversal core tool
moves.why: vision.md Rule 3 forbids cross-schema reads but RFC 0010 §Integration (about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0010-cross-butler-briefing-exception.md:146) states public-schema tables "are already within every butler's search_path by design" and therefore need no exception — so the fleet graph belongs in `public`, written write-behind by each owning butler, exactly as `public.memory_catalog` already is. The substrate is 90% built and 0% read: catalog rows already carry `entity_id`/`object_entity_id` with a dedicated index (core_009:143,172,218-223) and `list_entity_commitments` is already documented as the cross-butler per-entity read ("'what is outstanding between me and Sam' spans every butler that files commitments", src/butlers/core/commitments.py:458-464). Owner payoff: from any person, one page that answers what the whole household knows, with each butler's contribution, confidence, freshness and refusals named — the five-second verification the north star demands, on the fleet's most-opened detail page. Manifesto served: this move *removes* scope creep from the relationship butler (RFC 0014's chronicler boundary and roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md keep episodes and calendar out of relationship's domain) by moving fleet aggregation out of `/api/relationship` and into a fleet-level route, leaving each specialist owning only what its manifesto claims (vision.md Rule 6).
moves.integration_points:
SCHEMA (new, `public`, doctrine-legal because entity identity is fleet-shared by construction — openspec/specs/entity-identity/spec.md §"Entities table in public schema"): `public.entity_graph_edges (id UUID PK, src_entity_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.entities(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, dst_entity_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.entities(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, predicate TEXT NOT NULL, direction_of_record TEXT CHECK IN ('forward','symmetric'), source_butler TEXT NOT NULL, source_schema TEXT NOT NULL, source_table TEXT NOT NULL, source_id UUID NOT NULL, confidence DOUBLE PRECISION, validity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK IN ('active','retracted','superseded'), observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, projected_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), withheld_reason TEXT, CONSTRAINT uq_ege_source UNIQUE (source_schema, source_table, source_id), CONSTRAINT chk_ege_no_self CHECK (src_entity_id <> dst_entity_id))`; partial indexes `(src_entity_id, predicate) WHERE validity='active'`, `(dst_entity_id, predicate) WHERE validity='active'`, `(projected_at DESC)`. Why a table and not a UNION view over memory_catalog: (a) the catalog structurally excludes pii/confidential rows (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:86-100) so it can never be the only edge source; (b) `relationship.entity_facts` edges are granted to one role (roster/relationship/migrations/013_relationship_facts.py:173-175) and unioning them publicly would grant far more than edge tuples; (c) a view cannot carry `projected_at`, and the north star forbids stale data wearing current authority. GRANTS: migration mirrors core_009's `_grant_if_table_exists` guard (core_009:70-90) but the role list is repaired to match scripts/init-db.sql:110-122 (chronicler and lifestyle included) — and per finding #4 the spec must NOT claim DELETE is withheld unless scripts/init-db.sql:376-379,403-407 is narrowed in the same change.

WRITERS (three, each inside its own owner, no cross-schema writes): (1) memory write-behind — extend the `_upsert_catalog` call site at src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2005-2033 to also project an edge when `object_entity_id IS NOT NULL`, and change the early return at storage.py:93-100 so a sensitivity-excluded fact still projects an edge row with `withheld_reason='sensitivity'` and no summary; (2) relationship — project on the `assert_fact` path (roster/relationship/tools/relationship_assert_fact.py, the same hook identified in docs/concepts/identity-model.md:72) for `object_kind='entity'` rows of rel_013's table; (3) commitments — `create_commitment` already takes `counterparty_entity_id` (src/butlers/core/commitments.py:261-282), project `owner → counterparty` with predicate by `direction`.

MCP TOOLS (new core-tool group `graph`, new file src/butlers/core_tools/_graph.py registered by the `register_*_tool(ctx, mcp, _core_tool)` pattern of src/butlers/core_tools/_memory_access.py:50-60, dispatched from src/butlers/core_tools/__init__.py, gated by `core_groups` in src/butlers/core/runtime_config.py:39): `entity_graph_walk(entity_id: str, *, max_hops: int = 2, predicates: list[str] | None = None, direction: str = 'both', include_retracted: bool = False, limit: int = 200) -> dict` — docstring: "Walk the fleet's shared entity graph outward from one entity. Reads only public-schema tables (`public.entity_graph_edges`, `public.entities`), so this is not a Rule 3 exception and costs no LLM session. Every edge carries source_butler/source_schema/source_table/source_id — fetch the canonical record from the owning butler through its MCP tools, never by querying its schema. Every edge carries projected_at and a `stale` flag computed against that butler's projection-lag budget; an edge with withheld_reason='sensitivity' means the owning butler holds a fact linking these entities but classifies it above the shared-index ceiling — the link is real, the content is not here, and must not be guessed; ask via delegate_ask. Returns {nodes:[{entity_id,canonical_name,entity_type,roles,hop}], edges:[...], coverage:{butlers_projecting,butlers_never_projected,oldest_projection_at}, truncated:bool}; `truncated` is set when `limit` was hit — the walk never silently trims. Raises ValueError for an unknown entity_id, max_hops outside 1-3, or an unknown direction; a tombstoned entity (metadata.merged_into set, see public.entities uq index at core_002_identity.py:126-131) raises WITH the survivor id so the caller re-walks rather than reading an empty graph as 'no connections'." And `entity_graph_path(from_entity_id, to_entity_id, *, max_hops: int = 3) -> dict` returning `{path, hops}` or `{path: null, searched_hops, reason: 'no_path_within_max_hops' | 'unprojected_source'}` — 'we could not find one' is never rendered as 'there is none'. Both implemented as a single recursive CTE; no LLM, no fan-out.

PER-BUTLER DOSSIER CONTRIBUTION (MCP, Rule 3-clean, real-time): one new tool per participating butler, `entity_dossier_contribution(entity_id: str, since: str | None = None) -> dict` returning `{butler, headline, items:[{kind, ref, label, at, confidence}], withheld_by_sensitivity:{pii:int, confidential:int}, generated_at}` — `withheld_by_sensitivity` is the counter finding #5 says does not exist today, and it is what lets the dossier be honest about the catalog's structural blind spot. `kind` must come from the closed vocabulary in src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py:73 (`task|session|event|delegation|memory`), extended in the same change with `condition` and `calendar_event` so commitments and touchpoints are doors, not prose.

API: new fleet-level router src/butlers/api/routers/entity_dossier.py, `APIRouter(prefix="/api/entities", tags=["entities"])`, included in src/butlers/api/app.py beside `identity_router` (app.py:73,670). `GET /api/entities/{entity_id}/dossier` composes: public deterministic reads (the graph walk; `public.memory_catalog WHERE entity_id=$1 OR object_entity_id=$1` using the unused index at core_009:218-223; `list_entity_commitments` from src/butlers/core/commitments.py:451; `public.delegation_ledger`; `public.attention_ledger`), timed MCP fan-out over `db.butlers_with_module(...)` (src/butlers/api/db.py:333) using the exact pattern of `_fetch_chronicler_activity` (roster/relationship/api/router.py:6379-6407) but with per-source receipts instead of a bare `[]`, and upcoming touchpoints from the already-built RFC-0020 batch path (`calendar.v_overlay_contributions`, src/butlers/jobs/calendar_overlay.py:55-57 `OVERLAY_KEY_PREFIX`, joined on per-schema `calendar_event_entities` from alembic/versions/core/core_076_calendar_event_columns_and_entities.py:90-99) — zero LLM, zero new exception. Envelope threads `DegradedSources` (src/butlers/api/degraded.py:17) into `meta.sources_degraded` per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md:66-73, plus `meta.coverage = {contributing:[...], never_projected:[...], metadata_unavailable:bool}` (finding #8).

FRONTEND: new tier on frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx (3333 lines; add as a Tier-4/5 body slot under the `<Page archetype="detail">` contract in openspec/specs/detail-page-archetype/spec.md §"Detail-page six-tier body layout"), reusing `SourceDegradedNote` (EntityDetailPage.tsx:53), `ProvenanceMarks`/`StalenessBand` (EntityDetailPage.tsx:56), the freshness-plaque vocabulary proven at frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.freshness-plaque.test.ts, and the existing merged-entity redirect path `resolveMergeMetadata` (EntityDetailPage.tsx:~124-140) so a tombstoned entity redirects instead of showing an empty dossier.

SPEC DELTA: new `openspec/specs/entity-graph/spec.md` (edge table, projection contract, both MCP tools, coverage-receipt semantics, sensitivity-withheld edges); new `openspec/specs/entity-dossier/spec.md` (route contract, per-source receipts, honesty requirements); amend `openspec/specs/entity-identity/spec.md` (add "Requirement: Fleet edge projection" beside the public-entities requirement); amend `openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md` (add "Requirement: Entity-anchored catalog reads" for the unused index, and "Requirement: Counted sensitivity exclusion" turning storage.py:93-100's silent skip into a tallied one); amend `openspec/specs/dashboard-relationship/spec.md` to move fleet aggregation out and `openspec/specs/detail-page-archetype/spec.md` for the new tier. DOCTRINE: no new cross-schema exception is required, but one short RFC 0028 "Public-schema fleet projections" must land in slice 1 stating that a public-schema projection written write-behind by the owning butler is not cross-schema access, and fixing the projection contract (never canonical; provenance pointer mandatory; withheld edges carry shape not content; the grant model must match scripts/init-db.sql, not contradict it) — without it the next reviewer reads `entity_graph_edges` as an end-run around Rule 3.

It writes `state['entity_graph/backfill/<butler>'] = {completed_at, rows_projected, source_rows_scanned}` so the coverage receipt can distinguish `never_backfilled` from `backfilled_empty`. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet already discovers cross-butler situations and then destroys them. `_cluster_candidates` (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:840) runs union-find over `metadata.entity_id` and `metadata.event_window` to find candidates from different butlers that concern one real-world thing; `_synthesize_cluster_sentence` (broker.py:909) then spends a metered LLM call — token usage recorded under `purpose="insight_cluster_synthesis"` (broker.py:980-989) — to name what connects them; `_format_digest` (broker.py:1004-1046) interpolates that sentence into a string and returns. Nothing is written. The correlation, the synthesized situation name, and the membership all evaporate at the end of one cron tick. Worse, clustering only ever sees the top-B candidates selected by *this* cycle after cooldown (broker.py:309), dedup (broker.py:362) and budget (broker.py:405), so a trip's travel signal on Monday and its finance signal on Thursday are structurally incapable of clustering, and `insight_cooldowns` actively suppresses the follow-up signals of a developing situation as "repeats". The fleet has three durable ledgers that each answer one slice — `public.domain_events`/`domain_event_deliveries` (transport, src/butlers/core/domain_events.py:88), `public.domain_event_reactions` (per-wake outcome with typed evidence, src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py:60-73), `public.owner_conditions` (single-producer standing concern lifecycle, src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py:325,399) — and no object at which they join. Attention is budgeted per message, never per situation: `record_attention_event` (src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:184) keys everything to origin_butler/dedup_key and `is_priority_urgent` (attention_ledger.py:174) fails open per candidate, so five butlers each proposing a priority-95 signal about one illness produce five independent urgent bypasses of quiet hours. On the dashboard, the only multi-signal standing surface is a flat merged row list (frontend/src/components/system/StandingConditionsTile.tsx:1-30 via src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:1330-1345) with no container to open. The result is exactly what the north star forbids: the owner gets N uncoordinated pings about one thing, no door leads from any of them to the situation itself, and when the situation quietly ends nothing records that it did.
audits.ideal: One real-world situation is one durable object. When signals from two or more butlers concern the same trip, illness, move, or incident, the fleet opens exactly one `public.fleet_cases` row keyed on a readable correlation identity, and every butler thereafter contributes typed evidence to it through an MCP tool instead of proposing another independent insight. The case owns the attention posture — the urgent bypass is evaluated once per case, not once per contributing butler, so one situation costs the owner one interruption no matter how many specialists noticed it — and the posture always names who set it and why. Contribution is butler-local and doctrine-legal (evidence INSERT under the butler's own role, exactly as `domain_event_reactions` already is); identity, posture arbitration, and closure are Switchboard-only, routed through the existing `route()` dispatch, so no butler can unilaterally make the fleet shout and no butler ever touches another butler's schema. A case closes with a typed outcome and a real evidence ref, enforced as a database CHECK, and the only verdict a sweep may write about silence is `lapsed` — never `resolved`. The dashboard renders one attention row per live case, and that row is a door onto the full multi-domain dossier: every contributor, every evidence ref, the posture history, the linked insight candidates, domain events, owner conditions and approvals. Staleness demotes posture and says so; a contributor going quiet shows as "last evidence 6d ago from health", never as a resolved situation. The system reasons about situations; only domain butlers reason about domains.

findings.title: Cross-butler correlation and its LLM-synthesized name are computed, paid for, and discarded every delivery cycle
findings.detail: `_cluster_candidates` performs transitive union-find over entity_id / event-window to discover a multi-butler situation; `_synthesize_cluster_sentence` spends a metered `insight_cluster_synthesis` API call to name it; `_format_digest` renders it into a string and returns. Nothing is persisted — the same situation is rediscovered and re-synthesized (or lost) on the next tick, and no reader, session, or dashboard can ever see that the fleet knew two butlers were talking about one thing. This is the missing durable spine the case file must occupy, and it is already 90% computed.

findings.title: Correlation scope is one cycle's top-B, so a situation that unfolds over days can never be seen — and cooldowns actively suppress its follow-up signals
findings.detail: delivery_cycle clusters only the candidates it selected this cycle, after expiry, cooldown filtering, dedup and the daily budget. A trip's travel signal delivered Monday and its finance signal delivered Thursday are structurally incapable of clustering. Simultaneously `insight_cooldowns` (dedup_key PRIMARY KEY) suppresses the later signals of a *developing* situation as duplicate repeats, so the longer a real situation runs the less the fleet says about it.

findings.title: The urgent-priority bypass is per candidate, so one situation noticed by five butlers buys five independent quiet-hours overrides
findings.detail: URGENT_PRIORITY_THRESHOLD / is_priority_urgent are evaluated on each candidate's own priority_score; the attention policy fails open per candidate. Nothing in the ledger or the broker can tell that five priority-95 rows describe one illness, so the owner's quiet hours are broken five times for one event. The run-09 'one attention budget' move routes unsolicited notify() through the broker but still budgets per message, not per situation.

findings.title: Reaction receipts close a wake, not a situation, and the evidence vocabulary has no term for one
findings.detail: `domain_event_reactions` gives a per-(event, subscriber) terminal outcome with typed evidence and a database-enforced close-exactly-once invariant — the right discipline — but there is no object at which reactions to several event types aggregate into one outcome. EVIDENCE_KINDS is a closed set of five with no `case`/`situation` kind, so a butler that acted because of a multi-domain situation can only point at the single triggering event, and the run-08 'one evidence cohort per verdict' work has no cohort to hang on.

findings.title: The condition ledger has exactly the lifecycle a case needs but is single-producer by construction, so a case cannot be a metadata class on it
findings.detail: condition_ledger maintains at-most-one-active episode per (source, fingerprint) with open/aging/resolve, L0-L3 escalation, and mandatory resolution evidence — and commitments already reuse it as a metadata convention rather than a new table. But its identity is a fingerprint of ONE producer's facts and its write lock is keyed by (table, source): a cross-butler situation has no single source, so reusing it would either lie about `source` or serialize every butler on one advisory-lock key. This is the design evidence that the case file must be a new public table with a correlation-key identity, not `owner_conditions.metadata.class='case'`.

moves.title: Fleet Case File: one durable, situation-scoped object that accumulates cross-butler evidence, owns its attention posture, and closes with a typed outcome
moves.why:
Vision non-negotiable #3 (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:71-78) makes MCP-through-Switchboard the only sanctioned cross-butler channel, and #6 (:103-111) makes each specialist's manifesto binding — so the fleet has never had a place to say 'these five signals are one thing' without either a monolithic agent (forbidden, :42-48) or schema cross-reads (forbidden). The case file is the doctrine-legal shape: Switchboard arbitrates identity and posture (its own staffer contract: routing backbone, roster/switchboard/AGENTS.md), domain butlers contribute only their own domain's evidence, and no butler reads another's schema. It serves the north star's 'every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine': today the spine breaks at the last hop, because the correlation that would BE the case is computed at roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:840 and destroyed at :1046. Owner payoff: one trip = one interruption and one page, instead of N pings from travel, finance, health and calendar with no way to see they were the same trip; and when the trip ends the system records that it ended instead of going quiet.

--- DATA MODEL (public schema; placement rationale below) ---
New migration alembic/versions/core/core_209_fleet_cases.py, down_revision='core_208' (matches alembic/versions/core/core_208_runtime_attention_operator.py).

CREATE TABLE public.fleet_cases (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- open vocabulary, regex-validated like domain_events event_type
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  correlation_key TEXT NOT NULL,       -- readable identity, see recipe
  anchor_entity_id UUID REFERENCES public.entities(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  anchor_window TSTZRANGE,             -- half-open, same semantics as broker._candidate_time_window
  state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',  -- open|watching|closing|closed
  posture TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'silent',   -- silent|routine|active|urgent
  posture_reason TEXT, posture_set_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'switchboard',
  opened_by TEXT NOT NULL, opened_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_evidence_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  closed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, outcome TEXT,      -- resolved|lapsed|superseded|not_a_situation
  outcome_evidence JSONB, metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  CONSTRAINT fleet_cases_closed_needs_outcome CHECK ((state<>'closed') OR (outcome IS NOT NULL AND outcome_evidence IS NOT NULL))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX fleet_cases_one_active ON public.fleet_cases (correlation_key) WHERE state IN ('open','watching','closing');
  -- mirrors condition_ledger's at-most-one-active-episode invariant (src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py:29-36) and domain_event_reactions' close-exactly-once partial index (src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py:30-45)

CREATE TABLE public.fleet_case_evidence (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  case_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.fleet_cases(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  contributor TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, ref TEXT NOT NULL, label TEXT NOT NULL,
  significance TEXT NOT NULL,          -- observation|action|obstacle|resolution
  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, recorded_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  payload JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  UNIQUE (case_id, contributor, kind, ref)   -- idempotent re-contribution
);
CREATE INDEX ON public.fleet_case_evidence (case_id, occurred_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE public.fleet_case_links (
  case_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.fleet_cases(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  link_kind TEXT NOT NULL,   -- insight_candidate|domain_event|owner_condition|attention_ledger|approval|commitment
  link_ref TEXT NOT NULL, linked_by TEXT NOT NULL, linked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (case_id, link_kind, link_ref)
);

SECURITY DEFINER trigger on fleet_case_evidence AFTER INSERT bumps fleet_cases.last_evidence_at, so a contributing butler never needs UPDATE on fleet_cases.

`kind` is regex-validated, not an enum — same open-vocabulary posture as event_type (src/butlers/core/domain_events.py:64-70), so a new situation class needs no migration.
`correlation_key` recipe (deliberately readable, not a hash — a butler must be able to check for an existing case before opening one, and the dashboard must be able to show it; mirrors dedup_key's readable segment format, roster/switchboard/tools/insight/models.py:14-18): `entity:<uuid>` when anchored to a public.entities row, else `window:<kind>:<start-date>/<end-date>`.

--- WHY public IS DOCTRINE-LEGAL, AND NO RFC EXCEPTION IS NEEDED FOR THE SCHEMA ---
Every cross-butler table in this repo already lives in public with explicit per-role GRANTs: public.domain_events/domain_event_deliveries (alembic/versions/core/core_186_domain_events.py), public.domain_event_contracts/domain_event_reactions (alembic/versions/core/core_206_domain_event_contracts_and_reactions.py:39-56, _ALL_RUNTIME_ROLES + 'SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE'), public.attention_ledger, public.owner_conditions. Non-negotiable #3 forbids butlers reading each other's SCHEMAS and calling each other's functions; it does not forbid a shared public table that every butler reaches only through its own MCP tools. RFC 0010's read-only-view exception is NOT invoked here. Grants split by authority: SELECT on all three tables to every runtime role (copy the list at core_206:39-52); INSERT on fleet_case_evidence to every runtime role (butlers write their own evidence under their own role, exactly as record_reaction already does); INSERT/UPDATE on fleet_cases and fleet_case_links to butler_switchboard_rw ONLY. Identity, posture and closure are therefore single-authority by database grant, not by convention.

--- MCP TOOL SIGNATURES ---
New module src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py with `register_fleet_case_tools(ctx, mcp, _core_tool)`, structurally identical to `register_domain_event_tools` (src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py:888-902): same `if ctx.butler_type == ButlerType.STAFFER: return` gate, same `@_core_tool("fleet_cases")` + `@tool_span(...)` stacking (:903-910), wired at src/butlers/core_tools/_dispatcher.py:65 beside register_domain_event_tools. Mutations of fleet_cases go through the shared Switchboard dispatch, `dispatch_via_switchboard_route` (src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard_route_dispatch.py:90), exactly as _domain_events does — so no butler role ever needs INSERT on fleet_cases.

1) find_open_case(anchor_entity_id: str|None=None, on_date: str|None=None, kind: str|None=None) -> dict
   """Find the open fleet case, if any, that already covers this situation.
   Call this BEFORE proposing an insight about something that plausibly spans
   domains (a trip, an illness, a move). Returns {"status":"ok","cases":[...]}.
   An empty list means no case is currently open — it does NOT mean no case
   should be, and it is never evidence that nothing is happening. Read-only;
   never opens a case."""

2) open_case(kind: str, title: str, why: str, first_evidence: dict, anchor_entity_id: str|None=None, window_start: str|None=None, window_end: str|None=None) -> dict
   """Open one durable fleet case for a situation that spans more than your
   own domain, routed through the Switchboard (you are not the authority on
   case identity).
   Idempotent on the derived correlation key: if an active case already covers
   this identity you get THAT case back with "created": false — never a second
   case, never a silently merged one.
   `first_evidence` is required and typed ({kind, ref, label, significance}):
   a case with no evidence is a claim, not a case.
   Returns {"status":"ok","case_id":...,"created":bool} or
   {"status":"error","retryable":bool} when the Switchboard is unreachable —
   in which case you have NO case id: fall back to a plain insight candidate
   and do not invent one."""

3) contribute_case_evidence(case_id: str, kind: str, ref: str, label: str, significance: str, occurred_at: str|None=None, payload: dict|None=None) -> dict
   """Add one typed piece of evidence from YOUR domain to an existing case.
   Written under your own role directly (no Switchboard round trip) and
   idempotent on (case, you, kind, ref), so re-reporting the same fact is a
   no-op rather than a duplicate. `kind` must be one of the closed evidence
   vocabulary (task, session, event, delegation, memory, insight, condition,
   approval, case) — untyped evidence is refused, because a claim you cannot
   open is indistinguishable from a guess. Prose belongs in `label`.
   Contributing evidence refreshes the case's freshness; it does not change
   its posture — use propose_case_posture for that."""

4) propose_case_posture(case_id: str, posture: str, why: str) -> dict
   """Propose how loud this case should be (silent|routine|active|urgent).
   A proposal, not a setting: the Switchboard arbitrates across every
   proposer, the highest live proposal wins, and the winner's butler and
   reason are stamped on the case so the owner always sees WHO made this
   urgent and WHY. You cannot unilaterally make the fleet shout.
   Returns the arbitrated posture, which may not be the one you proposed."""

5) close_case(case_id: str, outcome: str, evidence: dict) -> dict
   """Close a case with a typed outcome: 'resolved' (the situation genuinely
   ended, and `evidence` points at what shows it), 'not_a_situation' (these
   signals were a coincidence), or 'superseded' (folded into another case).
   'lapsed' is reserved to the lapse sweep and refused here — you may not
   report silence as resolution. Evidence is mandatory and enforced by a
   database CHECK, mirroring the commitment ledger's no-silent-resolution
   rule (src/butlers/core/commitments.py:20-27). Only the opening butler or
   the Switchboard may close."""

6) read_case(case_id: str) -> dict
   """Read the full case dossier: every contributor, every evidence row in
   time order, linked insight candidates / domain events / conditions, and
   the posture history with reasons. Call this when a case_id appears in your
   prompt, so the situation is read once rather than re-derived in every
   session."""

Switchboard-side implementations these route() onto live in roster/switchboard/tools/case/{open,posture,close,merge}.py, registered like the existing roster/switchboard/tools/insight package.

--- MIGRATION + BACKFILL ---
core_209 creates the three tables and the grants split above. Backfill is a one-shot `fleet_case_backfill` job that re-runs `_cluster_candidates` (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:840) over 90 days of public.insight_candidates WHERE status='delivered', and for each multi-butler cluster inserts a case in state='closed', outcome='lapsed', posture='silent', metadata.backfilled=true, with evidence rows of kind 'insight' pointing at the candidate ids. It opens ZERO active cases: a historical correlation is not evidence a situation is live, and an auto-opened live case would be a fabricated present-tense claim. Backfilled cases are labelled as such in the UI. No existing data is mutated; insight_candidates.metadata gains an optional case_id key with no migration.

--- FAILURE MODES, EACH SURFACED HONESTLY ---
1. Coincidence mistaken for a situation -> 'not_a_situation' is a first-class closure verb with an owner action ('This isn't one thing'); the split is recorded with its author, never silently deleted.
2. Contributing butler goes down, evidence stops -> lapse sweep demotes posture to 'watching' with posture_reason='evidence_stale' and the header states 'last evidence 6d ago from health'. Never auto-closed: an unobserved situation is not a resolved one; staleness never wears current-data authority.
3. Owner moves on and nobody closes it -> after the stale window the sweep writes outcome='lapsed' with outcome_evidence={kind:'sweep',ref:'fleet_case_lapse_sweep',label:'no evidence for 30d'}. The sweep may never write 'resolved' — the same discipline that lets only the correlation sweep write 'unreported' in src/butlers/core/domain_event_reactions.py:37-40.
