audits.ideal: The single pane is one responsive product with a *declared* viewport and input-modality contract, not a desktop app with a hamburger bolted on. The Dispatch spec names three device bands and, for each of the seven Page archetypes, what collapses and what survives; the Page primitive — not Shell — owns the gutter ramp, and the shell frame is measured in dynamic viewport units inside the safe-area inset, so nothing the owner needs ever sits under a phone's toolbar or home indicator. Under `(pointer: coarse)` every consequential door widens to a 44px hit box automatically, and no fact — least of all a staleness or degradation reason — lives only in a hover channel; hover reveals become tap-to-pin, graph canvases declare `touch-action` and accept pinch, and every canvas has a list fallback. The dashboard knows the difference between "the fleet is down" and "my phone lost signal": one `useClientLink()` primitive gates every failure attribution, so a dropped LTE connection reads as *your link*, and cached rows served across it wear a client-side staleness stamp instead of current-data authority. The pane is installable and precached, so a Telegram approval link tapped on a train paints the frame and the last-known fleet state, labeled as last-known, instead of white. Those linked routes — `/approvals/:id`, `/audit-log?key=`, secrets focus — are a registered set with a phone-first landing shape: the consequential clause and its door above the fold at 375px, evidence one tap deeper. And all of it is a gate, not a habit: a coarse-pointer ESLint guard with a frozen baseline plus a phone Playwright project that walks every route in `router-config.tsx` asserting no horizontal document overflow, no sub-floor hit box, and no safe-area clipping.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the mobile story is a single 2022-era artifact — a Radix Sheet behind a 32px hamburger (`Shell.tsx:44-68`) — and nothing else. The binding design language is silent: `openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md` (459 lines) contains zero occurrences of breakpoint, responsive, viewport, or touch, and the only normative narrow-viewport text in the entire spec set is the sidebar-drawer scenario at `dashboard-shell/spec.md:124-130`. With no contract, responsiveness is a per-author habit: 90 of 736 `.tsx` files use any breakpoint prefix at all, and 26 of 41 page files use none. One of seven Page archetypes has a responsive padding ramp; the other six inherit Shell's unconditional `p-6`. There is no touch-target floor — the canonical 44px primitive exists (`inline-action-link.tsx:24`) and is imported by six files, while `size="sm"` (h-8/32px) appears 231 times and `xs`/`icon-xs` (24px) 29 times. There are zero `touch-action`, zero `pointer: coarse`, zero `env(safe-area-inset-*)`, zero `dvh`, and zero `navigator.onLine` occurrences in the whole frontend; no manifest, no service worker, no `theme-color`, no `viewport-fit=cover`. Playwright runs exactly one project, Desktop Chrome, over 16 specs, with a single 320px assertion on one dialog. Two north-star clauses fail specifically on the phone: the shell announces "Fleet event stream offline" and titles the indicator "Fleet event stream: Offline" when the *device* dropped its link, so a client-side failure impersonates a fleet outage; and 30-second-stale react-query cache is then served across that dead link with no client-connectivity stamp. Meanwhile the backend already mints `/approvals/{id}` and secrets deep links into Telegram — so the owner's single most common entry to the single pane is a phone tap onto a surface no test has ever opened at phone width.

findings.title: The binding design language declares no viewport or input-modality contract at all
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md (459 lines, zero hits for breakpoint/responsive/viewport/touch); only normative narrow-viewport text in the spec set is openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md:124-130 (sidebar drawer); frontend/src/pages/*.tsx — 26 of 41 page files contain no `sm:`/`md:`/`lg:`/`xl:` prefix; 90 of 736 .tsx files use any breakpoint
findings.detail: Dispatch is otherwise an unusually complete design language — it legislates surface tokens, a rem type-role scale, motion vocabulary, state-color discipline, even an attention-tint exception. It is silent on the one axis that decides whether the pane works away from the desk. Consequence: responsiveness is an author-by-author habit rather than a reviewable requirement, so a reviewer has nothing to cite and CI has nothing to check. Every other finding in this sweep is downstream of this absence, which is why it is the root move rather than a symptom.

findings.title: Client-side network loss is rendered and announced as a fleet outage
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/LiveIndicator.tsx:45 (label 'Offline'), :66 (title=`Fleet event stream: ${meta.label}`); frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:22-26 (STREAM_EDGE_LABEL.down = 'Fleet event stream offline', announced via aria-live at :82); zero `navigator.onLine` occurrences in frontend/src; frontend/src/lib/query-client.ts:6 (staleTime 30_000, retry 1, no networkMode/onlineManager wiring)
findings.detail: The shell has exactly one connectivity model — WebSocket health — and attributes every failure of it to the fleet. On a phone that loses LTE in a lift or on a train, the pane asserts a fact about the owner's infrastructure that it cannot know, in both the visible chip and the screen-reader announcement. It then keeps serving 30s-stale cached rows across the dead link with no client-side staleness stamp. This is a direct double hit on the north star: failure impersonating health (the client's failure wearing the fleet's name) and staleness wearing current-data authority. It is also mobile-specific — on a wired desk the case effectively never fires, which is why nine prior sweeps never surfaced it.

findings.title: No touch-target floor exists; the 44px primitive is used by six files and the only mobile nav entry is 32px
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/inline-action-link.tsx:24 (`min-h-11 min-w-11`) — the only 44px floor in src/ besides the skip link at frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:104; imported by 6 non-test files; frontend/src/components/ui/button.tsx:24-31 (default h-9/36px, sm h-8/32px, xs h-6/24px, icon-xs size-6/24px); `size="sm"` × 231, `xs`+`icon-xs` × 29; frontend/src/components/layout/Shell.tsx:64-68 (hamburger: p-1.5 around a 20px icon = 32px); frontend/src/components/layout/PageHeader.tsx:161 (theme toggle h-8 w-8)
findings.detail: The Button ladder's *largest* size (`lg`, h-10/40px) is still below the 44px coarse-pointer floor, and nothing in the codebase conditions size on input modality — there are zero `(pointer: coarse)` or `(hover: none)` media queries anywhere, even though the repo already honours `prefers-reduced-motion` in two places (index.css:766,787), proving the capability-query pattern is understood and simply never applied to input. The single worst instance is structural: the hamburger at Shell.tsx:64 is the *only* way to reach navigation below `md`, on every one of 59 routes, at 32px.

findings.title: No PWA, no offline shell, no safe-area, and a static-viewport-unit frame
findings.evidence: frontend/index.html:6 (`width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` — no `viewport-fit=cover`), no <link rel="manifest">, no theme-color, no apple-touch-icon; zero hits for serviceWorker/workbox/vite-plugin-pwa in frontend/src, vite.config.ts, package.json; no frontend/public/ directory; zero `env(safe-area-inset-` occurrences repo-wide; frontend/src/components/layout/Shell.tsx:41 (`flex h-screen overflow-hidden`); frontend/src/index.css:371 (`min-height: 100vh`); zero `dvh`/`svh` occurrences
findings.detail: Three separate gaps compound. (a) `h-screen` + root `overflow-hidden` means that on iOS Safari the frame is sized to the *large* viewport while the toolbar covers the bottom band — and because the root clips rather than scrolls, the occluded strip is unreachable. (b) With no safe-area inset, the bottom-pinned floating layer sits inside the home-indicator band in portrait and inside the notch cutout in landscape. (c) With no manifest or service worker the pane cannot be installed and cannot paint anything on a cold, flaky connection — which is precisely the state a Telegram approval link is tapped in. NOTE: the `<title>frontend</title>` / vite.svg favicon / remote-font halves of index.html are ledgered under run 09 first-frame identity and are deliberately excluded here.

findings.title: The top floating layer on every route is a keyboard-only affordance that displaces the touch-usable one
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/shortcut-hints.tsx:96 (`fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50 h-8 w-8 rounded-full opacity-60`) opening a dialog whose entire payload is keyboard bindings (:132-140, Kbd chips); frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:801-807 (comment states it was moved to `bottom-20` specifically to avoid the '?' trigger; `size-12 z-40`)
findings.detail: On a touch device the '?' button is a 32px, 60%-opacity target, in the prime right-thumb zone, at the highest z-index, 16px from the bottom edge (inside the 34px iOS home-indicator band), and its content is inert — there is no keyboard. It also physically evicted the one floating control a phone user can actually use, which had to be pushed 64px up the screen. The layer ordering is exactly inverted for the away-from-desk case, and the code comment documents the eviction as an accepted constraint rather than a defect.

findings.title: Interactive canvases declare no touch gesture contract; two primary surfaces are inoperable by finger
findings.evidence: zero `touch-action` occurrences repo-wide; frontend/src/components/topology/TopologyGraph.tsx:359-366 (ReactFlow with `fitView` and `nodesDraggable={true}` inside a fixed `h-96`, over hardcoded absolute node positions spanning ~0–690 × 0–500 at :93-94, :117 width 140, :131-132 90×90, :164 width 120, :193 width 130, fontSize 11-14px); frontend/src/components/relationship/PlexPage.tsx:1605-1626 (zoom bound solely to a `wheel` listener with `{passive:false}`; header comment :21-22 confirms wheel-zoom/drag-pan/`0`-reset as the only camera controls; no pinch handler); frontend/src/components/ingestion/timeline/HourFlameStrip.tsx:255-256 (per-minute counts revealed only via onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave)
findings.detail: TopologyGraph: at 375px the card column is ~280px wide, so `fitView` on a 690px canvas scales 11px labels to roughly 4-5px, and with `nodesDraggable` and no `touch-action` the widget swallows the vertical drag that should scroll the page. PlexPage: `/entities` is a whole domain surface whose graph is permanently locked at 1× on a phone — wheel events do not exist on touch and there is no gesture handler, so pinch escapes to browser page zoom instead. HourFlameStrip: the minute-resolution counts are the point of the strip and are hover-gated. Distinct from the ledgered 'topology keyboard activation' candidate, which concerns keyboard operability, not gestures.

findings.title: The phone is the primary entry to the single pane, and no test has ever opened it at phone width
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/notifications.py:92-97 (`approval_dashboard_url` → `{DASHBOARD_URL}/approvals/{action_id}`) and :108-121 (embedded as `Review: {action_url}` in the Telegram approval dossier); src/butlers/jobs/secrets_lifecycle.py:407 (`focus_url = f"{dashboard_url}{_focus_fragment(snapshot.key)}"`); src/butlers/api/routers/secrets_v2.py:3665 (`meta.deep_link` → `/audit-log?key=`); frontend/playwright.config.ts:52-57 (single project, `devices["Desktop Chrome"]`) across 16 spec files; only phone-class viewport in the suite is frontend/tests/e2e/entity-v3-depth.spec.ts:981-984 (320px, one Dialog) with the sole width assertion at :1018
findings.detail: The system already treats the phone as the notification channel and the dashboard as the resolution surface — the approval spine's door is literally a URL pasted into Telegram. So the modal first contact with the single pane is a tap on a phone. Yet the routes that link is aimed at (`/approvals/:id` at router-config.tsx:100, `/audit-log`, the secrets focus fragment) have never been rendered at 375px in CI, and `ApprovalsPage` is a 1600+ line surface. The handoff is one-directional too: there is no dashboard→phone counterpart (no 'continue on phone', no QR, no push), so the loop only closes if the phone-side landing works.

findings.title: The fleet-verification footer and 48 other grids are pinned to desktop column counts
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardFooter.tsx:112 (`grid grid-cols-6 gap-4`, no breakpoint prefix, on the ButlersPage status board whose own cell grid IS responsive at frontend/src/pages/ButlersPage.tsx:265); 9 unprefixed `grid-cols-[3-9]` sites total incl. frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2005 (cols-4), :2137 (cols-3), frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerManagementTab.tsx:568 (cols-3), frontend/src/components/approvals/rule-promotion-stats.tsx:85,104 (cols-3), frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx:303 (cols-4); 39 unprefixed arbitrary `grid-cols-[…]` templates

Six stat cells with `gap-4` inside `px-7` on a 375px viewport leaves roughly 30px per cell, into which go labels like 'SESSIONS 24H' and values like '$12.34'. The page above it was made responsive (1/2/4 columns) and its own footer was not, which is the signature of habit rather than contract: the author fixed what they were looking at.

findings.title: Only one of seven Page archetypes carries a responsive gutter; the shell hard-codes the rest
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:287 (`editorial` archetype: `px-4 py-8 sm:px-8 lg:px-14 lg:py-12`) vs :275-303 (detail/editor/status-board/overview/list/workspace wrappers with no padding ramp); frontend/src/components/layout/Shell.tsx:89 (`<main … className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-6">`) and :62 (`<header className="flex h-14 items-center border-b border-border px-6">`)
findings.detail: The archetype system is the obvious and correct home for a per-shape collapse contract — it already encodes max-widths, skeleton shapes, and heading treatment per archetype. It carries a padding ramp on exactly one archetype, apparently as a side effect of that page's editorial layout rather than as a rule. Meanwhile Shell spends an unconditional 48px of a 375px viewport (13%) on horizontal chrome, plus a fixed 56px header, before any content renders.

findings.title: Degradation and staleness explanations are carried in hover-only channels
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ChroniclesPage.tsx:425 (`title="The day-close summary may be out of date."` on the 'stale' eyebrow) and :458 (`title="Coverage or availability for this day could not be affirmed."`); 150 `title="…"` attributes across non-test .tsx; 9 non-test files behind Radix Tooltip (frontend/src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx — trigger is pointer/focus driven, does not open on tap); frontend/src/components/layout/PageHeader.tsx:144 (`title="Cmd/Ctrl+K"`)
findings.detail: The markers themselves stay visible, so this is not staleness claiming current-data authority — but the *reason* a day-close is unaffirmed, which is the part that tells the owner whether to act, is reachable only by hovering. Screen readers get it via the paired aria-label; a finger gets nothing. Native `title` never renders on touch and Radix's TooltipTrigger has no tap path, so both hover channels the codebase uses are dark on a phone. The fix is one `Revealable` primitive (tap-to-pin under coarse pointer, hover under fine) rather than 150 edits.

audits.jarvis_gap: Run 09 hardened each of these four pages individually to a high bar (shared board query, shared undo-window pattern, shared needs-attention classification), but the four routes were never audited as one continuous owner journey. The seams between them still leak: the same canonical board field is trusted in one place and silently mis-rendered in another, the same consequential-action pattern (propose, undo-window, decide) is fully keyboard-driven on one page and mouse-only on its sibling, and drilling from the fleet overview into a single butler's own scoped view of an action queue costs the owner strictly more clicks and keystrokes than staying on the fleet-wide page ever did. None of these are fabrications of new data -- they are all real, already-computed truth that gets dropped, reformatted inconsistently, or stripped of its keyboard door exactly one hop later in the same command-and-control story.
audits.ideal: The four routes should read as one instrument with four zoom levels, not four separately-maintained implementations of the same primitives. Every fact that has one canonical computation (liveness verdict, spend-to-date, needs-attention membership) should have exactly one formatter and one keyboard-verb set wired to it everywhere it appears, so a number or an action available at the fleet grain is never downgraded -- silently wrong, mouse-only, or an extra hop away -- at the single-butler grain. Zooming in from Dashboard's Needs-attention row to a butler's own console tab for that same domain (approvals, restore, spend) should never cost more capability than staying zoomed out; if anything the scoped page, having less to show, should make deciding faster.

findings.detail: A butler with $0.004 spent today shows '<$0.01' in Dashboard's Operations index and '$0.00' in the /butlers board cell for the identical canonical field on the identical butler, one hop apart. This is a real-data authority break, not a display nit: the board page is the one the owner checks first for 'is anything running,' and it is the one silently reporting real spend as zero.

audits.jarvis_gap: Any single hop on this spine — a session, an audit row, an issue occurrence, a decision — is honestly rendered, degradation-aware, and mostly one click from its neighbor: SessionDossier reaches timeline/audit/request context, AuditLogTable reaches sessions, IssuesPanel occurrences reach sessions. But the spine forks into two competing chronicles that never reference each other (/timeline vs /ingestion, both self-described as THE timeline, both keyed by the same `?trace=` contract, zero cross-links), so which "Timeline" an owner lands on after a trace click depends on which component happened to author the link rather than on any single source of truth — the opposite of "follows Dispatch as if built by one hand." And the newest addition to the spine, /decisions (the Owner Decision Desk), was built outside the shared `Page` shell that every sibling route in this group uses, so it silently drops the shell's page-identity screen-reader announcement, standardized loading/error/empty regions, and breadcrumb convention — a third, bespoke layout system coexisting with the `Page`-archetype pages and the `DispatchLayout` pages in one seven-route investigation spine.
audits.ideal: One trace concept, one destination: every `?trace=` link in the fleet — session dossier, notification feed, audit row, issue occurrence — lands on the same chronicle component with the same filter semantics, and if /ingestion's pipeline-scoped view is deliberately narrower than /timeline's fleet-wide one, that distinction is named in the UI (a sub-tab or scope toggle within one page) rather than expressed as two differently-branded pages that happen to share a query param. Every route on the spine — /sessions through /decisions — is built on the same `Page` (or `DispatchLayout`, but not a third bespoke shell) so page-identity announcement, breadcrumbs, loading/empty/error handling and the visual dialect are structurally guaranteed rather than re-implemented per page. An owner can start anywhere on the spine (a notification, an audit row, a session) and reach every other piece of evidence about that same event — session, audit trail, related issue, related approval/decision — without a single re-orientation hop that discards the identifier they were chasing.

findings.title: Two live, uncrosslinked "Timeline" surfaces share the same ?trace= contract
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/TimelinePage.tsx:1-16 (fleet chronicle, TimelineLedger) vs frontend/src/pages/IngestionTimelinePage.tsx:1-30 + frontend/src/components/ingestion/TimelineTab.tsx:37,1562-1568,2196 (separate ingestion-scoped chronicle, also owns ?trace=); frontend/src/components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:284-289 links trace to `/ingestion?trace=`, while frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionDossier.tsx:321-334 links trace to `/timeline?trace=`. Neither page references the other (grep for '/ingestion' in frontend/src/pages/TimelinePage.tsx and frontend/src/components/timeline/*.tsx and for '/timeline' in IngestionTimelinePage.tsx/TimelineTab.tsx returns zero hits beyond an unrelated import path).
findings.detail: Both pages are actively maintained, both call themselves the fleet's/pipeline's chronicle in their own header copy, and both accept the identical `?trace=<id>` deep-link parameter — but they are different route trees with different event sources (TimelineLedger: sessions+notifications+errors; TimelineTab: ingestion pipeline events) and no connective tissue. An owner who clicks a trace link from a notification lands in the ingestion console; the same owner clicking a trace link from a session dossier lands in the fleet timeline. For the same underlying trace_id, which of the two competing chronicles they see depends on which UI element they clicked, not on the trace itself — a direct violation of "follows Dispatch as if built by one hand" and a duplicated-but-divergent mechanism at the surface's most central evidence door.

audits.jarvis_gap: HealthOverviewPage itself is close to the north star — real freshness SLAs, honest degraded notes, a stable ledger index, no fabricated numbers. But the moment the owner leaves that landing page for any of the six record surfaces it indexes, the system stops acting like one hand built it. Three of six record pages (Measurements, Medications, Meals) speak Dispatch's editorial voice (mono Eyebrow, 44px Display, serif Voice); the other three (Conditions, Symptoms, Research) fall back to a generic 24px Title with a plain muted paragraph and no voice at all. None of the six implement the j/k list-triage keyboard pattern that Issues, Approvals, Decisions, Notifications, AuditLog and QA all share, and none register a single palette command (no 'Log dose', 'Log symptom', 'Add condition') even though the parent /health page two clicks upstream does exactly that. The data model already links conditions to symptoms and research (condition_id FKs exist and are populated), but the UI treats that graph as write-once: SymptomTracker renders the condition name as inert text, ResearchTracker and its form drop condition_id entirely, and no record page ever produces a real link to a related record on another page — every satellite page is an island the owner must cross-reference by memory. In Education, one query silently converts a source error into the calm 'No reviews scheduled' empty state, and the whole page never adopted the Dispatch primitives at all (raw Tailwind h1, unstyled shadcn Card/Tabs/Select), reading as a different, older application bolted onto the same shell.

findings.title: Review queue turns a fetch error into a calm 'nothing to review' empty state
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/education/ReviewTimeline.tsx:100 (useMindMaps — data destructured, isError never read), :109 (useAllPendingReviews(mapIds)), :118 (const nodes = reviewResults[i]?.data ?? []; — per-query isError from the underlying useQueries dropped), :174-182 (allEntries.length === 0 renders 'No reviews scheduled. Keep learning and reviews will appear here.' with no error branch)
findings.detail: useAllPendingReviews wraps useQueries, so each mind map's result carries its own isError, but ReviewTimeline only ever reads .data. If any (or every) pending-reviews call fails — or the upstream useMindMaps call fails — allEntries stays empty and the component renders the same reassuring copy it would show for a genuinely caught-up owner. This is the exact 'errors impersonating calm empty states' sin the audit brief names, newly instanced on the Education review queue: a killed backend here reads as 'you have nothing due,' not as a degraded source.

findings.title: Condition graph is stored but not navigable — every cross-reference is a label, not a door
findings.evidence: roster/health/migrations/001_health_tables.py:76-85 (symptoms.condition_id REFERENCES conditions(id)), :88-97 (research.condition_id REFERENCES conditions(id)); frontend/src/components/health/SymptomTracker.tsx:122-123,317 (conditionName rendered as plain uppercase <span>, not a link); frontend/src/components/health/ResearchTracker.tsx (no condition_id reference anywhere in the file) and frontend/src/components/health/ResearchForm.tsx (no condition_id field — the association is not even settable from the dashboard)
findings.detail: Health's own schema models the condition as the hub of a symptom's and a research note's meaning, but the frontend discards that relationship on the research side entirely (not read, not writable) and renders it as inert text on the symptom side. An owner reading 'Type 2 Diabetes' next to a symptom cannot click through to the condition, its medications, or its research — the six health record pages present as independent tables the owner must reconcile in their head, not as a butler that understands how their health data connects. This is 'raw tables to interpret alone' rather than a storefront for what the Health butler knows.

An owner on a keyboard-first workflow loses that model the instant they follow a HealthLedgerIndex link.

audits.jarvis_gap: Each of the four pages individually clears a high bar (honest degraded states, provenance reveals, keyboard palettes, evidence-first empties) — run 09 documented that at fine grain. But walked as one owner journey the surface is four vocabularies wearing one nav bar, not one connected world. The data model already links them: chronicles resolves companion entity_id, calendar resolves attendee/linked-people entity_id (down to Dunbar tier and commitments), and memory facts carry entity_id/entity_name — but three separate UI components that hold a real entity_id render it as inert text, and the entity dossier itself never reaches back into the memory register that produced its own displayed facts. The reader who meets a name on their calendar or in yesterday's chronicle has no keyboard or click path to that person's history; the reader on a person's dossier who wants to audit one fact's confidence/decay/supersession has no path to its canonical memory record. Two of four pages (chronicles, calendar) don't reference each other's routes at all despite chronicles literally rendering calendar data as a ghost track. And "episode" denotes two unrelated data types (raw consolidation-pending memory vs. a lived Gantt time-block) with identical reader-facing vocabulary and zero disambiguation.
audits.ideal: Any entity_id that reaches a render tree — whether from a chronicles companion, a calendar attendee, a linked-people chip, or a memory fact's subject/object — is the same live door to /entities/:id, using the same whole-row/whole-chip link convention already established in FactsRegister and RulesRegister, so a person's name is never just a label anywhere in the product. The entity dossier reciprocates: any curated field sourced from a memory-register Fact carries a visible route to /memory/facts/:id so an owner auditing a claim can reach its confidence, decay, supersession chain, and source episode without leaving through the global register and re-finding it by name. Chronicles and Calendar, which already share data (the ghost intent track), share navigation too — a past calendar day opens its chronicle and a chronicle day can jump to the underlying calendar event. And the two "episode" concepts get either a real UI rename (e.g., "memory episode" vs. "day episode") or a genuine unification, so the same word never means two unrelated database rows to the same reader on two routes of the same surface.

audits.jarvis_gap: Each of the three route families here—ingestion timeline, connectors roster/detail, and the QA dossier—is individually well-built and honestly instrumented (real degraded-source notes, tri-state circuit-breaker, evidence-bearing confirms), which is why run 09's page-grain pass came back mostly clean. But walked as one operator journey the group falls apart at exactly the seam where it matters: the moment something is off. The Timeline page grew its own second, divergent copy of the connector attention list instead of reusing the canonical one, and that copy is not a link at all — an operator sees "telegram/acct-1 · degraded" underlined like every other link on this page, clicks it, and nothing happens; they must remember the /ingestion/connectors path and re-locate the same connector by name. And the group's two failure vocabularies never speak to each other: a QA finding names a source_butler and a fingerprint, a connector incident names a connector_type/endpoint_identity, and nothing on either side of the fence points across it — so an operator chasing "the switchboard butler crashed" has no way to learn whether a flaky connector underneath it is why, and a connector operator staring at a repeating "offline" state has no way to see whether QA already diagnosed and is mid-repair on the root cause. The connectors roster, which is exactly the same shape of triage list as Issues/Notifications/Decisions/Approvals/QA-cases, is the one list in that family never wired to the shared j/k list-triage primitive, so the fastest path through the busiest page in this surface is mouse-only.
audits.ideal: One attention vocabulary, one attention mechanism: every place in ops-qa that lists "things needing attention" — the Timeline's connector strip, the roster's AttentionStrip, and (new) a QA-side surface — calls the same deriveConnectorDispatchInfo-shaped classifier and the same Link-to-detail affordance, so an operator never learns two different definitions of "needs attention" depending which page they landed on. A finding or incident on either side of the QA/ingestion boundary carries a typed pointer to its counterpart when one exists — a QA finding whose source_butler's recent session touched a degraded connector shows "possibly caused by: telegram/acct-1 (offline since 14:02)", and a connector's incident list surfaces "QA is investigating: case #4821" when a matching healing attempt exists — closing the loop from signal to responsible mechanism to proof of repair without a manual cross-reference. Every triage-shaped list in the group, connectors roster included, gets the fleet's j/k roving cursor and footer hint strip, so the busiest ops page is not the one exception to the app's own keyboard convention.

findings.title: Two divergent 'needs attention' classifiers for connectors, disagreeing across sibling pages

findings.detail: A connector with an auth issue (needs_reauth) that hasn't yet degraded state/liveness will show as attention-worthy on the roster and detail page but be invisible on the Timeline's strip; conversely the Timeline's cruder `liveness === 'offline'` check can flag a connector the roster's richer classifier would not yet call urgent. connector-auth.ts's docstring explicitly promises 'consistent auth label/color treatment across all three surfaces' (connector-auth.ts:17-20) — the Timeline strip is a fourth surface that was never brought under that guarantee.

findings.title: QA (butler-level self-healing) and ingestion/connectors (pipeline delivery) share zero cross-links in either direction
findings.evidence: QaFindingRecord (frontend/src/api/types.ts:5719-5737) carries only source_butler/source_type/fingerprint; ConnectorIncidentSummary (frontend/src/api/types.ts:4907-4914) carries only connector-scoped fields. No component under frontend/src/pages/Qa*.tsx or frontend/src/components/qa/ references a connector_type/endpoint_identity, and no ingestion component references a QA case/investigation id.
findings.detail: These are legitimately different failure classes (code exceptions vs. pipeline delivery), but an operator's actual question — 'is the butler erroring because a connector under it is down, or is this unrelated' — has no evidence door anywhere in the group. A QA case whose source_butler recently logged against a connector that was simultaneously offline/needs_reauth is exactly the kind of correlated evidence the north star's 'unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine' calls for, and today it doesn't exist even as a hint, let alone a door.

audits.jarvis_gap:
Today the four governance pages individually look consequence-honest — real enforcement in public.permissions (src/butlers/core/permissions.py:121-165), real ledger-priced spend figures with degraded-source honesty (SettingsConsolePage.tsx:86-92, SecretsPage.tsx:143-164), a real cascade-delete confirm dialog on the model catalog (SettingsModelsPage.tsx:367-413) — but the surface presents a single cross-page 'Audit reel' (SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:417-473, GET /audit-log?kind=privileged) as the fleet's unified privileged-action ledger, and that ledger silently drops two of the domains this very surface group governs. The SQL allowlist that defines 'privileged' (src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:86-97) enumerates model.%, permission.%, data.%, webhook.%, and credential actions — but never spend.%, so every spend.ceiling and spend.rule write (src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:1969-2193), i.e. every change to how much money the fleet may autonomously spend, never appears in the one place an owner would check for privileged changes, and SpendPage itself renders no history of its own. Separately, model-catalog create and delete (src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:672-710, 793-808) simply never call the audit.append primitive that three sibling endpoints in the same file (update, priority, verify-all) already use — so the most destructive write on the page, a cascade-delete that removes butler model overrides, leaves no trace anywhere, and its confirm dialog only offers generic prose ('cascade-delete any butler override entries') rather than the actual count, because the delete handler doesn't even query it before deleting. The ideal is not far off: enforcement, degraded-source honesty, and consequence dialogs are already the house style here — the gap is that the audit spine this surface advertises as unified has two silent holes precisely where the stakes are highest.</jarvis_gap>
<parameter name="ideal">A owner who lands on any of these four pages can answer 'what may the fleet do, and who changed that' within the same five seconds the north star demands: every write that changes fleet authority — a model added or removed from the catalog, a permission flipped, a spend ceiling or rule changed, a credential rotated — appears in one ledger with no allowlist blind spots, because the allowlist is derived from 'this call site wrote to a governance table' rather than a hand-maintained LIKE pattern that has to be remembered per domain. Every consequential confirm dialog states the actual blast radius it can compute (N butler overrides will be removed, not 'may cascade-delete'), because the backend already holds that count a query away. The Settings Console's panel grid, the Permissions audit reel, and the Spend/Secrets pages read as one governance surface with one vocabulary for 'privileged', not four independently-audited pages that happen to share a design system.

findings.title: Model catalog delete is the surface's most destructive write and is never audited
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:793-808 (delete_catalog_entry — no audit.append call, unlike update_catalog_entry at :778 and update_model_priority at :849 in the same file); src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:86-97 (_PRIVILEGED_CONSEQUENCE_SQL already matches `action LIKE 'model.%'`, so a `model.delete` entry would surface in the Permissions-page audit reel if it existed)
findings.detail: Deleting a catalog entry cascade-deletes every butler_model_override referencing it (comment at model_settings.py:798) — a fleet-wide routing-authority change — yet the handler performs the DELETE and returns without ever calling audit.append, unlike its siblings in the same file. The Permissions page's audit reel (SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:417-473) is presented as the privileged-action spine for this whole surface group and its backend allowlist already anticipates model.* events, but this specific consequential write leaves zero trace: no actor, no timestamp, no note of which overrides were cascaded away.

findings.title: Spend authority changes (ceiling, rules) are excluded from the privileged audit reel by allowlist, and SpendPage shows no local history either

ranked_moves.title: Forward obligation ledger with a cancellation door on every commitment
ranked_moves.why: The finance manifesto promises no un-warned renewal, but price changes are detected only after the charge posts, and no cancellation URL, notice period, or cancel-by date exists anywhere in schema — the warning arrives without the door.
ranked_moves.outcome: Subscriptions gain cancellation_url/notice_period_days/cancel_by; a forward obligation ledger registers known future charges with warn-by dates derived from notice periods; every renewal insight carries the cancellation door and the days-remaining-to-act, not just the amount.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No autonomous cancellation (owner-gated); no spend envelopes (dropped, owner decision pending).
ranked_moves.governing_intent: roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md renewal promise; vision.md: every consequential clause is a door
ranked_moves.surface_map: finance migrations, alerts.py detection -> ledger writer, insight payload shape, dashboard subscriptions panel; feeds move 3's expected_signals for renewal cadence.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: happy: known renewal warns at cancel_by - notice; missing metadata: obligation registered with unknown-door flag prompting owner enrichment; price change: pre-charge warning when next_amount known; idempotence: one obligation row per (subscription, period).
ranked_moves.verification: test: subscription with notice period warns before cancel-by, insight payload contains door fields; missing-url case renders enrichment prompt not silent omission.
ranked_moves.slice_plan: S1 schema + door fields; S2 obligation ledger + warn-by derivation; S3 insight payload + panel.

ranked_moves.title: Owner-scoped, room-resolved presence with arrival lead time
ranked_moves.why: at_home is asserted fleet-wide by ANY person entity (housemate, guest phone) on writer-clock freshness; away/commuting are declared context signals with zero producers while OwnTracks data sits unread. Every presence-conditioned behavior in the fleet is built on a signal that doesn't mean what its name says.
ranked_moves.outcome: Slice 1 (honesty): at_home derives only from owner-linked entities and HA's own last_updated clock; then in_space room-level occupancy from HA areas, and OwnTracks-derived commuting state with ETA so butlers get genuine arrival lead time for pre-conditioning.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No automation triggers in this move (consumers are moves 2/12 territory); no non-owner household presence modeling yet.
ranked_moves.governing_intent: vision.md: staleness never wears current-data authority; home manifesto presence promises
ranked_moves.surface_map: context_producers.py, context bus signal registry, HA entity->owner mapping config, OwnTracks connector read path, consumers of at_home across roster.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: happy: owner phone home -> at_home true with HA clock; housemate-only home -> at_home false; HA stale -> presence unmeasurable (joins move 3 semantics); commuting: OwnTracks transition emits ETA; failure: missing owner mapping -> explicit unconfigured state, not everyone-counts fallback.
ranked_moves.doc_impact: context bus doc; home module doc
ranked_moves.verification: test: non-owner entity fresh + owner absent -> not at_home; stale HA clock -> unmeasurable; OwnTracks fixture produces commuting+ETA signal.
ranked_moves.slice_plan: S1 owner scoping + HA clock (defect); S2 in_space occupancy; S3 OwnTracks commuting/ETA producer.

ranked_moves.title: home.observations perception ledger + ha_source_health freshness guard
ranked_moves.why: The house has no memory of itself — one upserted row per entity, captured_at stamped now() regardless of HA contact, poll failures swallowed — while the connector already writes every state change durably to connectors.home_assistant_history, which home has SELECT on and never reads. An HA outage reads as a healthy house.
ranked_moves.evidence: roster/home/modules/__init__.py:2069-2086 (:1322 swallow); src/butlers/jobs/home.py:168-210 (readers, no staleness check); alembic/versions/core/core_084_home_assistant_history.py:7-19
ranked_moves.outcome: ha_source_health row tracks last successful HA contact and poll error state; all snapshot readers join it and render unmeasurable on outage (slice 1, trust fix); home.observations builds durable, queryable house history views over the existing history table (occupancy patterns, door/window timelines, anomaly baselines).
ranked_moves.non_goals: No new polling infrastructure (history table already exists); no ML anomaly detection.
ranked_moves.governing_intent: vision.md: failure never impersonates health; home manifesto perception pillar
ranked_moves.surface_map: home module poll loop, new ha_source_health row/table, jobs/home.py readers, views over connectors.home_assistant_history, digest generation.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: happy: healthy poll updates source health + snapshot; outage: poll error recorded, readers return unmeasurable with last-good timestamp; recovery: health flips back, gap visible in history; idempotence: keyed health row upsert.
ranked_moves.doc_impact: home module doc; connector doc cross-reference
ranked_moves.verification: test: simulated HA outage -> readers return unmeasurable, digest marks the gap; history view returns real state transitions.
ranked_moves.slice_plan: S1 ha_source_health + reader guard (defect); S2 history views; S3 digest integration; S4 anomaly baselines.

ranked_moves.title: Viewport & modality contract + client-link honesty + phone entry routes
ranked_moves.why: The dashboard's highest-stakes entries (approval decisions, secrets re-auth) are minted as deep links into Telegram and opened on a phone — yet the binding design spec has zero viewport/touch content, the code has zero coarse-pointer/safe-area/dvh occurrences, CI runs desktop-only, and a dropped LTE link is announced as 'Fleet event stream offline'.
ranked_moves.evidence: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md (zero viewport content); frontend/src/components/layout/LiveIndicator.tsx:45,66; RootLayout.tsx:22-26; src/butlers/modules/approvals/notifications.py:92-97 (phone-entry links); playwright.config.ts (one desktop project)
ranked_moves.outcome: Dispatch spec amended with three device bands, 44px coarse-pointer floor, no-hover-only-facts rule; Page archetype owns the gutter ramp with dvh + safe-area; useClientLink() three-state (online/offline/reconnecting) so client loss renders as client loss, with cached-data age stamps; phone-entry route registry with declared landing shape, walked at 375px by a phone Playwright project in CI.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No PWA/offline shell, no gesture/Revealable lane, no ESLint viewport guard (all follow the contract, dropped this run).
ranked_moves.governing_intent: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md (amendment target); docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md; vision.md: failure never impersonates health (client-link honesty)
ranked_moves.surface_map: design spec, Page/layout primitives, LiveIndicator + RootLayout + query-client, new useClientLink hook, approvals/secrets phone-entry routes, playwright config.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: happy: desktop unchanged; phone: gutters/dvh/safe-area correct on entry routes; offline: banner states client link down + data age, no fleet-outage claim; reconnect: silent recovery; CI: 375px walk fails on horizontal scroll or clipped primary action.
ranked_moves.doc_impact: spec amendment (the deliverable); frontend docs note
ranked_moves.verification: phone Playwright project asserting entry-route landing shapes; component test: navigator.onLine false -> client-link banner, not fleet banner.
ranked_moves.slice_plan: S1 spec amendment; S2 useClientLink + LiveIndicator fix (defect); S3 Page gutter ramp + dvh/safe-area; S4 entry-route registry + phone CI project.

ranked_moves.title: Owner device bridge + watched-source channel registry
ranked_moves.why: Channel identity is a closed-world Literal with an hour-offset idempotency hack capping the fleet at 12 channels; Discord messages are ingested but invisible to Dunbar scoring; 'sms' is a validated NotifyChannel with no adapter — the owner's actual phone (calls, SMS) is outside the fleet's perception entirely.
ranked_moves.evidence: roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:803-828 (hour-offset + Discord gap); src/butlers/core/contracts.py:62 (closed Literal); src/butlers/daemon.py:901 (sms validated, no adapter)
ranked_moves.outcome: DB-backed source-channel registry replaces the Literal closed world and the hour-offset hack; Discord joins Dunbar scoring; a Watched Source connector pattern generalizes ingestion; the owner-device bridge path (telephony calls/SMS as perceived channels + sms notify adapter) is opened with its first adapter.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No clinical/FHIR, web-action, or shipment connectors (dropped); no autonomous outbound SMS without approval gating.
ranked_moves.governing_intent: connector-base spec; relationship manifesto (Dunbar completeness); adding-connectors-and-modules skill
ranked_moves.surface_map: contracts.py channel model, new registry table + migration, relationship_jobs idempotency keying, Discord->Dunbar join, notify adapter registry, new connector scaffold.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: happy: existing channels migrate to registry rows unchanged; new channel: registered without code change to contracts; idempotence: registry-keyed dedup replaces hour offsets; Discord: contact events feed Dunbar identically to Telegram; sms notify: adapter present or channel refuses at registration, never validated-but-dead.
ranked_moves.doc_impact: connector-base spec update (stale catalog refresh rides along); identity-model note
ranked_moves.verification: test: 13th channel registers without collision; Discord fixture moves a Dunbar score; sms notify without adapter is refused at config load.
ranked_moves.slice_plan: S1 registry + idempotency migration; S2 Discord into Dunbar (defect); S3 sms adapter or validation removal; S4 watched-source scaffold.

ranked_moves.title: One improvement-proposal spine + propose_amendment
ranked_moves.why: The fleet built the evidence->proposal->owner-decision lifecycle twice (switchboard rule promotion 'pending_review' vs autonomy suggestions 'pending') with divergent vocabularies, and neither can target prompts, skills, schedules, or tiers; the spec-declared AGENTS.md self-note channel has no callers — and a runtime write there would violate repo rule 5, so the only honest channel is a gated PR.
ranked_moves.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_suggestions.py:79-261; switchboard rule promotion pipeline; src/butlers/core/skills.py:267-287 (writers with no callers)
ranked_moves.outcome: public.improvement_proposals: target-agnostic (rule, autonomy grant, prompt, skill, schedule, tier) with one status vocabulary and provenance to friction evidence (move 9); both existing pipelines ported; propose_amendment renders identity-file changes as PRs through the QA healing machinery — a runtime never writes a git-tracked identity file directly.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No auto-adoption (owner decides); no retrospective scheduling or adoption-verification loop (dropped, follow-on).
ranked_moves.governing_intent: vision.md self-improvement with owner sovereignty; repo rule: runtime never writes git-tracked identity files
ranked_moves.surface_map: new public table + grants, autonomy_suggestions port, switchboard promotion port, QA healing PR machinery, proposal review surface on dashboard.
ranked_moves.behavior_matrix: happy: butler files typed proposal with evidence refs; review: owner accepts/rejects with one vocabulary; adoption: config targets apply transactionally, identity targets open a PR; idempotence: duplicate proposal keyed on (target, content hash) upserts; rollback: adopted config proposals record prior value.
ranked_moves.doc_impact: RFC for the proposal spine; autonomy + switchboard doc updates
ranked_moves.verification: test: both legacy pipelines produce spine rows with mapped statuses; identity-target adoption produces a PR branch, never a working-tree write.
ranked_moves.slice_plan: S1 table + spine; S2 port autonomy suggestions; S3 port rule promotion; S4 propose_amendment PR path; S5 review surface.
